cases.exclusivity: Correctly pricing the variance-risk premium AND surviving the tail via sizing/hedging — those who ran it naked blew up, so the durable 'edge' was really the capacity to bear a risk most couldn't stomach.
cases.evidence: BIS Quarterly Review (March 2018), "The role of exchange-traded volatility products"; CFTC/SEC complaint against LJM Partners (2019); Credit Suisse's termination of XIV (Feb 2018).

cases.name: Leveraged & inverse ETF/ETN end-of-day rebalance flow
cases.what: Exploit the mandatory, same-direction hedge that daily-reset leveraged/inverse ETPs must execute near the close: on an up day a 3x long fund must BUY more exposure and inverse funds must also buy to cover — a predictable end-of-day imbalance/momentum. The extreme case: on Feb 5, 2018 the VIX ETPs (XIV, SVXY) had to buy the equivalent of 100,000-200,000 VIX futures (~$800M) at the 4:15pm settlement; being long VIX futures into that close captured the reflexive spike.
cases.who: Systematic and volatility traders and dealers who anticipate the 'rebalance imbalance'; the mechanics were documented by Minder Cheng & Ananth Madhavan and by the BIS. ETPs involved: ProShares/Direxion (equity 3x) and XIV/SVXY (inverse VIX).
cases.instrument: Index/sector 3x ETFs and their underlying futures; VIX futures — deeply liquid, though the rebalance clusters into a thin window.
cases.why_it_worked: The rebalance is mechanical and its SIZE is computable from the day's return and the funds' known AUM and leverage, executed in a narrow end-of-day window regardless of price — a forced, price-insensitive flow. It repeats daily and scales with the leveraged-ETF complex (now tens of billions). The marginal price-setter is the funds' delta-one hedgers.
cases.lead: Intraday — the required end-of-day rebalance size is calculable from the day's move well before the close.
cases.exclusivity: Modeling each product's AUM, leverage factor and reset rules to estimate the AGGREGATE end-of-day imbalance across the complex, then executing ahead of it — a data-plumbing and estimation moat, not public knowledge.
cases.evidence: Cheng & Madhavan, "The Dynamics of Leveraged and Inverse ETFs" (2009); BIS Quarterly Review (March 2018) on exchange-traded volatility products and the Feb 5, 2018 close.

cases.name: Dealer gamma / GEX positioning; marquee: GameStop, Jan 2021
cases.what: Reconstruct options market-makers' aggregate gamma exposure (GEX) from open interest to predict whether dealer delta-hedging will DAMPEN moves (dealers long gamma → sell rallies, buy dips) or AMPLIFY them (short gamma → chase). The extreme exploitation: deliberately force a gamma squeeze by concentrated call buying so dealers short those calls must buy stock as it rises, compounded by a short squeeze.
cases.who: SqueezeMetrics coined and published 'Gamma Exposure (GEX)' in a March 2016 white paper; SpotGamma (2020) commercialized dealer-positioning levels. Marquee profitable operation: Keith Gill ('Roaring Kitty'/DeepF***ingValue) turned a ~$53,000 stake into hundreds of millions on GameStop, and the Reddit crowd's call buying forced dealer hedging plus short covering, driving GME up >1,500% in January 2021.
cases.instrument: Single-name equities and index options (SPX/SPY); GameStop (GME) and its options specifically.
cases.why_it_worked: Dealer hedging is a mechanical, positioning-determined flow. When dealers are short gamma near heavily-traded strikes, their hedging is self-reinforcing. GameStop layered a >100%-of-float short interest onto concentrated call buying, so forced dealer buying and short covering created a reflexive spiral in a liquid, option-rich name. Positioning imbalances recur, so GEX-conditioned strategies fire repeatedly.
cases.lead: The GEX/positioning read is available before the move it predicts — option open interest telegraphs where hedging pressure will build.
cases.exclusivity: Inferring dealer positioning from options open interest requires assumptions about who is long/short each strike — the processing SqueezeMetrics/SpotGamma built; and, for GameStop, recognizing the rare >100%-float-short + gamma setup before the crowd priced it.
cases.evidence: SqueezeMetrics GEX white paper (2016); a Cboe-hosted study relating dealer gamma to volatility; GameStop January 2021 documented in Keith Gill's Congressional testimony and the SEC staff report (Oct 2021).

cases.name: Front-running a forced ETF/index roll; marquee: USO and negative WTI, April 2020
cases.what: Anticipate (and, per regulators, allegedly accelerate) the forced selling of the expiring May 2020 WTI contract by large passive longs — the United States Oil Fund (USO) and other index/ETP holders that had to roll out before expiry into a storage-constrained, illiquid market — and be short into the settlement, profiting as the front contract collapsed to -$37.63/bbl.
cases.who: Nine independent traders affiliated with prop shop Vega Capital London (centered on former pit trader Paul Commins, trading from homes in Essex) made roughly $660M in a few hours on April 20, 2020; scrutinized by the CFTC and FCA, though no illegality has been proven. The forced seller was USO.
cases.instrument: WTI crude-oil futures (May 2020, CL) — a large, liquid contract, momentarily one-sided.
cases.why_it_worked: USO's roll schedule and size were public and mechanical, and with Cushing storage effectively full no buyer could take delivery — so the forced, price-insensitive selling had nowhere to go and being short the front month into the roll/settlement was hugely asymmetric. The marginal seller (a passive fund tracking front-month WTI) was maximally unsophisticated about delivery microstructure; the Trade-at-Settlement window concentrated the flow.
cases.lead: Days — USO publicly telegraphed its roll timing and had already begun shifting out of the front month before expiry.
cases.exclusivity: Knowing exactly when and how much USO and peers had to sell, understanding the Cushing storage/deliverability constraint and the TAS mechanics, and having the nerve and capital to press a sub-zero outcome the market thought impossible.
cases.evidence: Bloomberg / CTRM Center reporting and the Bayes Business School case "How Nine Traders Hit a Gusher with Negative Oil"; the CFTC/FCA investigation of Vega Capital London; the May 2020 WTI -$37.63 settlement on April 20, 2020.

cases.name: Commitments of Traders (COT) positioning
cases.what: Use the CFTC's weekly Commitments of Traders report to read positioning extremes — chiefly commercial hedgers' net position ('smart money') versus over-extended speculators — then fade crowded speculative extremes and lean with commercials across commodity and FX futures.
cases.who: Stephen Briese, the recognized COT authority (Bullish Review newsletter since 1988; author of "The Commitments of Traders Bible," Wiley 2008); many CTAs incorporate COT signals.
cases.instrument: Commodity, FX and rate futures — large, liquid markets across dozens of contracts.
cases.why_it_worked: The COT reveals who is positioned how: commercial hedgers are informed about the underlying cash business, while over-extended speculators are the sentiment-driven marginal price-setters whose crowded bets tend to mean-revert. Briese's backtest across 35-38 futures markets (2000-2007) generated ~3,502 trades and ~$1.7M total profit. It fires weekly across many markets, giving breadth and repeatability.
cases.lead: A processing/interpretation lead rather than a speed lead — COT is public but released with a ~3-day lag; the edge is normalizing and thresholding positioning correctly, which most readers get wrong or ignore.
cases.exclusivity: Briese's normalization methodology (the COT Index across 63 commodities) and the interpretive framework built over decades — the processing, not the raw report; the moat lies in reading it correctly at scale.
cases.evidence: Stephen Briese, "The Commitments of Traders Bible: How to Profit from Insider Market Intelligence" (Wiley, 2008); CSI Data's Briese COT Index; peer-reviewed COT-signal reversal studies.

cases.name: Bill Benter's Hong Kong horse-racing model
cases.what: Built a computerized multinomial (conditional) logit prediction model for Hong Kong Jockey Club races and bet it into the parimutuel (tote) pools. Over his career the operation won an estimated ~US$1 billion; a single 2001 triple-trio ticket paid about HK$100M.
cases.who: William 'Bill' Benter (blackjack-team alumnus), initially partnered with Australian gambler Alan Woods, operating in Hong Kong from 1984.
cases.instrument: Parimutuel win/place/exotic pools at the Hong Kong Jockey Club, one of the deepest betting markets on earth (billions of HK$ wagered per season) — high capacity that absorbs large stakes without a fixed bookmaker to bar the bettor.
cases.why_it_worked: The raw inputs (past-performance 'form' data plus live tote odds) were public, but the edge was years of proprietary work: a ~120-variable conditional-logit model whose key innovation was blending the MODEL's win-probability estimate WITH the public's odds, capturing information in both. The marginal price-setter was the unsophisticated betting public whose favorite-longshot bias persisted race after race, and the signal fired thousands of times per season — extreme repeatability and capacity.
cases.lead: Not a newswire race but a model-quality/information lead over the crowd's consensus odds, recomputed live in the seconds before each off. The crowd's price was systematically mis-calibrated; his model wasn't.
cases.exclusivity: Pure processing moat: a private, painstakingly tuned statistical model on public data. It LOST money 1984-1987 before calibration turned it profitable — the multi-year tuning is what could not be copied, not the data.
cases.evidence: Bloomberg Businessweek, Kit Chellel, 'The Gambler Who Cracked the Horse-Racing Code' (May 3, 2018); Benter's own paper 'Computer Based Horse Race Handicapping and Wagering Systems' (1994). Guinness World Records lists him among the most profitable gamblers.

cases.name: RS Metrics satellite car-counting
cases.what: First firm to systematically count cars in retailers' parking lots from satellite imagery and sell the derived foot-traffic signal (TrafficSignals) to hedge funds ahead of quarterly comparable-store-sales and earnings prints.
cases.who: RS Metrics (Remote Sensing Metrics LLC), founded ~2010 by Tom Diamond and Alex Diamond; later joined by peers like Orbital Insight and RS's UBS-study collaborators.
cases.instrument: Large-cap US retailers and their listed options — Walmart, Target, Costco, Home Depot, Whole Foods, Best Buy, JCPenney — all deeply liquid, so signal-driven positions clear transaction costs.
cases.why_it_worked: The imagery existed but nobody was buying and computer-vision-processing it at scale; RS Metrics had to license satellite imagery and build a car-detection pipeline across ~65,000 store locations. A UC Berkeley Haas study ('Stock Picks From Space') documented that traders using such counts earned roughly 4-5% abnormal returns around earnings, largely at the expense of retail investors taking the other side — an unsophisticated, persistent counterparty.
cases.lead: Car counts accumulate through the whole quarter — a read on sales weeks before the company reports comps/earnings.
cases.exclusivity: First-mover processing moat (2010-2011): buy the imagery + build and operate the CV counting system nobody else was running across tens of thousands of lots.
cases.evidence: CNBC 'Spying For Profits: The Satellite Image Indicator' (Aug 2010); UC Berkeley Haas 'Stock Picks From Space' (Katona, Painter, Patatoukas, Zdanowicz) and Haas Newsroom write-up; RS Metrics TrafficSignals product materials.

cases.name: Genscape power-plant sensor network
cases.what: Deployed a proprietary field network of electromagnetic-field/monitoring sensors near transmission lines (and later infrared cameras) to measure real-time electricity generation, then sold the live output to power and energy traders before any official grid data existed.
cases.who: Genscape, founded 1999/2000 in Louisville by Sterling Lapinski and Sean O'Leary, both former power traders frustrated by market opacity; acquired by Verisk for $364M in 2018.
cases.instrument: Wholesale electricity and natural-gas markets, later crude/products via Cushing (Oklahoma) storage and pipeline monitoring — large, liquid energy futures and OTC markets.
cases.why_it_worked: They physically installed and maintained hardware at plant and substation perimeters — real capex and field engineering no competitor had — turning a plant's magnetic signature and heat into a live megawatt estimate. Officials reported the same generation/flow data only with a lag. FERC becoming a customer legitimized the (initially 'feels like spying') data.
cases.lead: Real-time (minutes to hours) reads on generation and, for oil, tank/pipeline activity — versus official releases that lagged by days.
cases.exclusivity: A physical, plant-by-plant sensor network plus infrared interpretation — arguably the hardest-to-replicate data moat of the set, requiring hardware deployment rather than just software.
cases.evidence: Energy Risk 'Pioneers: power — Genscape'; StateImpact/NPR 'Oil Espionage: Traders Spy on Oklahoma Hub With Satellites, Sensors and Infrared Cameras' (2012); Verisk's $364M acquisition (2018).

cases.name: Orbital Insight oil-tank shadow inventory
cases.what: Measured the crescent-shaped shadows cast by floating-roof lids inside crude-storage tanks in satellite imagery, converting shadow geometry to roof height to oil volume, and packaged it as a World Oil Storage Index sold to funds.
cases.who: Orbital Insight, founded 2013 by James Crawford (ex-Google Books, ex-NASA); parallel players Ursa Space Systems (radar/SAR) and Kayrros. Index distributed on Bloomberg terminals.
cases.instrument: Crude oil futures (WTI/Brent), the USO ETF, and energy equities — deep, liquid markets where an inventory surprise moves price enough to clear costs.
cases.why_it_worked: Had to source fresh commercial imagery and build computer vision that reads shadow -> height -> barrels across ~20,000+ tanks worldwide, including in opaque economies (China, Iran) that publish no inventory data at all. During the 2020 storage glut this gave a multi-week lead on builds/draws.
cases.lead: Weeks ahead of EIA/IEA official inventory reports, plus coverage of countries where there is no official number to wait for.
cases.exclusivity: Buying imagery + a proprietary shadow-to-volume CV pipeline that nobody else was parsing at global scale — a processing/data moat.
cases.evidence: HBS Digital Initiative case 'This Startup Makes Money from Oil Tank Shadows'; Orbital Insight 'Bringing Transparency to Oil Supply in Closed Economies'; Bloomberg terminal World Oil Storage Index.

cases.name: Descartes Labs satellite crop-yield forecasts
cases.what: Applied deep learning to multi-source satellite imagery to forecast US corn and soybean yields more accurately and earlier than the USDA — reportedly within ~1% of realized production.
cases.who: Descartes Labs, spun out of Los Alamos National Laboratory in 2014 (founders including Mark Johnson and Steven Brumby); used Planet, Landsat and MODIS imagery. Cargill was a strategic investor.
cases.instrument: CBOT corn and soybean futures and options — large, liquid agricultural commodity markets the whole grain trade prices off the USDA number.
cases.why_it_worked: Processed roughly a petabyte of imagery across ~30,000 processors to estimate national yield ahead of the USDA's flagship August WASDE, the consensus figure the market trades around. Beating that number is a genuine compute/CV moat built by ex-national-lab scientists — not something a generalist desk could stand up.
cases.lead: Forecasts released days before the USDA's monthly crop reports (e.g., its 2016 corn estimate on Aug 9 vs the USDA on Aug 12).
cases.exclusivity: Petabyte-scale imagery ingestion plus a custom ML yield model — hard to replicate in both data volume and modeling talent.
cases.evidence: Descartes Labs 'Advancing the science of corn forecasting' (2016); Planet Stories 'Using Satellite Imagery & Deep Learning to Predict a $67B Corn Market'; AgFunderNews on Cargill's Series B investment.

cases.name: SpaceKnow China Satellite Manufacturing Index
cases.what: Analyzed satellite imagery of 6,000+ Chinese industrial sites with machine learning to build an independent index of Chinese manufacturing activity, published on Bloomberg — the first alternative-data index to appear on the terminal.
cases.who: SpaceKnow, founded ~2013 by Pavel Machalek and Jerry Javornicky; China Satellite Manufacturing Index (SMI) launched on Bloomberg terminals in 2016.
cases.instrument: China-exposed macro instruments — offshore yuan (CNH), Chinese equity ETFs (e.g., FXI), and industrial commodities (copper, iron ore) — liquid enough for macro sizing.
cases.why_it_worked: Official Chinese PMI/GDP data is widely distrusted and smoothed, so an independent, imagery-derived read on 6,000 sites has no clean substitute. The CV pipeline over thousands of industrial areas is a real processing moat; the index flagged the October 2018 contraction that Bloomberg reported.
cases.lead: Published Monday/Wednesday/Friday, ahead of and independent of official Chinese statistics — and not subject to their manipulation.
cases.exclusivity: Proprietary ML over thousands of industrial sites; because the official numbers are distrusted, there is no cheaper alternative to bootstrap from.
cases.evidence: Bloomberg 'Satellites Show China Manufacturing Output Contracted in October' (Oct 31, 2018); Quartz coverage of the China SMI; SpaceWatch.Global / Eagle Alpha writeups of the first alt-data index on Bloomberg.

cases.name: Corporate-jet (ADS-B) M&A tracking
cases.what: Tracked private-jet tail numbers via ADS-B transponder data to detect executives converging for undisclosed merger or financing negotiations, positioning in the target/acquirer before the announcement.
cases.who: Quandl 'Corporate Aviation Intelligence' dataset (26,000 jets tied to 1,300 public companies, ~70% of the S&P 500); Gordon Haskett Research's Don Bilson used jet-tracking in the April 2019 Occidental/Berkshire/Anadarko call; academic corroboration from Oxford's Matthew Smith et al.
cases.instrument: Large-cap target and acquirer equities and options (e.g., Occidental, Anadarko) — liquid names where deal targets routinely jump 20-40% on announcement.
cases.why_it_worked: Raw ADS-B is public, but resolving anonymized/blocked tail numbers to specific corporate owners and cross-referencing flight convergence is the processing moat — Quandl fused five sources, several licensed exclusively. A Gulfstream V owned by Occidental spotted at Omaha preceded Buffett's $10B Occidental commitment by two days.
cases.lead: Days ahead of the public deal/financing announcement.
cases.exclusivity: Tail-number-to-owner resolution plus multi-source flight fusion (with exclusively-licensed feeds) — a defensible processing moat over freely-available ADS-B.
cases.evidence: Bloomberg 'Hedge Funds Are Tracking Private Jets to Find the Next Megadeal' (2019); CNBC 'A corporate jet suggested Buffett's energy deal was in works days before it was announced' (Apr 30, 2019); WatersTechnology 'Quandl Launches Corporate Jet Dataset for Predicting M&A Activity.'

cases.name: Congressional-trade replication
cases.what: Mirror the disclosed stock transactions of US members of Congress, who historically earned significant abnormal returns; now packaged as replication ETFs and copy-trading apps.
cases.who: Academic foundation: Ziobrowski, Cheng, Boyd & Ziobrowski (JFQA 2004, Senate; Business & Politics 2011, House). Modern replication: Unusual Whales / Subversive NANC (Democratic) and KRUZ (Republican) ETFs, launched Feb 2023, and the Autopilot app.
cases.instrument: US large-cap equities — the replication funds are dominated by Microsoft, Nvidia, Apple and Amazon — i.e., maximally liquid names.
cases.why_it_worked: Ziobrowski found Senators' purchases beat the market by ~12%/yr (85 bps/month) and House members' by ~6%/yr, consistent with an informational advantage. The historical edge was aggregation: disclosures were buried and hard to compile, and the marginal retail investor ignored them. NANC has outpaced the S&P 500 by roughly 7 points since 2023.
cases.lead: STOCK Act filings appear up to ~45 days after the trade, yet still ahead of the broad market recognizing the position; the durable edge was the parsing/aggregation lead over an inattentive public.
cases.exclusivity: Weakest moat of the set — the data is public filings, so the edge is disclosure-parsing speed/aggregation plus a persistently inattentive retail counterparty. Included for its documented record, with the honest caveat that post-STOCK-Act studies (e.g., Belmont et al.) dispute persistence and the edge has decayed.
cases.evidence: Ziobrowski et al., 'Abnormal Returns from the Common Stock Investments of the U.S. Senate,' JFQA 2004; Morningstar and NPR (2024) coverage of NANC/KRUZ performance vs the S&P 500.

cases.name: Polymarket 'Théo' neighbor-poll election bet
cases.what: A French trader commissioned proprietary 'neighbor-effect' polls — asking respondents who their neighbors would vote for, to strip out shy-Trump social-desirability bias — judged public polls skewed to Harris, and bet ~$30M+ on Trump across Polymarket, netting an estimated ~$85M.
cases.who: 'Théo,' identified by the Wall Street Journal as a former French banker/trader; blockchain firm Chainalysis tied ~11 accounts to him and estimated the ~$85M haul.
cases.instrument: Polymarket 2024 US election contracts (presidency, popular vote, blue-wall sweep) — the deepest prediction market ever, roughly $3.6B in volume, giving real capacity for eight-figure stakes.
cases.why_it_worked: The exotic input was privately-commissioned neighbor-effect polling, an academically grounded method that corrects a systematic public-poll bias most bettors weren't running. Combined with a contrarian thesis, it beat a consensus (public polls, and a market priced near a coin flip) that was wrong. The marginal price-setters were poll-following bettors.
cases.lead: His late-October proprietary poll results gave conviction to add size before the market repriced on election night.
cases.exclusivity: Self-funded proprietary polling with a specific bias-correction method — a genuine private-data moat versus bettors reading the same public poll averages.
cases.evidence: Wall Street Journal profile of 'Théo'; Bloomberg 'Trump Whale's Polymarket Haul Boosted to $85 Million' (Nov 7, 2024, citing Chainalysis); CBS 60 Minutes. Caveat: a single high-conviction event rather than a repeatable factory, included for the documented exotic-data edge.

cases.name: Enron weather-derivatives desk (Lynda Clemmons)
cases.what: Created the first standardized weather-derivatives trading desk, writing temperature (heating- and cooling-degree-day) contracts to hedge energy demand and trading the book against proprietary forecasts.
cases.who: Lynda Clemmons at Enron, who launched the desk in 1997 at age 27; it did ~350 transactions and turned its first profit in 1998, writing ~$1B in weather hedges within two years. The market later institutionalized (CME weather futures; ~$25B notional by 2023) with players like Nephila in adjacent catastrophe risk.
cases.instrument: OTC and (later) CME temperature/HDD-CDD weather derivatives tied to power and natural gas — the underlying power and gas markets are enormous and liquid.
cases.why_it_worked: Weather is the exotic input; the moat was proprietary long-range meteorological forecasting plus being the market-making franchise that could price contracts counterparties couldn't. Energy-meteorology desks translate sub-seasonal and seasonal forecasts into an edge over the market-implied/consensus temperature expectation, which drives gas heating and power-cooling demand.
cases.lead: A proprietary forecast lead over the market's consensus temperature outlook, from days to a full season ahead.
cases.exclusivity: Proprietary forecasting plus a first-mover market-making book — a real processing/franchise moat in a domain (meteorology) most trading desks had no capability in.
cases.evidence: Washington Post 'A Hot (and Cold) New Investment Opportunity' (Jul 4, 1998); HBS case 'Enron Corporation's Weather Derivatives'; Insurance Journal 'Worsening Weather Igniting $25 Billion Weather Derivatives Market' (2024).

patterns.name: Build-Moat on Commodity Raw Material
patterns.description: The largest cluster (RS Metrics, Orbital Insight, Descartes Labs, SpaceKnow, CargoMetrics, container-port CNN, YipitData, PriceStats, Revelio Labs) shares one DNA: the raw feed — satellite imagery, AIS pings, web pages, resumes — was cheap or outright public, and therefore worthless on its own. The entire edge lived in the expensive, unglamorous BUILD: a computer-vision pipeline over 65,000 parking lots, a scraper-plus-reconciliation engine that maps messy pages to a company's exact reported KPI definition, entity resolution over a billion profiles. A rival would have to redo years of engineering, not write a check. This is the sharpest winner/loser divide in the set: losers buy a finished number anyone else can also buy and the edge is already arbitraged; winners own the processing that converts raw exhaust into the number nobody else has computed. The signal fires every reporting cycle across many liquid names, so the build amortizes.
patterns.how_to_generate: Start from a raw, noisy, under-parsed data exhaust (imagery, sensor pings, web pages, documents, telemetry) that maps to something economically meaningful, then ask: 'What pipeline would I have to build to turn this into a clean, tradeable number, and would that build take a competitor years to copy?' If the honest answer is 'just license the finished dataset,' reject the idea — the moat must be in the WORK, not the data's existence.

patterns.name: The Metric That Finishes Before the Announcement
patterns.description: Car counts, worker-shift geolocation, foot traffic, card spend and e-receipts (RS Metrics, Thasos/Tesla, Foursquare/Chipotle, Second Measure/Blue Apron, Slice, Edison, Froot-Kang-Ozik-Sadka) all exploit a mechanical TIMING edge distinct from macro front-running: the quantity you measure IS a tight proxy for the exact number the company will report, and it accumulates continuously through the reporting window — so it is essentially complete weeks before the print while sell-side consensus and slow retail flow still price off stale data. Peer-reviewed work (JFQA, MIT/Sigmetrics, Berkeley Haas) confirmed prices did NOT embed the signal before disclosure and that the abnormal return came at retail's expense. Losers measure something loosely correlated and noisy; winners measure a direct, already-finished proxy for a scheduled binary catalyst.
patterns.how_to_generate: Take any company or asset with a scheduled disclosure (earnings, same-store comps, unit production, deliveries) and ask: 'Which observable real-world quantity accumulates in near-lockstep with that reported number across the reporting period, so it is fully formed before the announcement?' Prioritize proxies that ARE the KPI (dollars spent, units sold, visits) over ones merely correlated with it, and confirm the reporting crowd has no comparable panel.

patterns.name: Front-Run the Slow Official Statistic
patterns.description: EIA inventories, USDA WASDE, BLS non-farm payrolls, CPI, ICSG copper output and the official PMIs are scheduled, market-moving numbers produced by a slow surveyor. Genscape, Ursa Space, Kayrros, Earth-i, LinkUp, PriceStats and Descartes each produced an independent, higher-frequency estimate of the SAME quantity days-to-weeks ahead of the official print (LinkUp beat NFP consensus ~65% of the time; PriceStats runs daily vs a monthly CPI; Genscape published Cushing stocks during an EIA shutdown), then traded it into the deepest, most liquid macro instrument — crude, ag futures, rates, FX — where transaction costs clear trivially. The unsophisticated counterparty is the entire market still waiting for the lagging release.
patterns.how_to_generate: Enumerate scheduled government/industry statistics that visibly move a liquid futures or rates/FX market. For each, ask: 'Can I measure this exact quantity independently, at higher frequency, before the release?' The best targets pair a slow, laggy, market-anchoring official number with an enormous, cheap-to-trade instrument so even a modest lead pays.

patterns.name: Measure What Has No Trustworthy Official Number
patterns.description: SpaceKnow's China Satellite Manufacturing Index, Orbital Insight's China/Iran crude stocks, PriceStats exposing Argentina's understated inflation, and Kayrros' read on opaque floating storage worked partly for a special reason: the official series was manipulated, smoothed, delayed indefinitely, or simply did not exist. That has two consequences money can't buy — there is no cheaper substitute to bootstrap from, and there is no consensus number for your edge to converge on and decay against. Distrust or absence of the official figure is itself the durable opportunity: the market must price SOMETHING, and your independent read becomes the only credible input.
patterns.how_to_generate: Hunt for economically important quantities where the official measurement is absent, chronically delayed, politically manipulated, or covers an opaque geography (state-controlled economies, illicit/grey flows, hidden reserves). The more distrusted or missing the official number, the more durable and un-arbitraged an independent, from-scratch measurement becomes.

patterns.name: Own the Panel Nobody Can License
patterns.description: Foursquare's ~50M-user location panel, App Annie's Connect SDK telemetry, Edison's own mail client, Slice/Rakuten's receipt app and Envestnet|Yodlee's bank-aggregation layer produced first-party data that was structurally impossible for a rival to buy or scrape — because it flowed from an asset the firm OWNED outright (an app, an SDK, an inbox, a payment/aggregation chokepoint). Exclusivity here is not 'we processed it better,' it is 'this data physically cannot exist for anyone else.' The App Annie SEC case marks the boundary of the pattern: secretly using confidential SDK telemetry to sharpen estimates is exactly where an ownership moat crosses into securities fraud.
patterns.how_to_generate: Look for businesses sitting on proprietary first-party exhaust — an app userbase, an SDK, an email client, an aggregation layer, a payment rail — whose ordinary operation reveals behavior about OTHER (public) companies. Ask 'Who owns a chokepoint that sees this activity and could never sell the raw view?' Then pressure-test the legal line on how the owner is permitted to use and represent it.

patterns.name: The Physical or Exclusive-License Access Moat
patterns.description: Some moats cannot be coded. Genscape chartered aircraft with infrared cameras and bolted electromagnetic sensors to power-plant and refinery perimeters; Premise Data paid on-the-ground contributors in 120+ countries where web-price density is too thin to scrape; Majestic/M Science and Quandl locked datasets under EXCLUSIVE license. The barrier is capex, field operations, or a signed exclusivity that a software-only rival cannot leap with money-plus-code — and this class of moat kept producing even when official channels stopped (Genscape crude data during the EIA furlough). Corporate-jet M&A tracking is the hybrid: public ADS-B, but tail-number-to-owner resolution fused across five feeds, several exclusively licensed.
patterns.how_to_generate: Ask what signal would require boots on the ground, deployed hardware, or an exclusive contract to observe — deliberately choosing a barrier that capital-plus-code alone can't clear. Favor observation methods that keep working when the official or free channel stops, and consider fusing a public feed with an exclusively-licensed one to make the combination unreplicable.

patterns.name: Bet Against a Structurally Biased Crowd
patterns.description: Every parimutuel and sports case (Benter, Woods, Ranogajec, Bloom/Starlizard, Benham/Smartodds, Voulgaris, Walters/Computer Group) shares one counterparty: an unsophisticated crowd — or a margin-laden book fed by recreational money — whose bias is persistent and structural (favorite-longshot bias, home/popular-team shading). Benter formalized the winning move: build a fundamental probability model, then fold the crowd's OWN implied probability back in as a model variable, so the final estimate strictly dominates both your raw model and the consensus. It fires thousands of times per season with enormous capacity, and the edge is durable precisely because the bias is behavioral and recurs every event.
patterns.how_to_generate: Find a market cleared by sentiment-driven amateurs (or a dealer passing their bias through) with a documented, repeating mispricing. Build a fundamental probability estimate, then explicitly incorporate the crowd's price as an input so your output beats both. Prize high-frequency arenas where the identical bias recurs across thousands of events, giving repeatability and capacity.

patterns.name: Transfer a Proven Edge-Discipline Into a Softer Arena
patterns.description: Thorp (blackjack card-counting → warrants/convertibles at Princeton Newport), Yass/SIG (poker and racetrack pricing → options market making) and Hull (blackjack → options market making) all carried the SAME machinery — quantify a probabilistic edge, size by Kelly, manage variance, never be the least-informed player at the table — from a game they had already beaten into a financial market where the marginal counterparty was less sophisticated than they were. Thorp was pricing options before Black-Scholes was published. The generalizable insight: a rigorous framework that wins decisively in one venue is often simply un-applied one venue over.
patterns.how_to_generate: Take a probabilistic discipline proven in a niche (gambling, insurance, weather, forecasting tournaments, esports) and ask where the identical math applies against a demonstrably less-sophisticated counterparty — especially two-sided market-making or convergence trades where you can quote around a better fair-value estimate and harvest the spread against naive flow across millions of repetitions.

patterns.name: Front-Run Mechanical, Price-Insensitive Forced Flow
patterns.description: Index inclusions (Tesla Dec 2020), Russell reconstitution, the Goldman/GSCI roll, leveraged-and-inverse ETF end-of-day resets and USO's front-month roll all feature a counterparty that MUST trade a computable size at a publicly known time regardless of price, to control tracking error. Model the imbalance from published rules and get in front of it. This pattern also carries the set's loudest failure lessons about durability: the S&P additions premium decayed from ~7.4% (1990s) to a statistically insignificant ~0.8% as arbitrageurs crowded in, and Mou showed the Goldman-roll edge compresses as arb capital deploys. It survives only where the forced flow overwhelms the front-runners (Tesla's ~1.7% index weight) or a structural constraint makes it asymmetric (USO into a full Cushing with no buyer, driving WTI negative).
patterns.how_to_generate: List forced, calendar-driven, price-insensitive flows (index rebalances, ETF/ETN rolls and daily resets, rating- or mandate-driven flows). Compute the mechanical size and timing from public rules — then screen HARD for crowding and decay: take it only where the flow dwarfs likely arbitrage capital, a single name's weight is huge, or a physical constraint (no deliverability, capped storage) makes the payoff asymmetric.

patterns.name: Infer Positioning That Forces Future Flow
patterns.description: COT (over-extended speculators mean-revert while informed commercial hedgers sit on the other side), dealer gamma/GEX (short-gamma hedging is self-reinforcing), and the GameStop >100%-of-float short plus concentrated call buying all reward inferring WHO is long or short, so you can predict the flow their hedging or capitulation will be forced to produce. The processing moat is the inference itself: COT must be normalized correctly (Briese's COT Index across 63 commodities), and dealer positioning must be reconstructed from options open interest with the ownership assumptions SqueezeMetrics/SpotGamma built. The read is available before the move it predicts — open interest telegraphs where hedging pressure will build.
patterns.how_to_generate: Find a public dataset that reveals participants' POSITIONING (open interest, short interest, Commitments of Traders, fund holdings, ETF creation/redemption). Build the inference layer that converts raw positioning into 'who will be forced to buy or sell, and when,' correctly normalized — then act before that hedging or unwind hits the tape.

patterns.name: Get Paid by a Counterparty With No P&L Discipline
patterns.description: The most durable 'counterparties' in the set aren't traders. Cum-ex extracted multiple refunds from a tax authority whose reclaim system never reconciled withholding to a single claim; Ranogajec's Punters Club earned more from tote and casino REBATES on LOSING bets (~US$44M) than from picking winners (~US$8M), because its billions in turnover fattened operator commissions; index rollers pay the roll every month by mandate. These institutions disburse money mechanically for structure or volume, not because you were right. The edge is legal/operational engineering or sheer scale — with the explicit caveat that cum-ex's engineering eventually drew criminal prosecution, so legality must be settled before profitability.
patterns.how_to_generate: Look for institutions that pay out by RULE rather than by judgment — tax authorities, rebate/commission schemes, mechanical index payers, subsidy or incentive programs. Ask what structure or volume threshold unlocks a payment that does not depend on being right, then stress-test its legality and reconciliation loopholes before sizing it.

patterns.name: Out-Handicap a Binary Catalyst, Then Diversify the Tail
patterns.description: Paulson's merger-arbitrage desk (and COT-style mean-reversion) win by reading a discrete outcome's odds — deal completion under antitrust, financing, shareholder-vote and MAC-clause risk — better than the marginal holder, and by holding many independent bets so any single break is survivable. The spread IS the compensation for binary risk; the edge is superior odds-estimation (Paulson's seven-point completion checklist) plus portfolio construction that absorbs size. The failure mode is written into the same case: concentration killed returns when he over-sized breaking deals (Valeant, failed mergers) in 2015-2018.
patterns.how_to_generate: Find event-driven spreads (mergers, litigation, regulatory approvals, refinancings, drug approvals) where the market price compensates for a binary risk you can handicap better than average through genuine domain expertise. Require enough independent, diversified positions that no single adverse outcome is fatal — the diversification is as load-bearing as the handicapping.

patterns.name: A Bespoke Private Signal Aimed at One Big Catalyst
patterns.description: Theo's self-funded neighbor-effect election polling on Polymarket, corporate-jet ADS-B tracking that caught Occidental's Gulfstream at Omaha two days before Buffett's US$10B commitment, and Enron's proprietary long-range weather forecasting each created a PRIVATE input that corrected a SPECIFIC consensus error ahead of a SPECIFIC high-stakes event. Unlike always-on panels, these are commissioned or bespoke observations built for one catalyst where the public consensus rests on a known, correctable bias (public-poll bias, no visibility into private jets, market-implied temperature). The counterparty is everyone pricing off the same flawed public input.
patterns.how_to_generate: Pick a discrete, high-stakes, hard-to-forecast event (election, M&A, weather-driven commodity demand, regulatory decision) whose consensus rests on a biased or incomplete PUBLIC input. Commission or build a private observation that specifically corrects that bias — a targeted poll, a physical-movement tracker, a proprietary forecast — and size to the conviction it buys.

patterns.name: Machine-Read Recurring Text Faster and More Consistently
patterns.description: Prattle (later Liquidnet) replaced slow, inconsistent, human-biased interpretation of central-bank statements with an instant, identical quantitative score derived from a per-institution lexicon covering 15 central banks and ~3,000 companies. It beat the marginal human reader on BOTH speed and consistency at every scheduled meeting and print, into enormous rates/FX liquidity. The unsophisticated counterparty is a human parsing dense policy language slowly and idiosyncratically; the moat is the years-built, trained lexicon that cannot be reconstructed overnight. It fires on a known calendar, so the edge is repeatable and scalable.
patterns.how_to_generate: Find recurring, market-moving TEXT or speech that humans currently interpret slowly and inconsistently — central-bank statements, filings, earnings-call language, regulatory notices, court rulings. Build a domain-specific scoring model that reads it instantly and identically every time, and trade the gap before a slow, uneven human consensus forms around it.

ideas.name: Data-Center Waste-Heat Thermal Census
ideas.source: Reject-heat plumes and rooftop chiller/dry-cooler thermal signatures from hyperscale AI data-center campuses. Total heat rejected is ~equal to IT power drawn, so a campus's thermal footprint is a near-linear proxy for its live electrical load and therefore its GPU utilization.
ideas.collection: Fuse recurring thermal-infrared passes (Landsat-9 TIRS ~100m, ECOSTRESS off the ISS, and commercial thermal smallsats) over a hand-curated registry of 300+ hyperscale campuses. Register each thermal pixel to specific buildings and cooling equipment, subtract a per-site weather/ambient baseline (regressing out air temp, wind, humidity), and correct for cooling type (air vs. evaporative vs. liquid) to back out megawatts of IT load, then aggregate into a per-operator compute-ramp index.
ideas.instrument: NVDA stock and weekly options; secondarily hyperscaler equities (MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL) and data-center REITs EQIX and DLR, all with deep options chains.
ideas.mechanism: Aggregate live IT load across a hyperscaler's campuses is the physical embodiment of deployed accelerator capacity, which drives cloud revenue and the capex guidance the market trades on. Rising measured heat across a quarter is a direct, already-accumulated read on data-center revenue and next-quarter capex before those are guided.
ideas.lead: Thermal load accumulates continuously and is fully formed weeks before quarterly earnings/capex guidance and before EIA regional electricity data. Consensus still prices off the prior quarter's guide and sell-side channel checks.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is the build: a validated thermal-pixel-to-building registry, the weather/ambient-normalization model, and the cooling-type inversion that converts a fuzzy hot blob into megawatts. No finished 'data-center-load' dataset is licensable at this granularity; a rival must redo years of registry curation and calibration against known-nameplate sites.
ideas.why_clears_costs: NVDA trades near $180 with a $0.01 tick and ~$0.02 stock spread; data-center-revenue surprises routinely move it 6-10% (~$11-18/share). Capturing even a 1.5% pre-print drift is ~$2.70/share, ~135x the round-trip spread. ATM weekly options are penny-wide with multi-thousand-contract depth.
ideas.lens: Geospatial/sensor exhaust with a processing moat (imagery, RF/ADS-B, acoustic, thermal) that leads an official number

ideas.name: Electric-Arc-Furnace Thermal Pulse Index
ideas.source: The intense, transient thermal bloom emitted each time an electric-arc-furnace (EAF) melts a heat of scrap. Tap frequency and furnace-on duty cycle are a tight physical proxy for tons of crude steel produced at a mill.
ideas.collection: Task high-revisit thermal-IR smallsats and stack Landsat/ECOSTRESS passes over a registry of every US EAF minimill (Nucor, SDI, and peers). Detect the characteristic melt-cycle heat spikes, count heats per furnace per day, and convert duty cycle to tons using per-furnace nameplate calibration, building a weekly per-company output index.
ideas.instrument: NUE and STLD equities and options (both liquid large-caps), plus the SLX steel ETF.
ideas.mechanism: Measured heats-per-week maps almost directly onto raw steel tonnage, which is exactly the AISI weekly capacity-utilization figure and the quarterly shipment number these stocks trade on. Utilization is the single most-watched steel KPI.
ideas.lead: The AISI raw-steel-production and utilization report publishes Monday for the prior week; the thermal count is complete days earlier and, aggregated over a quarter, front-runs shipment guidance. Consensus reacts to AISI on release.
ideas.exclusivity: Moat is detecting and classifying sub-minute melt transients against a moving thermal background and calibrating each specific furnace's heat-to-tons ratio. This is a bespoke CV/thermal pipeline over a private mill registry, not a purchasable feed.
ideas.why_clears_costs: NUE near $140, $0.01 tick, ~$0.03-0.05 spread; steel-utilization and price surprises move it 3-5% (~$4-7/share). A 2% anticipatory move is ~$2.80/share, ~56x a nickel spread. SLX (~$70) and NUE options add penny-wide capacity.
ideas.lens: Geospatial/sensor exhaust with a processing moat (imagery, RF/ADS-B, acoustic, thermal) that leads an official number

ideas.name: Refinery Process-Heater Thermal Run-Rate
ideas.source: Fired-heater and FCC-regenerator thermal output at petroleum refineries. The thermal intensity of crude-distillation-unit charge heaters and cat-cracker regenerators scales with barrels processed, making it a direct proxy for refinery throughput.
ideas.collection: Stack thermal-IR passes (commercial thermal constellations + Landsat TIRS + VIIRS I-bands for hotspot confirmation) over every US refinery's process-unit footprint. Segment CDU heaters and FCC units by geolocation, derive a per-unit thermal index, subtract ambient baselines, and roll up to a weekly national and PADD-level crude-runs estimate.
ideas.instrument: VLO and MPC equities/options (very liquid), plus RBOB and heating-oil crack-spread futures (RB, HO vs. CL).
ideas.mechanism: Aggregate heater thermal output is a near-mechanical read on crude runs and refinery utilization, precisely the EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report utilization line and the throughput that drives crack spreads and refiner margins.
ideas.lead: EIA's report lands Wednesday for the week ending the prior Friday; the thermal read is complete before publication and detects unplanned rate cuts/turnarounds days ahead of the print. The whole crude-products complex prices off the lagging EIA number.
ideas.exclusivity: The build is unit-level segmentation (distinguishing CDU heaters from flares, coker heaters, and sulfur units) and the thermal-to-barrels calibration per refinery configuration. IIR's outage database is phone-verified and Genscape's Cushing work is tank shadows; independent process-unit throughput inference is a separate, costly pipeline.
ideas.why_clears_costs: RBOB near $2.30/gal, 42,000-gal contract worth ~$96,600, $0.0001 tick = $4.20; a utilization-driven 2c/gal crack move is ~$840/contract vs. a ~$4-8 round-trip. VLO (~$140) moves 3-6% on refining-margin surprises; a 2% pre-print drift is ~$2.80/share vs. a 3c spread (~93x).
ideas.lens: Geospatial/sensor exhaust with a processing moat (imagery, RF/ADS-B, acoustic, thermal) that leads an official number

ideas.name: Ammonia Synthesis-Loop Thermal Outage Detector
ideas.source: The steam-reformer and high-temperature synthesis-loop thermal signature of ammonia/urea plants. A running plant glows hot and steady; an unplanned trip shows as an abrupt thermal collapse, revealing lost nitrogen capacity that the operator has no obligation to announce in real time.
ideas.collection: Monitor a global registry of ammonia plants with high-revisit thermal-IR smallsats plus VIIRS/Landsat hotspot confirmation. Flag step-changes in per-plant thermal state (on/hot-standby/tripped), estimate tons/day of nitrogen offline, and net against known planned turnarounds to produce a real-time unplanned-outage tonnage index.
ideas.instrument: CF Industries (CF) and Nutrien (NTR) equities and options, both liquid.
ideas.mechanism: Nitrogen fertilizer is a thin, outage-driven market: a single large ammonia/urea trip removes enough supply to spike weekly urea/ammonia benchmarks, which is the price CF and NTR margins and quarterly volumes trade on. There is no trustworthy real-time official outage registry, so an independent thermal read is the only credible input.
ideas.lead: Thermal detection of a trip precedes the operator's disclosure, the weekly Green Markets/ICIS nitrogen price fixings, and any USDA/company volume print by days to weeks. The market moves only when the price service or the company confirms.
ideas.exclusivity: Combines 'physical/thermal observation' with 'measure what has no official number.' The moat is a maintained plant registry, planned-turnaround calendar, and a trip-detection model tuned to reformer/synthesis-loop thermal behavior. No vendor sells a clean real-time global ammonia-outage tape.
ideas.why_clears_costs: CF near $90, $0.01 tick, ~$0.03 spread; nitrogen-price and outage news move it 4-8% (~$3.60-7/share). A 3% anticipatory move is ~$2.70/share, ~90x the spread. CF options are penny-to-nickel wide with real depth.
ideas.lens: Geospatial/sensor exhaust with a processing moat (imagery, RF/ADS-B, acoustic, thermal) that leads an official number

ideas.name: Cement Kiln Active-Burn Thermal Census
ideas.source: Rotary-kiln thermal emission at cement plants. A kiln burning clinker is one of the hottest, most unambiguous industrial thermal sources; on/off state and burn intensity map almost one-to-one onto clinker (and thus cement) tonnage.
ideas.collection: Stack thermal-IR and SWIR passes (Landsat TIRS, ECOSTRESS, VIIRS Nightfire-class hotspot bands, commercial thermal) over a registry of every US cement kiln. Classify each kiln as burning/idle per pass, estimate clinker rate from thermal magnitude, weight by regional footprint, and roll up to a monthly volume index by producer and region.
ideas.instrument: Vulcan Materials (VMC) and Martin Marietta (MLM) equities and options, both liquid large-caps (~$20-40B).
ideas.mechanism: Kiln burn-hours are a tight proxy for clinker/cement volumes, which drive the shipment tonnage that dominates VMC/MLM quarterly results and the USGS Mineral Industry Surveys cement series. Volume beats/misses, not price, move these stocks.
ideas.lead: Thermal accumulates through the quarter and is essentially complete before earnings; it also front-runs USGS's lagged monthly cement stats by weeks. Consensus tracks price surveys and prior-quarter volumes.
ideas.exclusivity: Moat is a maintained kiln registry with per-kiln thermal-to-clinker calibration and the discipline to separate kiln burn from adjacent flares/heaters and cloud contamination. This is unglamorous CV/thermal engineering, not a licensable 'cement output' feed.
ideas.why_clears_costs: VMC near $280, $0.01 tick, ~$0.05-0.10 spread; volume surprises move it 3-5% (~$8-14/share). A 2% pre-print drift is ~$5.60/share, ~70x a dime spread. VMC/MLM options are liquid with tight quotes.
ideas.lens: Geospatial/sensor exhaust with a processing moat (imagery, RF/ADS-B, acoustic, thermal) that leads an official number

ideas.name: AIS-Dark Tanker RF-Geolocation Flow Meter
ideas.source: Radio-frequency emissions (navigation radar, VHF, satcom uplinks) from crude tankers that have switched off their AIS transponders to hide sanctioned Russian/Iranian/Venezuelan cargoes. The vessels vanish from AIS but still radiate detectable RF.
ideas.collection: Fuse commercial spaceborne RF-geolocation feeds (HawkEye 360, Unseenlabs, Kleos) with SAR ship-detection (Sentinel-1, ICEYE, Capella) to place and classify tankers that are dark to AIS. Chain detections into voyages, infer laden/ballast from SAR draft, and build a weekly dark-fleet crude-lifting-volume estimate by origin.
ideas.instrument: Brent and WTI crude futures (CL, BZ) and the USO ETF; extremely deep, cheap-to-trade.
ideas.mechanism: Sanctioned barrels are an economically huge but officially unmeasured slice of global supply. An independent count of dark-fleet liftings corrects the supply picture the IEA/OPEC/EIA balances get wrong, and crude reprices as those balances and sanctions-enforcement headlines catch up.
ideas.lead: RF+SAR detections are near-real-time, weeks ahead of monthly IEA/OPEC supply reports and slower than any official series on grey flows (which effectively doesn't exist). The market prices off delayed balances and headlines.
ideas.exclusivity: Explicitly the 'physical/exclusive-access + measure-what-has-no-official-number' moat: RF geolocation requires exclusively-licensed constellations, and the fusion/entity-resolution across RF and SAR to reconstruct a dark voyage is bespoke. AIS-based trackers (heavily worked) go blind exactly here.
ideas.why_clears_costs: WTI near $70; contract = 1,000 bbl worth $70,000, $0.01 tick = $10/bbl-lot. A supply-revision-driven $0.50-2.00/bbl move is $500-2,000/contract against a ~$10-20 round-trip. Even a 30c move clears costs 15x.
ideas.lens: Geospatial/sensor exhaust with a processing moat (imagery, RF/ADS-B, acoustic, thermal) that leads an official number

ideas.name: SAR All-Weather Iron-Ore Port Stockpile Volumetrics
ideas.source: Iron-ore stockpile volumes at China's major import ports. Optical pile-counting is defeated by the region's persistent cloud and haze; synthetic-aperture radar sees through both, day and night.
ideas.collection: Run Sentinel-1 plus commercial SAR (ICEYE, Capella, Umbra) over the ore yards at Qingdao, Rizhao, Caofeidian and peers. Use SAR amplitude/shadow and interferometric height to reconstruct pile geometry and convert to tonnage with density calibration, producing a weekly aggregate port-inventory estimate independent of weather.
ideas.instrument: SGX 62% Fe iron-ore futures and DCE contracts; plus RIO, BHP, and VALE ADRs (all liquid).
ideas.mechanism: Chinese port stockpiles are the dominant swing indicator for iron-ore pricing; the weekly Mysteel/SteelHome survey is what the futures react to. An all-weather SAR read anticipates that survey and the inventory swings that set the price.
ideas.lead: SAR gives a complete weekly volumetric even under total cloud cover, ahead of the surveyed inventory print and free of the multi-day optical gaps rivals suffer. The futures move on the survey.
ideas.exclusivity: Moat is SAR-specific: converting radar backscatter and layover into pile volumes and calibrating ore density is a hard, distinct pipeline versus optical parking-lot counting, and it keeps working when optical (what most vendors use) is clouded out for weeks.
ideas.why_clears_costs: SGX 62% Fe futures near $110/t, 100-t lot = ~$11,000, $0.01/t tick; a 2-4% inventory-driven move is $2-4/t = $200-400/lot vs. a few-dollar round-trip. VALE ADR (~$11) moves 2-3% (~$0.28) against a $0.01 tick/1c spread, ~28x.
ideas.lens: Geospatial/sensor exhaust with a processing moat (imagery, RF/ADS-B, acoustic, thermal) that leads an official number

ideas.name: Sentinel-5P NO2 China Industrial-Activity Nowcast
ideas.source: Tropospheric nitrogen-dioxide column density over China's industrial clusters. NO2 is a combustion byproduct of heavy industry, power generation, and freight, making its satellite-measured column a physical proxy for real industrial output in an economy whose official statistics are widely distrusted.
ideas.collection: Ingest daily Sentinel-5P TROPOMI NO2 retrievals, mask to industrial polygons (Yangtze/Pearl River deltas, Hebei steel belt, etc.), correct for meteorology (boundary-layer height, wind ventilation) and seasonal/holiday effects, and build a de-weathered weekly industrial-activity index distinct from methane leak detection.
ideas.instrument: COMEX copper futures (HG) and the FXI China large-cap ETF; secondarily BHP/RIO as China-demand proxies. All liquid.
ideas.mechanism: De-weathered NO2 tracks industrial production and thus the metals-demand impulse the market prices. It front-runs and cross-checks the NBS monthly industrial-output figure and official PMIs, which markets treat skeptically precisely because they can be smoothed.
ideas.lead: Daily satellite retrievals aggregate into a weekly read weeks before NBS monthly output and ahead of the official PMIs. The distrust of the official series means there is no clean consensus number for the edge to decay against.
ideas.exclusivity: Moat is the meteorological de-confounding and industrial-polygon masking that turns a noisy pollution column into an activity index; this is application/processing work far removed from methane-plume attribution, and TROPOMI's raw column alone is useless without it.
ideas.why_clears_costs: HG copper near $4.50/lb; 25,000-lb contract = ~$112,500, $0.0005 tick = $12.50. China-activity surprises routinely move copper 2-4c/lb = $500-1,000/contract vs. a ~$25 round-trip. FXI (~$35) moves 1-2% (~$0.35-0.70) against a penny spread.
ideas.lens: Geospatial/sensor exhaust with a processing moat (imagery, RF/ADS-B, acoustic, thermal) that leads an official number

ideas.name: GNSS-Reflectometry Root-Zone Soil-Moisture Yield Model
ideas.source: GPS/GNSS signals reflected off cropland, whose reflectivity encodes near-surface soil moisture. Microwave reflectometry penetrates cloud and reads moisture that optical NDVI cannot see, giving an early physical driver of eventual yield.
ideas.collection: Fuse commercial GNSS-R constellations (Spire, and NASA CYGNSS land products) with SMAP microwave radiometry and thermal-stress data into a proprietary root-zone soil-moisture field over the US Corn Belt, Brazil, and the Black Sea. Feed the moisture time-series through a calibrated agronomic model to nowcast yield deviations by region.
ideas.instrument: CBOT corn (ZC) and soybean (ZS) futures and options; among the deepest ag markets globally.
ideas.mechanism: Root-zone moisture through the critical grain-fill window is a leading physical determinant of final yield, which is the number USDA WASDE and Crop Progress reports deliver and grain futures violently reprice on. A moisture-driven yield nowcast anticipates those prints.
ideas.lead: Microwave reflectometry sees moisture stress weeks before it shows in optical greenness or in USDA's monthly WASDE yield and weekly Crop Progress condition ratings. The market moves on WASDE.
ideas.exclusivity: Moat is the multi-sensor fusion and agronomic calibration, not any single public feed: SMAP and CYGNSS are public but coarse and useless raw; the edge is the root-zone inversion and yield model that took years to tune (the Benter-of-soil-moisture build), which no one sells finished.
ideas.why_clears_costs: ZC corn near $4.50/bu; 5,000-bu contract = ~$22,500, $0.0025 tick = $12.50. WASDE yield surprises move corn 10-25c/bu = $500-1,250/contract vs. a ~$25 round-trip. Soybeans (ZS) carry even larger dollar swings; options are tight and deep.
ideas.lens: Geospatial/sensor exhaust with a processing moat (imagery, RF/ADS-B, acoustic, thermal) that leads an official number

ideas.name: Dark-Fiber DAS Rail-Traffic Census
ideas.source: Ground strain waves from passing trains, captured acoustically. Every locomotive and loaded car imprints a distinctive vibration on nearby buried fiber, so an interrogated fiber strand becomes a continuous train-counting sensor along a rail corridor.
ideas.collection: Acquire dark-fiber IRUs (or partner for fiber access) paralleling high-value rail corridors (Powder River Basin coal, major intermodal lanes) and run Distributed Acoustic Sensing interrogators. Classify axle counts, speed, direction, and loaded-vs-empty from strain waveforms with ML, yielding a real-time train- and car-count feed per corridor and per railroad.
ideas.instrument: Union Pacific (UNP), CSX, and Norfolk Southern (NSC) equities and options, all liquid.
ideas.mechanism: Corridor car-counts and loaded/empty mix roll up to the carload and intermodal volumes that drive railroad revenue and the quarterly volume/earnings numbers the stocks trade on, and lead the AAR weekly carload report.
ideas.lead: DAS is continuous and real-time; car-counts accumulate through the quarter, fully formed before earnings and ahead of the AAR weekly print and any company volume disclosure.
ideas.exclusivity: A hard physical + processing moat: it requires securing fiber access along specific corridors (capex/contract barrier a software rival cannot leap with code) plus a bespoke acoustic-classification model. Unlike the wayside defect-detector radio approach, DAS reconstructs full train composition, and the fiber footprint is exclusive to whoever contracts it.
ideas.why_clears_costs: UNP near $230, $0.01 tick, ~$0.03 spread; volume/earnings surprises move it 3-6% (~$7-14/share). A 2% anticipatory move is ~$4.60/share, ~150x the spread. CSX (~$35) moves 3-5% (~$1-1.75) against a 1-2c spread; all three have penny-wide, deep options.
ideas.lens: Geospatial/sensor exhaust with a processing moat (imagery, RF/ADS-B, acoustic, thermal) that leads an official number

ideas.name: Reinsurer Live-Cat Loss Model
ideas.source: NHC public advisories (track, wind radii), HWRF/HMON windfield model output, FEMA/USGS building-stock and parcel/property-value data, plus each carrier's statutory Schedule P and 10-K geographic exposure and per-occurrence retention/reinsurance tower.
ideas.collection: Run a private vulnerability-times-exposure catastrophe model: overlay the modeled windfield on gridded insured exposure, apply per-peril damage functions, and roll up to an industry insured-loss estimate and per-company net-of-reinsurance loss within hours of landfall.
ideas.instrument: RenaissanceRe (RNR), Everest (EG), Travelers (TRV), Allstate (ALL) common and listed options; RLI and other reinsurance-heavy names.
ideas.mechanism: Post-landfall the tape marks reinsurers off the headline 'Category X made landfall near Y' and TV damage imagery. A calibrated insured-loss number tells you whether the event breaches the industry threshold that actually dents a given carrier's tower versus is a non-event. Trade the gap before PCS/Verisk and sell-side notes converge.
ideas.lead: Hours to several days ahead of the PCS/Verisk industry loss estimate and analyst updates.
ideas.exclusivity: The vulnerability curves, exposure disaggregation, and per-company tower reconstruction are years of actuarial cat-modeling engineering (the RMS/Verisk moat). A rival must rebuild the model and re-map each carrier's book, not license a finished number.
ideas.why_clears_costs: RNR trades ~$230-260. A correct above/below-threshold call routinely drives a 5-15% move ($12-38/share) over 1-5 days. Stock spread is ~$0.02-0.05 on 1-cent ticks; even ATM options at a few-dollar premium move multiples of their spread. The dollar move dwarfs costs by roughly two orders of magnitude.
ideas.lens: Private model on public data (the Benter template): a market with an unsophisticated marginal price-setter you out-model

ideas.name: Agency mREIT Book-Value Nowcast
ideas.source: Daily TBA/agency-MBS and specified-pool prices (dealer runs / TRACE), on-the-run Treasury and swap curves, and the REIT's last 10-Q portfolio disclosure (coupon stack, CPR assumptions, hedge notionals, duration/convexity).
ideas.collection: Reconstruct each mREIT's asset and hedge book from the 10-Q, then mark it daily against live MBS and rate moves with a prepayment/convexity model to produce a running book-value-per-share estimate and dividend-coverage read.
ideas.instrument: Annaly (NLY), AGNC Investment (AGNC), and agency-mREIT peers plus their liquid options.
ideas.mechanism: mREITs are ~70% retail-held and trade off trailing dividend yield and headline rates; the crowd only learns book value at the quarterly print. A private daily BV mark tells you whether the quarter's book value is up or down mid-to-high single digits and whether the dividend is covered, before disclosure.
ideas.lead: Continuous through the quarter; a full book-value estimate weeks before the earnings release.
ideas.exclusivity: Correctly reconstructing the portfolio and marking convexity/prepayment is real fixed-income quant work. You cannot license 'NLY's book value today' — the number does not exist until you compute it.
ideas.why_clears_costs: NLY ~$19-21, AGNC ~$9-10. A book-value surprise moves the stock 3-8% (about $0.60-1.60 on NLY) in a day. Spread is penny-wide on 1-cent ticks and options are penny-quoted and liquid, so the move is 30-150x the spread.
ideas.lens: Private model on public data (the Benter template): a market with an unsophisticated marginal price-setter you out-model

ideas.name: Constant-Quality Used-Vehicle Price Nowcast
ideas.source: Public retail and dealer used-car listing prices scraped across marketplaces (make/model/trim/mileage/region), auction consignment listings, and the lagged, paywalled Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index as the anchor the market prices off.
ideas.collection: Build a hedonic mix-adjustment model that converts the noisy listing panel into a constant-quality wholesale price index calibrated to reproduce Manheim, then nowcast the next Manheim print and each retailer's realized gross profit per unit.
ideas.instrument: CarMax (KMX) and Carvana (CVNA) common and options; Ally (ALLY) and auto-ABS spreads as secondary expressions.
ideas.mechanism: KMX/CVNA earnings and the used-car complex move on wholesale price direction and GPU; the crowd waits for the mid-month Manheim release and the quarterly print. A constant-quality nowcast front-runs both, telling you the sign and size of the GPU surprise in advance.
ideas.lead: 1-3 weeks ahead of the Manheim index release; a full-quarter GPU read before earnings.
ideas.exclusivity: Manheim is paywalled and lagged. The moat is the hedonic mix-adjustment model that turns free, biased listings into a Manheim-quality constant-quality index — years of feature engineering, not a licensed dataset.
ideas.why_clears_costs: CVNA ~$250-350 moves 6-15% ($20-50) on used-car data; KMX ~$70-85 moves 4-10% ($3-8). Spreads are a few cents and options are deeply liquid, so the move is hundreds of times the tick.
ideas.lens: Private model on public data (the Benter template): a market with an unsophisticated marginal price-setter you out-model

ideas.name: Restaurant Comp Price/Mix Model
ideas.source: Public item-level menu prices scraped location-by-location from chain ordering apps and sites nationwide (item prices, limited-time offers, portion/price changes), plus each chain's disclosed same-store-sales definition and historical price-versus-traffic decomposition.
ideas.collection: Build a geo-panel of item-level menu prices, compute the exact price/mix contribution to same-store sales per each chain's own definition, and layer a demand-elasticity model to net out the traffic response.
ideas.instrument: McDonald's (MCD), Chipotle (CMG), Starbucks (SBUX), Darden (DRI) common and options.
ideas.mechanism: Comps = traffic + price/mix. The price/mix half is fully observable from menu data and accumulates continuously, while consensus prices off stale prior-quarter menu pricing and macro sentiment. Predict the pricing contribution to comps before the print.
ideas.lead: Menu changes land throughout the quarter and the pricing contribution is fully formed weeks before the comps release.
ideas.exclusivity: The national item-level scrape reconciled to each chain's precise comp definition, plus the elasticity model, is a YipitData-class build. You cannot license 'CMG's Q3 pricing contribution.'
ideas.why_clears_costs: CMG ~$50-60 (post-split) moves 5-12% on comps; MCD ~$290 moves 3-6% ($9-17). Penny ticks, tight spreads, deep options; the comp-driven move is 50-200x costs.
ideas.lens: Private model on public data (the Benter template): a market with an unsophisticated marginal price-setter you out-model

ideas.name: Airline Unit-Revenue Inversion Model
ideas.source: Live published fares scraped by origin-destination market, fare-class buckets and seat availability across carriers' booking engines and GDS shopping, plus each airline's scheduled available seat miles and historical booking-curve shape.
ideas.collection: Invert the fare-plus-availability panel through a yield-management booking-curve model to nowcast unit revenue (PRASM/TRASM) per carrier for the whole quarter — not a single fare-bucket tell but a full revenue reconstruction.
ideas.instrument: Delta (DAL), United (UAL), American (AAL), Southwest (LUV) common and options.
ideas.mechanism: The crowd trades airlines mostly off jet-fuel prices and headlines and only learns unit revenue at the mid-quarter investor update or earnings. A RASM nowcast built from the booking curve leads that, giving the sign and size of the unit-revenue guidance surprise early.
ideas.lead: Weeks; bookings for the quarter accumulate and the curve is largely set before the guidance update.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is the booking-curve inversion model (fare bucket plus availability into realized yield) calibrated per carrier and route bank — real revenue-management engineering, not a scraped price anyone can also scrape.
ideas.why_clears_costs: DAL ~$45-60, UAL ~$80-100. A RASM guidance surprise moves them 5-12% ($3-12). Cent-wide spreads and penny-quoted liquid options mean the move is 100x-plus the tick.
ideas.lens: Private model on public data (the Benter template): a market with an unsophisticated marginal price-setter you out-model

ideas.name: Earnings-Move Overpricing Model
ideas.source: Public option chains (implied straddle/ATM vol into each print), the company's guidance-versus-actual surprise history, business seasonality, and a fundamental nowcast of the quarter's key reported line versus consensus.
ideas.collection: Build a private model of the realized earnings-move distribution per name (expected absolute move plus tail shape), then compare it to the option-implied move to rank names where implied is rich or cheap, folding the crowd's implied back in as a model feature.
ideas.instrument: Liquid large-cap single-stock options — sell overpriced straddles/strangles or buy underpriced ones, delta-hedged, across an earnings-season book.
ideas.mechanism: Retail systematically overpays for earnings lottery convexity on high-attention names and underprices moves on 'boring' names. A calibrated realized-move model harvests the gap. This is Benter-pure: a fundamental distribution with the crowd's implied distribution folded in so the final estimate beats both.
ideas.lead: You know the implied is mispriced days before the scheduled print; the edge is a strictly better distribution than the marginal option buyer holds.
ideas.exclusivity: The per-name realized-move and surprise-magnitude model, trained across many seasons and calibrated to each name's behavior, is the build. The chain is public but the fair distribution is not.
ideas.why_clears_costs: On a $100-300 name the implied earnings move is often 5-8% ($5-24) of premium. A typical 1-2 vol-point mispricing is ~$0.30-1.00 of edge per straddle against a $0.05-0.15 option spread — several times the spread, repeated across dozens of names each season for large aggregate capacity.
ideas.lens: Private model on public data (the Benter template): a market with an unsophisticated marginal price-setter you out-model

ideas.name: Clinical Probability-of-Success Model
ideas.source: ClinicalTrials.gov design fields (phase, endpoints, N, randomization, control, biomarker enrichment), the sponsor's prior-phase public data, mechanism-of-action class base rates, and a hand-labeled database of decades of historical trial outcomes.
ideas.collection: Train a phase-transition probability-of-success model on trial-design features, output a calibrated PoS for each pending readout, then fold in the option-implied probability from the event straddle to form a final estimate that dominates both the raw model and the market.
ideas.instrument: Liquid biotech options (mid/large-cap single names and XBI), held as a diversified book of independent binary bets.
ideas.mechanism: Retail biotech traders over-handicap hype and headline mechanism. A disciplined PoS model priced against the option-implied probability finds systematically mispriced binary readouts; diversifying across many independent names ensures no single break is fatal (Paulson discipline).
ideas.lead: The model's better prior exists before each scheduled readout or PDUFA date — the estimate is complete while the crowd is still pricing off narrative.
ideas.exclusivity: The labeled outcome database plus feature engineering plus calibration is an Intelligencia/BioAI-class build taking years. The registry is public; the trained model that maps design features to true odds is not.
ideas.why_clears_costs: Binary readouts move names 40-100% ($10-40 on a $30-50 stock); straddles cost 15-40% of spot. A 10-15 percentage-point PoS edge sized across 30-50 independent names produces expected edge many multiples of the (wider but tradable) biotech option spreads, with the diversification carrying the variance.
ideas.lens: Private model on public data (the Benter template): a market with an unsophisticated marginal price-setter you out-model

ideas.name: P&C Reserve-Adequacy Triangle Model
ideas.source: Statutory Schedule P loss-development triangles from public annual and quarterly statutory filings, industry development patterns, line-of-business mix, and social-inflation/loss-trend indicators.
ideas.collection: Fit a private reserving model to each insurer's triangles to estimate ultimate losses and the gap versus carried reserves, flagging pending adverse or favorable reserve development before it is booked to GAAP.
ideas.instrument: Travelers (TRV), Chubb (CB), Allstate (ALL), Hartford (HIG), Cincinnati Financial (CINF) common and options.
ideas.mechanism: Reserve charges and releases are discrete earnings surprises the crowd only learns at the print. The statutory triangles telegraph inadequacy or redundancy quarters ahead. Trade the expected development gap into the report.
ideas.lead: Statutory data and the triangle signal lead the GAAP charge by one or more quarters.
ideas.exclusivity: Correct triangle reserving — tail factors, curve fitting, line-mix adjustment, calendar-year diagonal effects — is unglamorous actuarial work. You cannot license 'TRV's coming reserve charge.'
ideas.why_clears_costs: TRV ~$240, CB ~$280. A material reserve charge or release moves the stock 3-8% ($7-22). Cent spreads and liquid options make the move 100x-plus the tick.
ideas.lens: Private model on public data (the Benter template): a market with an unsophisticated marginal price-setter you out-model

ideas.name: Auto-Parts Comp Demand Model
ideas.source: Public FHWA vehicle-miles-traveled data, IHS/BEA fleet-age and registration data, realized regional weather (harsh-winter and heat stress drive failure rates), and gas prices; plus each retailer's DIY-versus-commercial mix and comp definition.
ideas.collection: Build a private parts-demand model mapping already-realized miles-driven, aging fleet, and weather stress to same-store sales for each chain, using realized (not forecast) inputs so there is no weather-forecast risk.
ideas.instrument: AutoZone (AZO), O'Reilly Automotive (ORLY), Advance Auto Parts (AAP) common and options.
ideas.mechanism: The crowd trades auto-parts retail off consumer-sentiment and recession headlines, but the true demand drivers — miles driven, fleet age, weather-induced failures — are largely realized during the quarter and predict comps before the print.
ideas.lead: The driving and weather inputs are realized through the quarter; the comp nowcast is complete weeks before earnings.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is the demand model that translates macro and weather exhaust into each chain's exact comp, calibrated per banner and DIY/commercial mix — not a purchasable number.
ideas.why_clears_costs: AZO ~$3,300/share moves 4-9% on comps ($130-300 per share); ORLY moves 4-8%. Even at a wider few-dollar spread on the high-priced AZO, a $130+ move clears it by ~40x, and options are liquid.
ideas.lens: Private model on public data (the Benter template): a market with an unsophisticated marginal price-setter you out-model

ideas.name: Utility Realized-Weather Earnings Model
ideas.source: Realized degree-day and weather data by service territory (NOAA), each utility's disclosed load shape and customer mix, and — critically — its regulatory weather-normalization mechanism (decoupling / weather riders versus full exposure) from rate-case filings.
ideas.collection: Convert already-realized quarter weather into a per-utility EPS weather contribution, adjusting for whether the tariff normalizes weather (no earnings effect) or passes it through (full effect).
ideas.instrument: NextEra (NEE), Duke (DUK), Southern (SO), Dominion (D) common and options.
ideas.mechanism: The crowd treats utilities as bond proxies and is repeatedly surprised by weather-driven volume and O&M beats and misses. Because the weather is already realized during the quarter, the earnings contribution is fully formed before the print; the key modeling insight is which utilities are actually exposed versus decoupled.
ideas.lead: Weather is realized through the quarter, so the EPS-contribution read is complete before the earnings release.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is the load-shape plus regulatory-mechanism model per utility (decoupled versus exposed). Inputs are public, but the bespoke mapping from realized degree-days to reported EPS is the work.
ideas.why_clears_costs: NEE ~$70, DUK ~$110. A weather-driven EPS surprise moves a utility 2-4% ($1.5-4.5). Penny ticks, tight spreads, and liquid options make the move 30-90x the spread, and it fires every reporting cycle across many names.
ideas.lens: Private model on public data (the Benter template): a market with an unsophisticated marginal price-setter you out-model

ideas.name: BNPL Checkout-Offer Panel
ideas.source: Buy-now-pay-later widgets (Affirm/Afterpay/Klarna) rendered at merchant checkouts, which expose the offered installment term, APR, approved amount, and approve/decline outcome per cart.
ideas.collection: A fleet of headless browsers driven by a rotating library of synthetic shopper identities (varied BIN ranges, device fingerprints, cart sizes) adds SKUs to cart across thousands of Affirm-integrated merchants and scrapes the live offer object: 0% vs interest-bearing, term length, 'as low as $X/mo', and decline reasons. Aggregate approval rate, average offered APR, and 0%-promo share by merchant and by inferred credit tier.
ideas.instrument: Affirm (AFRM) equity and options; secondarily large-cap merchant partners whose GMV rides on Affirm financing.
ideas.mechanism: Affirm's reported GMV, take rate, and revenue-less-transaction-costs (RLTC) are driven by approval rates, promo mix, and funding cost.
