Rising decline rates and higher offered APR signal tightening plus margin pressure; falling 0%-promo share signals weaker take rate. The panel nowcasts the exact P&L levers before the print.
ideas.lead: Offers are read continuously through the quarter; approval and APR shifts show up in real time, while consensus waits for the roughly six-week-lagged earnings release.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is the cart-simulation + identity-farm + offer-parser infrastructure and the merchant-coverage map that resolves each offer back to Affirm's reported segments, plus a live anti-bot arms race. Anyone can see one offer on one site; nobody else has computed the population-level approval/APR surface. Rebuilding it is quarters of engineering, not a license fee.
ideas.why_clears_costs: AFRM trades roughly $50-70 and routinely moves 15-25% on earnings, about $8-15/share. The stock has a penny tick and ~1-2c spread with deep weekly options, so one correct GMV/RLTC read clears costs by roughly three orders of magnitude.

ideas.name: National Menu-Price Grid
ideas.source: Restaurant chains' own digital menus, which carry item-level prices that vary by store and change on a rolling basis - the price/mix half of same-store sales that management guides to explicitly.
ideas.collection: Query each chain's store-locator and delivery-app menu endpoints (chain app, DoorDash, Uber Eats) for every location nightly, capturing per-SKU price. Compute a store-count-weighted national menu-price index, regional pass-through of announced price increases, and stealth mix changes (item removals, size or portion re-pricing).
ideas.instrument: Chipotle (CMG), McDonald's (MCD), Starbucks (SBUX), Wingstop (WING) - equity and options.
ideas.mechanism: Comps = transaction growth x ticket, and ticket is dominated by menu pricing. The grid measures the pricing component with near-perfect fidelity across the whole footprint, pinning down a large, known fraction of the reported comp before the print - and flags when a chain quietly raises or holds price versus what it guided.
ideas.lead: Prices are locked into the menu the moment an increase goes live, weeks-to-months before the quarter's comp is reported; the full-footprint average is computable in real time.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is full-footprint nightly coverage plus SKU normalization across menu versions and delivery-inflated prices (reconciling third-party markups back to in-store), mapped to each chain's comp geography. A one-store or one-city sample is worthless; the population panel is the edge. Distinct from stealth price-test sniffing, which flags experiments rather than the national price level.
ideas.why_clears_costs: MCD ~$300 moving 3-5% is $9-15/share; CMG (post-split ~$50) moving 5-8% is $3-4; SBUX ~$95 moving 5-9% is $5-8. Penny ticks, ~1c spreads, deep option chains - the pricing read alone clears costs many times over.

ideas.name: Achievement-Unlock Install-Base Nowcast
ideas.source: Per-title achievement/trophy global-completion percentages published by Steam, PlayStation, and Xbox, which mechanically encode how many unique owners have reached each stage of a game.
ideas.collection: Poll global achievement-rarity tables for target titles at launch and daily after; anchor the 'started the game' achievement to a calibrated owner-count model (rarity-to-owners regression trained on titles with later-disclosed sell-through), fused across all three platforms and adjusted for subscription bundling, free weekends, and region locks.
ideas.instrument: Take-Two (TTWO) and Electronic Arts (EA) - equity and options.
ideas.mechanism: A single tentpole release (GTA, NBA 2K, EA Sports FC, Battlefield) makes or breaks the quarter's bookings. Owner count back-solved from achievement percentages nowcasts units sold within days of launch, versus a bookings print weeks later.
ideas.lead: Launches typically fall mid-quarter; achievement data accumulates from hour zero, giving a multi-week lead on the units/bookings disclosure.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is the cross-platform rarity-to-owners calibration model and the contamination controls (subscription plays, delisted achievements, regional gating), not the public percentages themselves. Already-generated wishlist and preorder counts only proxy intent; owner count from post-launch unlocks measures the realized sale.

ideas.exclusivity: The moat is full-fleet, full-schedule daily capture with cabin-category normalization and a year-over-year same-days-to-sail curve model - not a spot price check. ideas.name: Vol-Control De-Risk Cascade
ideas.source: The managed-volatility complex: variable-annuity vol-control sub-accounts, risk-parity funds, and CTA vol-target overlays all rebalance daily toward a fixed volatility budget. Inputs are public: daily realized vol (from index prints), the funds' disclosed target-vol bands and lookback windows (annuity prospectuses, risk-parity fact sheets), and estimated AUM.
ideas.collection: Reconstruct the complex's aggregate equity exposure as a function of trailing realized vol: scrape target-vol parameters and lookback lengths from ~40 large VA prospectuses and risk-parity fund documents, estimate AUM per sleeve from N-PORT/annual filings and NAIC separate-account data, then run their published deleveraging formula on live realized-vol to produce a next-day forced-buy/sell notional in ES.
ideas.instrument: E-mini S&P 500 futures (ES) and 10yr Treasury futures (TY) for the risk-parity leg.
ideas.mechanism: When a vol spike pushes realized vol above the target band, every vol-control sleeve must mechanically cut equity exposure the following session regardless of price; the aggregate sell notional is computable the evening before. Position ahead of the concentrated, price-insensitive deleveraging (and the symmetric re-leveraging as vol mean-reverts).
ideas.lead: 12-36 hours: the deleveraging is a deterministic function of a realized-vol number that is already fixed at today's close, but the mechanical trades execute across tomorrow's session.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is the reconstruction, not the data: correctly mapping which sleeves use 20d vs 60d lookbacks, one-day vs multi-day rebalance smoothing, and their true AUM. A rival must re-do the prospectus archaeology and calibrate the response function; the raw vol number is worthless without the exposure model. Distinct from leveraged-ETF EOD rebalancing (that's a same-day 4pm print on a tiny AUM base); this is a next-day, multi-hundred-billion-dollar target-vol base.
ideas.why_clears_costs: ES tick = 0.25 pt = $12.50/contract; round-trip cost ~1 tick + commission ≈ $16. A modeled deleveraging event moves ES 0.5-1.5% intraday = 27-82 pts = $1,350-$4,100 per contract. Edge dwarfs cost by ~100x, and ES trades ~1.5M contracts/day so capacity is effectively unlimited.
ideas.lens: Flow/positioning/microstructure mechanics that force predictable, computable trades in liquid instruments

ideas.name: Buffer-ETF FLEX Roll Front-Run
ideas.source: Defined-outcome ('buffer'/'floor') ETFs (Innovator, First Trust, Allianz, Calamos) now hold ~$60B in FLEX options. ideas.collection: Scrape each fund's daily holdings file and outcome-period calendar to get exact strikes, notionals, and reset dates; aggregate across the complex to a per-day 'FLEX roll schedule' listing which SPX strikes will see forced buy/sell of what size and on which morning.
ideas.instrument: SPX index options and SPY options; hedge residual with ES.
ideas.mechanism: On each reset date the funds must, price-insensitively, buy a ~1-delta call and sell a call at the new cap and buy the buffer put spread. This concentrates demand at specific strikes and reliably bids/offers skew and term vol at those strikes. Trade the predictable local vol/skew dislocation before the roll prints.
ideas.lead: 1-10 trading days: the reset date and approximate strikes are known from the calendar and prior holdings weeks ahead; the exact new strikes crystallize as the reset spot is approached.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is stitching the full complex's FLEX ladder — hundreds of series across dozens of funds with staggered monthly/quarterly resets — into one net strike-level demand curve. Anyone can see one fund's holdings; nobody else has computed the aggregate roll pressure at each strike. Distinct from the JHEQX collar (single fund, quarterly) — this is a fragmented $60B complex with resets nearly every week.
ideas.why_clears_costs: SPX options carry a $100 multiplier; penny/nickel ticks. The strike-concentrated roll demand shifts local implied vol ~0.5-1.5 vol pts; at ~$8-15 vega per vol point on a 1-year ATM-ish SPX contract that is $4-22 of edge per contract vs a $0.10-0.50 spread. Trading it via SPY (tick $0.01) the analogous per-contract edge is $0.30-0.80 vs a $0.02 spread.
ideas.lens: Flow/positioning/microstructure mechanics that force predictable, computable trades in liquid instruments

ideas.name: Income-ETF Call-Write Roll Pin
ideas.source: Covered-call income ETFs (JEPI, JEPQ, QYLD, XYLD, RYLD, plus levered single-stock call-writers) now exceed ~$90B and mechanically write index/ELN calls on a fixed monthly schedule (e.g., QYLD/XYLD write ATM calls tied to the third-Friday cycle and roll at expiry).
ideas.collection: Pull each fund's holdings/prospectus to extract its option-writing rule (strike moneyness, notional coverage %, roll date), estimate the written notional from AUM, and aggregate to a monthly 'forced call-write' calendar plus a net dealer long-gamma map at the written strikes.
ideas.instrument: Nasdaq-100 futures (NQ) and S&P 500 futures (ES); NDX/SPX options for the vol leg.
ideas.mechanism: The complex is a large, scheduled seller of upside vol and a source of dealer long-gamma clustered at the written strikes, which suppresses realized vol and pins spot toward those strikes into expiry. Trade the mechanical vol-supply (short-vol into the write, cover after) and the pin drift into the roll.
ideas.lead: 1-15 days: writing/roll dates are calendar-fixed; the strikes are set by the roll-day spot, so the pin location is estimable days ahead and precise on roll morning.
ideas.exclusivity: Moat is reconstructing the writing schedule, moneyness rules, and notional across a dozen funds with different mechanics (some write ATM index, some sell ELNs, some do daily/weekly writes) into one net gamma-by-strike surface. Distinct from generic GEX: this isolates the deterministic, AUM-scaled income-ETF supply rather than the whole-market gamma estimate.
ideas.why_clears_costs: NQ tick = 0.25 = $5/contract; round-trip ~$12. A modeled pin drift of 0.3-0.8% on NQ (~19,500) = 60-160 pts = $1,200-$3,200/contract. The short-vol leg captures 0.5-1.0 vol pt of over-supplied upside vol. Both clear costs by orders of magnitude; ES/NQ depth absorbs size.
ideas.lens: Flow/positioning/microstructure mechanics that force predictable, computable trades in liquid instruments

ideas.name: Treasury Futures Roll Congestion
ideas.source: CME Treasury futures (TU/FV/TY/US/UB) roll every quarter from front to back contract. Positioning is structurally one-sided: asset managers are net long and leveraged funds net short (CFTC Traders-in-Financial-Futures), so the roll's calendar-spread is pushed predictably as the long side rolls forward earlier and larger.
ideas.collection: Track daily open-interest migration between front and back contracts per instrument, overlay CFTC TFF net positioning to infer roll direction/size, and model the historical roll path (spread cheapening as the crowded long side rolls) to time entry into the calendar spread.
ideas.instrument: TY (10yr) and US/UB (bond/ultra) calendar spreads, and the outright front contract.
ideas.mechanism: The dominant long cohort must roll to avoid delivery, mechanically demanding the calendar spread in size; the spread dislocates from fair (carry + CTD optionality) during peak roll days. Provide the other side of the congestion and capture the reversion post-roll.
ideas.lead: 3-10 sessions: OI migration and the TFF long/short imbalance telegraph the roll's direction and intensity before the bulk of it executes in the roll's compressed window.
ideas.exclusivity: Moat is the joint inference layer — normalizing OI migration into an expected roll-flow size and conditioning on the TFF cohort imbalance and CTD/carry fair value. Raw OI and COT are public; the calibrated 'how mispriced will this specific roll get' model is the work. Not on the excluded list (Goldman roll is commodity; this is the rates futures roll).
ideas.why_clears_costs: TY tick = 1/2 of 1/32 = $15.63/contract. At peak congestion the calendar spread dislocates ~1-3/32 from fair = $31-94/contract vs ~1-2 tick round-trip cost ($16-31). On US/UB the DV01 is larger so the dislocation is $60-180. TY trades ~2M contracts/day, giving enormous capacity even on a few-tick edge.
ideas.lens: Flow/positioning/microstructure mechanics that force predictable, computable trades in liquid instruments

ideas.name: Auction Concession Cycle
ideas.source: The Treasury auction calendar is fixed and market-moving. Dealers must absorb supply, so the specific issue and its futures cheapen into the auction ('concession') and richen after, with magnitude conditioned on dealer inventory (weekly FR 2004 primary-dealer positions) and auction size.
ideas.collection: Combine the published auction calendar/sizes with FR 2004 net dealer Treasury positions by tenor to estimate how much concession dealers will demand for each auction, then model the cheapening path into and the reversion out of each auction for the on-the-run tenor.
ideas.instrument: On-the-run note/bond futures (TY, FV, US) and the CTD.
ideas.mechanism: Underwriting the auction is a scheduled, price-insensitive absorption event; when dealer balance sheets are already heavy, they demand a larger yield concession pre-auction and unwind after, producing a repeatable cheapen-then-richen path in the liquid future. Position for both legs.
ideas.lead: 1-5 days: the auction date/size are known well ahead; the concession builds over the two-to-three sessions before the auction and reverses over the day or two after.
ideas.exclusivity: Moat is conditioning the concession model on dealer inventory (FR 2004) and recent auction tails/bid-to-covers — turning a well-known calendar into a sized, inventory-aware forecast of concession depth. Distinct from settlement-fails (FR 2004 fails data) ideas already listed; this uses dealer position/inventory to forecast auction concession, a different mechanism.
ideas.why_clears_costs: TY DV01 ≈ $65-70/contract per bp. A typical 1.5-3 bp concession-and-reversal path = ~$100-210 of round-trip capture per contract vs ~$16-31 cost. FV/US variants scale with tenor. Auctions recur ~weekly across tenors, giving high repeatability in the deepest rates market on earth.
ideas.lens: Flow/positioning/microstructure mechanics that force predictable, computable trades in liquid instruments

ideas.name: Month-End Agg Duration Extension
ideas.source: The Bloomberg US Aggregate and Treasury indices rebalance at each month-end: newly issued Treasuries enter and the index's duration 'extends'. Index-tracking bond funds and ETFs (~multi-trillion AUM) must mechanically buy duration on the last day to match, and the extension size is computable from that month's issuance and coupon roll-down.
ideas.collection: Ingest the month's Treasury auction results and coupon schedule, replicate the index inclusion rules to compute the projected month-end duration extension (in years), and translate into the aggregate DV01 that passive funds must add — producing a per-month-end forced-buy magnitude.
ideas.instrument: TY and UXY (ultra 10yr) Treasury futures; the on-the-run long end.
ideas.mechanism: The extension forces a concentrated, price-insensitive duration purchase into the month-end close; larger extensions (heavy long-end issuance months) reliably richen yields into the close and can fade after. Front-run the mechanical duration bid.
ideas.lead: 5-20 days: issuance and coupon data accumulate through the month, so the extension size is essentially known a week-plus before the last business day when the flow actually hits.
ideas.exclusivity: Moat is replicating the index rebalance rules to compute the extension DV01 and scaling by true passive-tracking AUM — most participants know 'month-end extension exists' but have not computed this month's precise size and direction. Explicitly different from the excluded month-end pension equity/bond rebalancing (that's driven by cross-asset return gaps; this is driven by Treasury issuance mechanics).
ideas.why_clears_costs: TY DV01 ≈ $70/contract per bp. A larger-extension month-end typically richens the relevant point 1-3 bps into the close = $70-210/contract vs ~$16-31 round-trip. UXY DV01 is ~$120+, scaling the capture. Fires 12x/year in the most liquid duration instruments.
ideas.lens: Flow/positioning/microstructure mechanics that force predictable, computable trades in liquid instruments

ideas.name: MSCI Inclusion-Factor Ladder
ideas.source: MSCI runs scheduled index reviews (quarterly/semiannual) and steps foreign-inclusion factors (e.g., China A-shares) up in pre-announced tranches. Adds/deletes and FIF changes are deterministic functions of published rules (size, liquidity, foreign-room screens) applied to observable market data — but MSCI announces the results only ~2 weeks before the effective date.
ideas.collection: Replicate MSCI's Global Investable Market methodology: pull float, ADV, foreign-ownership-room and size-segment data for the candidate universe, run the screens to predict adds/deletes and inclusion-factor steps, and estimate the passive AUM ($ tracking EM/ACWI) that must buy/sell each name on the effective date.
ideas.instrument: Liquid EM ADRs and the EEM/VWO ETFs; the largest adds (mega-cap Asian ADRs) are deeply liquid.
ideas.mechanism: Passive EM funds must trade the review changes price-insensitively on the effective close; predicted adds see billions of forced buying and drift up into the effective date. Position before MSCI's announcement, and again before the effective-date print.
ideas.lead: Weeks to months: the methodology is replicable continuously, giving a lead over MSCI's own ~2-week-ahead announcement and a much larger lead over the effective-date rebalance.
ideas.exclusivity: Moat is faithfully reproducing MSCI's screens and correctly handling edge cases (foreign-room caps, size-segment cutoffs, number-of-securities rules) plus sizing passive AUM per name — years of methodology tuning, not a licensed list. Distinct index family from the already-listed Russell reconstitution.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A predicted large add moves the ADR ~1-4% into the effective date as passive buys; on a $180 ADR that is $1.80-$7.20/share vs a $0.01 spread. EEM ($40) moves less but its penny spread and huge ADV clear costs on any 0.3%+ move. Recurs at every review across many names.
ideas.lens: Flow/positioning/microstructure mechanics that force predictable, computable trades in liquid instruments

ideas.name: Commodity Index January Reweight
ideas.source: The S&P GSCI and Bloomberg Commodity Index reweight annually (effective January), changing constituent weights based on world-production and liquidity data. The new weights are computable from the same public production/liquidity inputs the index committees use, and index funds (~$200B+ tracking) must rebalance to them.
ideas.collection: Ingest the world-production series (e.g., EIA/USGS/USDA) and exchange ADV/OI liquidity data that feed the index formulas, replicate GSCI/BCOM reweighting math to compute each commodity's target weight change, and translate into the forced buy/sell notional per front-month contract.
ideas.instrument: WTI/Brent crude, natural gas, gold, copper, corn, wheat, soybean futures — all deeply liquid.
ideas.mechanism: The January reweight is a scheduled, price-insensitive shift of index weights; commodities gaining weight see mechanical index buying and those losing weight see selling during the reweight window. Front-run the reweight flow computed from the source data. This is the annual reweighting, not the monthly front-month roll.
ideas.lead: Weeks to months: the production/liquidity inputs are available well before the index sponsors publish the new weights, and long before the January reweight executes.
ideas.exclusivity: Moat is replicating the exact reweighting formulas (world-production-weighting with liquidity constraints, dollar-weight caps, roll-adjustment) from raw production data before the funds trade — not buying the published target weights after release. Explicitly distinct from the excluded Goldman/GSCI monthly roll (this is the once-a-year weight change).
ideas.why_clears_costs: WTI tick = $0.01 = $10/contract (1,000 bbl); round-trip ~$15. Reweight flow moves front WTI ~0.5-1.5% over the window = $0.35-1.05 on $70 oil = $350-1,050/contract. Natgas/grains scale similarly. Edge exceeds cost by ~30-70x in the world's most liquid futures.
ideas.lens: Flow/positioning/microstructure mechanics that force predictable, computable trades in liquid instruments

ideas.name: Vanna-Charm OPEX Drift
ideas.source: Dealers' aggregate options book carries second-order Greeks — vanna (delta sensitivity to vol) and charm (delta decay with time) — that force mechanical hedging flows distinct from gamma. These are reconstructable from the full listed options surface (open interest, strikes, expiries) plus standard dealer-ownership assumptions.
ideas.collection: Reconstruct the dealer book across the entire SPX/SPY listed surface, compute net vanna and charm by strike/expiry, and model the deterministic hedging flow as implied vol drifts and calendar time decays into monthly OPEX — producing a projected supportive/negative drift path for the days before expiry.
ideas.instrument: E-mini S&P 500 futures (ES) and SPX/SPY options.
ideas.mechanism: In low-and-falling-vol regimes a large short-put-heavy dealer book generates positive charm/vanna hedging demand (dealers must buy the index as time passes and vol drifts down), producing a mechanical drift up into OPEX week; the sign flips when vol is rising. Trade the computed drift, not just the gamma pin.
ideas.lead: 3-10 sessions: the vanna/charm flow is a deterministic function of the current OI surface and the calendar, so the drift path into monthly OPEX is estimable a week-plus ahead.
ideas.exclusivity: Moat is the second-order Greek reconstruction with correct ownership/sign assumptions across thousands of strikes and expiries — materially harder than the gamma-only GEX estimate already on the excluded list, which ignores vanna and charm. The processing (surface reconstruction + regime-conditioned hedging model) is the edge.
ideas.why_clears_costs: ES tick = 0.25 = $12.50; round-trip ~$16. A modeled OPEX-week vanna/charm drift of 0.5-1.5% = 27-82 pts = $1,350-$4,100/contract. Clears costs ~100x; recurs monthly with ES depth to absorb size.
ideas.lens: Flow/positioning/microstructure mechanics that force predictable, computable trades in liquid instruments

ideas.name: Month-End FX Hedge-Rebalance Fix
ideas.source: Passive currency-hedged international equity/bond funds and pension FX overlays rebalance their FX forward hedges at month-end, executed around the 4pm London WM/Reuters fix. The required rebalance is a deterministic function of the month's cross-market equity return divergence (US vs international) and the funds' hedge ratios — both observable.
ideas.collection: Estimate the hedged-AUM base by currency (from ETF assets like HEDJ/DBEF/DXJ and disclosed pension hedge ratios), compute this month's US-vs-international equity return gap from index prints, and apply the rebalance rule to size the forced FX-forward flow hitting the month-end fix, with direction from which market outperformed.
ideas.instrument: EUR/USD (6E) and USD/JPY (6J) FX futures; deep spot FX.
ideas.mechanism: When international equities outperform, hedgers must sell more foreign currency forward at month-end (and buy back when they underperform), producing a directional, price-insensitive flow concentrated at the fix. Position ahead of the computed fix imbalance.
ideas.lead: 1-5 days: the month's return divergence is essentially locked by the penultimate session, so the direction and rough size of the month-end fix flow are known before the fix executes.
ideas.exclusivity: Moat is sizing the true hedged-AUM base per currency and calibrating the rebalance-response function (hedge ratios, rebalance thresholds, which pools rebalance monthly vs quarterly) — the raw return gap is public, the flow model is the work. Explicitly different from the excluded month-end pension equity/bond rebalancing: this isolates the FX-forward hedge leg at the WMR fix.
ideas.why_clears_costs: 6E tick = 0.00005 = $6.25/contract (€125k notional); round-trip ~$12. A meaningful month-end fix imbalance moves EUR/USD ~10-40 pips = $125-500/contract vs the sub-$15 cost. 6J similar. Fires 12x/year (plus quarter-ends larger) in the most liquid FX pairs; known-crowded, so edge is sized to months with large, one-sided return gaps.
ideas.lens: Flow/positioning/microstructure mechanics that force predictable, computable trades in liquid instruments

ideas.name: AdCom Briefing-Book Reader
ideas.source: FDA Advisory Committee briefing documents, which the agency posts to its meeting web pages roughly two U.S. business days before an oncology/CV/neuro advisory-committee panel votes on an approvable question. These packages include the FDA review division's OWN written assessment, whose hedging and tone systematically foreshadow the panel vote and the later PDUFA action.
ideas.collection: Poll each pending AdCom meeting page on a fixed schedule and pull the 100-300 page PDF the instant it drops at ~2pm ET. Run a per-division trained lexicon (ODAC vs CRDAC vs PCNS reviewers hedge differently) that scores efficacy-acceptance, safety-concern, benefit-risk, and 'voting-question framing' language into a single directional score, plus extraction of the FDA's own posed voting questions (a hostile question framing is itself predictive).
ideas.instrument: Single-name biotech/pharma equity and its listed options straddles/verticals (e.g., mid-cap names with a scheduled ODAC), and sector proxies (XBI) for basket hedging.
ideas.mechanism: The FDA reviewer memo leaks the agency's stance before the human crowd digests a dense 300-page packet and before the panel actually votes; the machine-read directional score front-runs both the panel vote and the eventual approval/CRL.
ideas.lead: The briefing book is public ~48 hours before the vote and weeks before the PDUFA action date; the scored read is available minutes after the 2pm drop while sell-side and retail take a day-plus to parse it.
ideas.exclusivity: Raw docs are public, but the moat is a division-specific regulatory-tone lexicon calibrated over many past AdCom cycles against realized vote/PDUFA outcomes, plus the pipeline to parse and score a huge PDF the instant it posts. A rival must rebuild and back-test the lexicon over years of meetings, not license a finished feed.
ideas.why_clears_costs: AdCom-stage biotechs routinely move 30-70% on the panel/PDUFA binary; the briefing-doc drop itself moves the stock 10-40%. On a $40 name that is $4-16/share against a 1-cent tick and a 2-5 cent spread. On options, ATM straddles price a ~50% implied move; a 15-point directional edge dwarfs even a $0.10 option spread.
ideas.lens: Regulatory/scientific calendars and databases that lead a binary catalyst in a liquid single name or sector

ideas.name: FAERS Signal Front-Run
ideas.source: The FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) quarterly public dashboard/data files of drug adverse-event reports. The regulatory binary catalyst is a black-box warning, REMS, Dear-Doctor letter, or market withdrawal that the FDA imposes on a specific marketed drug AFTER a safety signal crosses threshold.
ideas.collection: Ingest the raw FAERS quarterly files, deduplicate the notoriously dirty reports (same event filed by patient, physician, and manufacturer), normalize free-text drug names to RxNorm, and compute disproportionality statistics (PRR, ROR, and Bayesian EBGM/MGPS) per drug-event pair with denominator adjustment. Flag drugs where a serious-event signal is accelerating past the FDA's own action thresholds.
ideas.instrument: Liquid pharma single names carrying the flagged drug as a material revenue line, plus their options (large-cap specialty/branded pharma with penny spreads).
ideas.mechanism: A safety signal that will force a label change or withdrawal is statistically detectable in the accumulating report stream quarters before the FDA acts; you position ahead of the label/withdrawal catalyst that re-rates the franchise.
ideas.lead: FAERS data lags one quarter, but the FDA typically acts one to four quarters AFTER a disproportionality signal is first detectable; the clean-signal read leads the DailyMed label change and any Dear-Doctor letter by months.
ideas.exclusivity: Anyone can download FAERS; almost no one cleans it correctly. The moat is the deduplication + drug-name normalization + proper Bayesian disproportionality pipeline validated against historical label actions. Buying the raw file is worthless; the from-scratch pharmacovigilance engine is the edge.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A black-box warning or withdrawal knocks 10-30% off a name whose flagged drug is material. On a $100 large-cap that is $10-30/share against a 1-cent tick and a 1-3 cent spread; even a $0.05-spread mid-cap clears with a wide margin.
ideas.lens: Regulatory/scientific calendars and databases that lead a binary catalyst in a liquid single name or sector

ideas.name: Star-Ratings Reconstructor
ideas.source: CMS Medicare Advantage & Part D Star Ratings, released each October, which set the Quality Bonus Payments that drive managed-care margins. The underlying ~40 component measures (CAHPS, HEDIS, HOS, Part D pharmacy, administrative) become knowable from published measure data and plan reporting well before CMS publishes the composite star per contract.
ideas.collection: Assemble the component-measure inputs per contract, then model CMS's exact composite methodology: measure weights, the Tukey-outlier-deletion cut-point rules, reward-factor/guardrail logic, and the improvement measures. Output a projected star per major contract and roll up to each insurer's bonus-eligible membership.
ideas.instrument: Managed-care large caps and their options: HUM, UNH, CVS, ELV, CI — deep, penny-wide options markets.
ideas.mechanism: A contract slipping below 4.0 stars (or recovering above it) is a large, mechanical EPS swing the market prices only on the October release; reconstructing the composite ahead lets you position before the print.
ideas.lead: Component measure and plan-performance data is available weeks to months before the October star release; the reconstructed composite leads CMS's publication and the sell-side's model update.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is a multi-year build that faithfully replicates CMS's Tukey cut-point and guardrail methodology and maps measures to bonus-eligible membership, calibrated against prior-year realized ratings. The measure files are public; the correct composite-and-dollars model is the unglamorous work.
ideas.why_clears_costs: When Humana slipped below 4 stars on a major contract (Oct 2023) the stock fell ~19% in a day, roughly a $50 move on a ~$260 share. Even a single-contract surprise is multiple dollars per share against a 1-cent tick and ~1-2 cent spread on HUM/UNH.
ideas.lens: Regulatory/scientific calendars and databases that lead a binary catalyst in a liquid single name or sector

ideas.name: NCD Coverage Clock
ideas.source: CMS National Coverage Determination dockets on cms.gov: the tracking sheet, proposed decision memo, public-comment window, and statutorily-timed final decision. A national Medicare coverage grant or denial is a binary revenue catalyst for a diagnostic or drug.
ideas.collection: Scrape the NCD tracking sheet and docket for each open analysis; model the statutory clock (proposed decision memo, then 30-day comment, then final within the fixed window) and parse the proposed memo's coverage language (full vs Coverage-with-Evidence-Development vs non-coverage), then map the HCPCS/coding impact to the affected company's revenue line.
ideas.instrument: Liquid single names with Medicare-dependent revenue: EXAS (diagnostics), LLY/BIIB (Alzheimer therapeutics), plus device large caps; all with liquid options.
ideas.mechanism: The proposed decision memo is a near-deterministic tell of the final decision and lands ~90 days ahead of it; positioning off the proposed memo (and the docket cadence that precedes it) front-runs the market-moving final coverage catalyst.
ideas.lead: Docket filings lead the proposed memo, and the proposed memo leads the final decision by roughly 90 days; the crowd typically trades the final headline.
ideas.exclusivity: The docket is public, but the moat is entity-resolution of an analysis to a specific company's coded revenue and a coverage-language model that reads CED nuance correctly. The read-through from a coverage-with-evidence caveat to actual reimbursed volume is the work, not a licensable number.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A national coverage grant/denial moves a diagnostic name 10-25%; on a $60 stock that is $6-15/share. Alzheimer-coverage decisions moved billions of market cap on LLY/BIIB — dollars per share on penny-spread large caps against a 1-cent tick.
ideas.lens: Regulatory/scientific calendars and databases that lead a binary catalyst in a liquid single name or sector

ideas.name: Embargo-Lift Abstract Scanner
ideas.source: Major medical-congress abstract databases (ASCO, ESMO, ASH, AHA, ACC): titles are released roughly a week ahead, and full abstracts are posted at a precise embargo-lift time (often the evening before or days before the oral presentation). The abstract IS the pivotal efficacy/safety data readout — the binary catalyst.
ideas.collection: Pre-register access to the embargoed abstract portal, hit the endpoint the instant the embargo lifts, and NLP-score each relevant abstract for magnitude of effect (ORR, PFS/OS hazard ratios, p-values) and safety flags across tumor types, mapped to the sponsoring public company. Also mine the pre-released title/late-breaker list for which programs are reporting.
ideas.instrument: Oncology/cardio biotech single names and their options; sector proxy XBI/IBB for basket exposure.
ideas.mechanism: Trial data drives 20-60% biotech moves; the abstract text carries the numbers hours-to-days before the podium presentation and the company press release, and before humans digest a dense abstract book.
ideas.lead: Title release leads by ~a week; the full-abstract embargo lift leads the presentation by hours to days; the scored read is available seconds after the lift while humans skim.
ideas.exclusivity: The abstract portal is access-gated (member/press), and the moat is the scoring model that reads hazard ratios and safety across indications plus the infrastructure to hit the embargo endpoint at the lift instant. A rival needs both the credentialed access pipeline and a calibrated efficacy-scoring engine.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A positive/negative oncology readout moves a mid-cap biotech 20-60%; on a $30 name that is $6-18/share against a 1-cent tick and 3-5 cent spread. Options straddles pricing a ~40% move are dwarfed by capturing the direction hours early.
ideas.lens: Regulatory/scientific calendars and databases that lead a binary catalyst in a liquid single name or sector

ideas.name: CHMP Agenda Decoder
ideas.source: The EMA's Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) monthly meeting: the agenda is published shortly before the meeting and the positive/negative opinions land in the post-meeting highlights, days before company press releases. A CHMP opinion is a binary EU-approval catalyst that also reads through to global sentiment.
ideas.collection: Scrape the CHMP agenda and map its internal product codes/molecule identifiers to specific companies and assets; at meeting close, parse the 'highlights' bulletin's opinion language (positive opinion, negative, re-examination, withdrawal) and match it to the mapped assets before the sponsor issues its own release.
ideas.instrument: Liquid EU/US pharma: large-cap ADRs (NVS, AZN, GSK, SNY) with penny-ish spreads, and mid-cap EU biotech single names with a specific asset up for opinion.
ideas.mechanism: The opinion is decided at the monthly meeting and surfaced in the EMA highlights before the company's own PR; the crowd trades the company headline, so parsing the EMA bulletin gives a same-session lead.
ideas.lead: The agenda leads the meeting by days (telling you which assets are decided this cycle); the highlights bulletin leads the sponsor press release by minutes-to-hours.
ideas.exclusivity: The agenda uses coded product identifiers; the moat is the mapping of those codes to public-company molecules plus a language model on the highlights. The bulletins are public but the resolve-and-score layer is the build.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A CHMP opinion moves a mid-cap EU biotech 20-40% and a large-cap 3-10%. On an €80 ADR that is €2.40-8/share against a 1-3 cent spread; on a mid-cap single-asset name it is multiples more, clearing the tick with room.
ideas.lens: Regulatory/scientific calendars and databases that lead a binary catalyst in a liquid single name or sector

ideas.name: FERC eLibrary Certificate Clock
ideas.source: FERC's eLibrary docket system for interstate gas pipeline and LNG certificate proceedings and rate cases: filings, environmental documents (draft/final EIS), comment-close notices, and orders. A FERC certificate or order is a binary go/no-go catalyst for a specific midstream project.
ideas.collection: Poll eLibrary per open docket, resolve each docket to its project and the parent public company, and model the Natural Gas Act / NEPA clock: a final EIS issuance and comment-close date bound when the order can issue, and the sequence of filings telegraphs staff posture. Parse order-precursor documents for approval/deficiency signals.
ideas.instrument: Midstream large/mid caps and options: WMB, KMI, ET, and project-concentrated names (e.g., a pipeline pure-play), plus AMLP for basket hedging.
ideas.mechanism: The docket sequence and statutory clock reveal when a certificate order will issue weeks ahead; positioning off the final EIS and comment-close leads the order headline that re-rates a project-heavy name.
ideas.lead: Final EIS issuance and comment-close dates lead the certificate order by weeks; docket filings lead those milestones further.
ideas.exclusivity: eLibrary is a clunky, poorly-indexed document store; the moat is entity-resolution (docket to project to public company) and a calibrated NGA/NEPA timeline model. The documents are free; converting them into an order-timing/probability estimate is the years-long work.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A pipeline certificate approval has moved project-concentrated names 10-30% (e.g., Equitrans on Mountain Valley milestones). On a $10-40 stock that is $1-12/share against a 1-cent tick and 2-4 cent spread.
ideas.lens: Regulatory/scientific calendars and databases that lead a binary catalyst in a liquid single name or sector

ideas.name: H.2 Bank-Merger Handicapper
ideas.source: The Federal Reserve's H.2 weekly release of bank-holding-company applications and actions, plus the FDIC/OCC application pipelines and public CRA-protest and comment filings. Regulatory approval is the binary catalyst that closes a bank merger and collapses the arb spread.
ideas.collection: Track each pending bank deal through the H.2 application-accepted date, the statutory comment period, CRA protests, and required branch divestitures; build an approval-probability-and-timeline model per deal (including DOJ competitive review) that beats the arb crowd's implied odds. Flag stalling signals (protest volume, extended comment periods, second-request-equivalents).
ideas.instrument: Regional-bank merger pairs (target + acquirer) as a merger-arb spread, both liquid mid/large-cap banks with penny-wide markets.
ideas.mechanism: Approval timing and probability are the compensation embedded in the arb spread; reading the H.2/CRA pipeline better than the marginal holder lets you buy underpriced completions and avoid the breaks.
ideas.lead: The application pipeline and protest cadence make the Fed's approval timing modelable weeks ahead of the decision the market waits for.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is a cross-agency (Fed/FDIC/OCC/DOJ) approval-probability model with CRA-protest and divestiture inputs, calibrated on decades of bank-deal outcomes — superior odds-estimation, not a licensable dataset. Diversifying across many pending deals absorbs single-break risk.
ideas.why_clears_costs: Regional bank-merger arb spreads run 3-8%; on a $30 target that is $0.90-2.40/share. Correctly re-rating completion probability or pull-forward timing captures a large fraction against a 1-2 cent spread on liquid regionals.
ideas.lens: Regulatory/scientific calendars and databases that lead a binary catalyst in a liquid single name or sector

ideas.name: Pesticide Docket Kill-Switch
ideas.source: EPA pesticide registration-review and re-registration dockets on regulations.gov: proposed interim decisions (PIDs), risk assessments, and final decisions that can cancel, restrict, or re-approve an active ingredient. A cancellation or favorable re-registration is a binary catalyst for the registrant's franchise.
ideas.collection: Scrape each open registration-review docket, resolve the active ingredient to its registrant(s) and their public parent and product-line revenue, and model the PID-to-final clock; parse the risk-assessment language (ecological/human-health findings) for cancellation vs restriction vs clean re-approval signals.
ideas.instrument: Ag-chem single names and options: CTVA, FMC, NTR, BAYRY (and Nutrien/Mosaic for read-through); liquid large caps with penny-ish spreads.
ideas.mechanism: The proposed interim decision signals the final direction and leads it by months; a cancellation removes a product's revenue outright, a binary the market prices on the final headline.
ideas.lead: The PID leads the final decision by months and telegraphs direction; docket risk-assessment filings lead the PID.
ideas.exclusivity: The docket is public, but the moat is entity-resolution of active-ingredient to registrant to revenue line plus a risk-assessment language model that distinguishes cancellation from label-restriction. Converting a scientific docket into a per-share revenue-at-risk number is the work.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A single high-volume active-ingredient cancellation moves a diversified name 3-8% (CTVA ~$1.80-4.80/share on a $60 stock) and a concentrated name (FMC) meaningfully more, against a 1-cent tick and 1-2 cent spread.
ideas.lens: Regulatory/scientific calendars and databases that lead a binary catalyst in a liquid single name or sector

ideas.name: PMTA Order Docket Tracker
ideas.source: FDA Center for Tobacco Products premarket tobacco application (PMTA) actions: marketing-granted orders (MGOs) and marketing-denial orders (MDOs) tracked via CTP's decision listings, technical-project-lead (TPL) review status, deficiency letters, and the active federal-court dockets litigating specific product and menthol decisions. Each order is a binary product go/no-go.
ideas.collection: Map PMTA submission numbers to specific products and their public-company owners; track TPL/deficiency status and monitor the appellate/district-court dockets (many MDOs are litigated) for stay grants and ruling calendars that gate when an order takes effect. Score the docket toward grant vs denial.
ideas.instrument: Tobacco/vape single names and options: MO, PM, BTI ADR, and vape-exposed names (e.g., Turning Point Brands); liquid large caps with penny-to-few-cent spreads.
ideas.mechanism: An MDO on a key product or a favorable menthol/next-gen decision is a franchise-level catalyst; the docket and litigation calendar reveal the timing and likely direction before the order headline hits.
ideas.lead: TPL/deficiency status and court-docket ruling calendars telegraph the order by weeks ahead of the FDA announcement or court decision the market trades.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is mapping opaque PMTA submission numbers to products and companies and fusing CTP status with the litigation docket into an order-timing/probability read. Public pieces, but the resolve-and-score layer is the build.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A key-product denial or a favorable menthol decision moves MO/BTI 3-10% — $1.50-5/share on a $50 stock against a 1-cent tick and 1-2 cent spread; vape pure-plays move far more, clearing costs decisively.
ideas.lens: Regulatory/scientific calendars and databases that lead a binary catalyst in a liquid single name or sector

ideas.name: Catalog-Multiple Ticker
ideas.source: Completed secondary music-royalty auctions on Royalty Exchange, SongVest, ANote Music, plus Duetti/Concord tender data. Each listing discloses last-12-month royalty income alongside the clearing bid, i.e. a freely-set implied price-to-annual-royalty multiple for catalog rights.
ideas.collection: Scrape every closed auction's hammer price, disclosed LTM/DVM royalty income, genre, vintage, and rights type (writer's share vs master vs neighboring rights). Deduplicate re-listings, then normalize into a rolling, genre- and vintage-weighted catalog-multiple index.
ideas.instrument: Warner Music Group (WMG) and Universal Music Group (UMG.AS) common + options; Reservoir Media (RSVR).
ideas.mechanism: The auction market reprices catalog acquisition multiples continuously; the majors' balance-sheet catalog values and sell-side SOTP comps only update at quarterly impairment/valuation dates. When market multiples compress (rate/AI-licensing fear) or expand, WMG/UMG equity re-rates at the next print or analyst comp refresh.
ideas.lead: Weeks to a full quarter ahead of impairment tests, catalog-M&A comp refreshes, and the read-through into guidance.
ideas.exclusivity: Auctions are public but messy: heterogeneous royalty-accounting disclosures, ambiguous rights types, survivorship in re-listings. Building a clean, mix-normalized multiple index is years of taxonomy and entity-resolution work; no one licenses a 'catalog multiple index.' The moat is the reconciliation, not the data's existence.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A 1-2x turn in the market catalog multiple shifts WMG's SOTP by roughly $3-6 on a ~$35 stock. WMG trades a 1c tick with a ~2-4c spread and dollar-deep penny options, so a multi-dollar re-rate exceeds costs by two-plus orders of magnitude.

ideas.name: Wholesale Lane Nowcast
ideas.source: Per-vehicle hammer prices from OPENLANE/ADESA digital lanes, ACV Auctions, and Manheim/Copart non-salvage dealer lanes — the daily freely-clearing wholesale used-car market that sets residual values.
ideas.collection: Ingest per-lot VIN, mileage, condition grade, and sale price; VIN-decode and mix-adjust into a daily, seasonally-adjusted wholesale price index by segment, published ahead of Manheim's mid-month/monthly MUVVI release.
ideas.instrument: Carvana (CVNA), CarMax (KMX), Ally Financial (ALLY), AutoNation (AN) — all liquid with deep options.
ideas.mechanism: Wholesale acquisition cost and residual values are the dominant swing in used-vehicle gross-profit-per-unit and in auto-lender residual/loss marks. The lane market clears daily; retailers report monthly/quarterly and even Manheim lags ~2 weeks, so a rising/falling daily index foretells GPU and residual surprises.
ideas.lead: Days to two weeks ahead of Manheim; a full quarter ahead of CVNA/KMX GPU and ALLY residual disclosures.
ideas.exclusivity: Same DNA as parking-lot computer vision: the moat is the mix-adjustment engine over noisy per-lot data (VIN decode, condition normalization, lane-mix weighting). The raw lots are scattered across platforms; the clean daily index nobody else computes.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A $500 swing in wholesale price per unit maps to ~$300-400 GPU delta, which has moved CVNA several dollars on a ~$200+ stock (1c tick, ~5-10c spread). The earnings-window dollar move dwarfs costs and fires every reporting cycle.
ideas.lens: Cross-market/parallel-market pricing gaps where a freely-clearing market leads the primary security

ideas.name: NdPr Shadow Price
ideas.source: Chinese domestic and FOB-China neodymium-praseodymium oxide/metal daily quotes from Asian Metal, Shanghai Metals Market (SMM), and the Baotou Rare Earth Exchange — the only freely-clearing global reference for magnet rare earths, quoted in Chinese-language feeds.
ideas.collection: Scrape daily Chinese-domestic and export NdPr oxide/metal quotes plus Dy/Tb, translate and reconcile the divergent quote sources, and construct a magnet-basket netback specific to each Western miner's product mix.
ideas.instrument: MP Materials (MP) and Lynas (LYC.AX) — both liquid with options; USA Rare Earth (USAR).
ideas.mechanism: MP/Lynas revenue is priced almost entirely off NdPr, and there is no trustworthy Western reference, so the Chinese domestic market is the price-setter. It moves daily while MP reports realized prices quarterly and US holders underweight the Chinese-language prints, so equity lags the shadow price.
ideas.lead: Days-to-weeks vs US-investor attention; a full quarter vs MP's realized-price disclosure.
ideas.exclusivity: No official Western NdPr index exists (measure what has no trustworthy number). The moat is sourcing, translating, and reconciling opaque, sometimes-conflicting Chinese quotes and mapping to each miner's exact basket — a multilingual data-ops build, not a license.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A 10% NdPr move (~$6-7/kg) has repeatedly moved MP $1-3 on a ~$15-30 stock (1c tick, ~2-3c spread, deep options). The move clears costs by two-plus orders of magnitude.
ideas.lens: Cross-market/parallel-market pricing gaps where a freely-clearing market leads the primary security

ideas.name: Guangzhou Night Tape
ideas.source: Guangzhou Futures Exchange (GFEX) lithium carbonate futures — a genuinely freely-clearing forward market with an evening session — plus SMM Chinese spot lithium carbonate/hydroxide quotes.
ideas.collection: Pull GFEX front- and second-month settlement and intraday prints each session, including the ~21:00-23:00 CST night session that closes before the US open, plus daily SMM spot; map to each Western producer's contract/hedge mix and carbonate-vs-hydroxide split.
ideas.instrument: Albemarle (ALB) and SQM (NYSE) — very liquid with deep options; Pilbara (PLS.AX), Arcadium/Rio.
ideas.mechanism: Chinese lithium futures are the global price-discovery venue; they trade and gap during Asian hours before US lithium equities open, and lead sell-side realized-price estimates by weeks. US holders underweight the Guangzhou session, so ALB/SQM open partly stale to the overnight lithium move.
ideas.lead: The overnight GFEX/SMM move leads the US equity open by hours; weeks ahead of realized-price estimate refreshes.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is real-time ingestion of the Chinese-language GFEX/SMM feed and mapping to each producer's specific contract structure and spodumene-to-carbonate conversion economics — an ops-plus-modeling build a US-only desk cannot replicate overnight.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A 5% overnight lithium move maps to a ~$1-3 gap in ALB (a ~$70-90 stock, 1c tick, ~3-5c spread, penny options). Trading the US open against the settled overnight tape clears costs comfortably and fires nearly every session.
ideas.lens: Cross-market/parallel-market pricing gaps where a freely-clearing market leads the primary security

ideas.name: Get-In Premium Panel
ideas.source: Real-time secondary 'get-in' (cheapest-available) prices and active-listing counts on StubHub, SeatGeek, Vivid Seats, and Viagogo for every tour date and major sporting event — the freely-clearing resale market for live-event demand.
ideas.collection: Poll each event's get-in price, listing depth, and (where visible) face price across the tour; build a resale-premium index (resale/face) and sell-through velocity per artist/venue, mix-normalized by market size.
ideas.instrument: Live Nation (LYV) common + options; Liberty Formula One (FWONK); MSG Entertainment/Sphere, Atlanta Braves (BATRA), MSG Sports (MSGS).
ideas.mechanism: The resale market reveals true demand and the pricing power LYV monetizes via platinum/dynamic pricing and on-site spend. It forms continuously across a tour and is essentially complete before LYV's quarterly Concerts/ticketing AOI print, which the market still models off stale attendance assumptions.
ideas.lead: Weeks-to-a-quarter ahead of LYV's segment prints; days ahead of an individual mega-tour on-sale read.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is the matched face-vs-resale panel and mix normalization across thousands of venues/artists: entity resolution (which listing maps to which LYV-promoted show), face-price back-fill, and bot-listing filtering. A finished 'resale premium index' is not for sale.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A 10-point swing in the resale-premium index has mapped to concert-AOI surprises that move LYV $3-8 on a ~$90-150 stock (1c tick, ~3-6c spread, deep options); dollars-per-share vastly exceed costs.
ideas.lens: Cross-market/parallel-market pricing gaps where a freely-clearing market leads the primary security

ideas.name: Barge-and-Tampa Netback
ideas.source: Freely-clearing wholesale fertilizer benchmarks — NOLA urea/UAN barge trades, the Tampa ammonia monthly settlement, and Corn Belt potash/DAP — captured from Green Markets, Profercy, Argus, and daily barge-trade chatter.
ideas.collection: Assemble daily/weekly NOLA barge clears and the Tampa ammonia settlement, freight-adjust to each producer's plant gate, weight by product mix, and compute a per-producer realized-price netback index.
ideas.instrument: CF Industries (CF), Nutrien (NTR), Mosaic (MOS), Yara (YAR.OL) — all liquid with options.
ideas.mechanism: Producer earnings are near-pure price times volume on these benchmarks. The wholesale market moves weekly (NOLA barge intra-week) while equities' realized prices print quarterly and sell-side lags; US holders underweight barge/Tampa microstructure.
ideas.lead: Weeks-to-a-quarter ahead of realized-price disclosures and estimate refreshes.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is the clean, freight- and mix-adjusted netback per producer built from fragmented trade-press and barge data — the raw benchmarks are scattered and inconsistently defined; the reconciled per-name netback index nobody licenses. This is the fertilizer output-price benchmark, distinct from input-cost gas tripwires.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A $50/ton nitrogen move swings CF annualized EPS materially and has moved CF $3-6 on an ~$80-100 stock (1c tick, ~3-5c spread, deep options); the print-window move is far above costs.
ideas.lens: Cross-market/parallel-market pricing gaps where a freely-clearing market leads the primary security

ideas.name: Pre-IPO Mark Arbitrage
ideas.source: Freely-clearing private-company secondary transactions and tender clears from Caplight, Forge Global, Nasdaq Private Market, EquityZen, and Hiive — bid/ask and completed-trade marks for late-stage names (SpaceX, Stripe, Databricks, Anthropic, OpenAI).
ideas.collection: Aggregate completed secondary trade prices, tender clearing prices, and derived bid/ask by name; weight by the disclosed holdings of public vehicles to compute a live implied-NAV for each vehicle.
ideas.instrument: Destiny Tech100 (DXYZ) common + options; publicly-traded interval funds/BDCs that fair-value late-stage private tech.
ideas.mechanism: DXYZ holds the private names but marks NAV quarterly with stale, board-blessed valuations; the secondary market clears the same underlying continuously. A jump/drop in secondary marks for a top holding (e.g., SpaceX) foretells the next NAV mark and the vehicle's re-rate.
ideas.lead: Up to a full quarter — NAV marks lag secondary clears badly.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is assembling a reliable, deduplicated secondary-price panel (thin, noisy, conflicting, access-gated broker quotes) and mapping it precisely to each vehicle's disclosed weights — an entity-resolution and valuation build, not a purchasable dataset.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A 20% secondary re-mark of DXYZ's top holdings shifts implied NAV several dollars on a ~$25-50 vehicle (1c tick; wider ~10-20c spread but dollar-scale mark-to-clear gaps clear it comfortably).
ideas.lens: Cross-market/parallel-market pricing gaps where a freely-clearing market leads the primary security

ideas.name: Resale Heat Index
ideas.source: Freely-clearing sneaker/streetwear resale on StockX, GOAT, and eBay — SKU-level last-sale prices, bid/ask, and sales volume that price real-time brand demand.
ideas.collection: Scrape SKU-level resale price-to-retail premium and sell-through velocity; map every SKU to its brand and franchise, mix-normalize hype-SKU vs volume-SKU, and build a per-brand demand-heat index.
ideas.instrument: Nike (NKE), Deckers/HOKA (DECK), On Holding (ONON), Crocs (CROX), adidas (ADS.DE) — NKE/DECK very liquid with deep options.
ideas.mechanism: Resale premium is a direct, freely-set read on consumer demand and brand pricing power that leads the brand's DTC/wholesale sell-through reported quarterly; sell-side 'brand heat' reads form slowly off channel checks while the resale market clears every second.
ideas.lead: Weeks-to-a-quarter ahead of brand revenue/gross-margin prints and analyst brand-heat re-rates.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is SKU-to-brand-to-franchise entity resolution and hype-vs-volume normalization over millions of listings — a launch SKU spiking is noise, a broad premium fade is signal. A heavy CV/NLP-plus-taxonomy build, not a purchasable dataset. Distinct from LEGO/luxury-daigou resale.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A sustained brand-heat inflection has moved NKE $2-5 on a ~$70-100 stock (1c tick, ~2-4c spread, deep penny options); dollars-per-share far exceed costs and the signal fires across many brands each cycle.
ideas.lens: Cross-market/parallel-market pricing gaps where a freely-clearing market leads the primary security

ideas.name: Lease-Rate-Factor Mark
ideas.source: The freely-negotiated commercial-aircraft lease and secondary-sale market — lease-rate factors, appraised current market values, and part-out/secondary sale prices by type from Ishka, Cirium/Ascend, and IBA.
ideas.collection: Track lease-rate factors and secondary transaction/appraisal values by aircraft type and vintage (A320neo, 737 MAX, 787, widebody), and map to each lessor's exact fleet composition and lease-expiry schedule.
ideas.instrument: AerCap (AER) and Air Lease (AL) — AER large-cap, liquid with options.
ideas.mechanism: Lessor equity value equals fleet market value plus embedded lease margins. The lease/secondary market reprices aircraft values continuously (post-shock: engine AOGs, MAX issues, China demand swings) while lessors mark book value quarterly and impair slowly, so equity book-value re-rates lag the parallel market.
ideas.lead: A quarter-plus — book marks and impairments trail the transaction market badly.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is assembling type-level lease-rate/secondary-value data (fragmented, appraisal-gated) and mapping it to AER's specific fleet and lease-expiry ladder — a fleet-accounting modeling build; there is no off-the-shelf AER mark-to-market feed. Distinct from private-jet ADS-B trackers.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A 5% shift in current market values across AER's fleet moves NAV several dollars on a ~$90-110 stock (1c tick, ~4-8c spread, options available); the re-rate dwarfs transaction costs.
ideas.lens: Cross-market/parallel-market pricing gaps where a freely-clearing market leads the primary security

ideas.name: Rate-on-Line Precursor
ideas.source: The freely-clearing catastrophe-bond/ILS market — primary issuance spreads, weekly secondary dealer marks (Aon Securities, Swiss Re, GC Securities indices), and daily UCITS ILS-fund NAVs that reprice reinsurance risk and post-event losses.
ideas.collection: Track cat-bond primary spreads and secondary marks by peril/region and ILS-fund NAV moves; after events, map bond-specific attachment losses and the forward rate-on-line to each reinsurer's peak-peril exposure and renewal calendar.
ideas.instrument: RenaissanceRe (RNR), Everest Group (EG), Arch Capital (ACGL) — liquid with options.
ideas.mechanism: The ILS market prices reinsurance risk transfer in the capital markets and reprices it within days of a catastrophe (bond-specific triggers, freely marked) and ahead of Jan-1/mid-year renewals. The hardening/softening of rate-on-line telegraphs reinsurer pricing power weeks before it shows in equity earnings/guidance, which trade on rougher loss guesses.
ideas.lead: Days for precise loss-to-layer reads; weeks-to-a-quarter for the rate-on-line trajectory into renewals.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is mapping the ILS market's peril-specific spreads and loss marks to each reinsurer's exact exposure and renewal book (attachment overlap, retro cover) — a specialist actuarial-mapping build over gated dealer runs, not a license. Distinct from SERFF rate filings or D&O premium tapes.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A meaningful rate-on-line inflection has moved RNR $5-12 on a ~$200-260 stock (1c tick, ~5-15c spread, options); the multi-dollar re-rate clears costs by a wide margin.
ideas.lens: Cross-market/parallel-market pricing gaps where a freely-clearing market leads the primary security

ideas.name: Kiln Glow Index
ideas.source: Thermal-infrared satellite radiance over the world's ~150 largest rotary cement kilns. The kiln shell and clinker cooler run a characteristic 1,400-2,000C hotspot; run-hours and hotspot intensity track clinker (and thus cement) throughput continuously.
ideas.collection: Ingest Landsat-8/9 TIRS (100m thermal), ASTER, and Sentinel-3 SLSTR fire channels over a hand-built registry of kiln coordinates; run thermal-unmixing to convert sub-pixel hotspot radiance into kiln on/off state and relative burn intensity; calibrate against nameplate capacity and historical reported volumes to output tons of clinker per plant per month, aggregated to each public producer's asset footprint.
ideas.instrument: US aggregates/cement large-caps and their options: Vulcan Materials (VMC), Martin Marietta (MLM), Eagle Materials (EXP), CRH plc (CRH), Cemex (CX).
ideas.mechanism: Quarterly cement/aggregate volume is a scheduled disclosure; kiln burn-hours accumulate through the quarter and are essentially complete before the print, while consensus prices off lagged government construction spend and last-quarter guidance. The kiln-hours ARE the reported tonnage proxy, not merely correlated with it.
ideas.lead: 3-8 weeks ahead of quarterly volume disclosure; also leads the monthly USGS/PCA cement shipment tallies by days.
ideas.exclusivity: Years to build the kiln coordinate registry, the sub-pixel thermal-unmixing pipeline (cloud, sun-glint, cooler-vs-kiln separation), and the radiance-to-tonnage calibration per plant. Raw imagery is cheap; the per-producer clinker number is not licensable anywhere.
ideas.why_clears_costs: VMC ~$270 with a 1-cent tick and a typical 2-5 cent spread; a few-percent volume surprise historically moves it 4-8% ($11-22/share) on print. Capturing even $2-4/share of pre-print drift dwarfs a ~3-cent round-trip; VMC weekly options clear costs trivially on a multi-dollar move.
ideas.lens: Physical-world telemetry (grid, logistics, industrial) that leads a commodity or a liquid equity

ideas.name: Brine Bloom
ideas.source: Multispectral satellite imagery of lithium brine evaporation ponds in the Lithium Triangle (Atacama, Olaroz, Hombre Muerto) and China's Qinghai. Pond surface area and color/turbidity shift as brine concentrates from dilute blue-green to Li-rich yellow-green, telegraphing production stage and volume 12-18 months ahead because of the evaporation cycle.
ideas.collection: Sentinel-2 (10m, 5-day revisit) and PlanetScope over a registry of every pond cell; segment pond boundaries, extract per-cell spectral indices, and map the color-progression sequence to kilograms of lithium carbonate equivalent reaching the plant, calibrated to each operator's reported output. Current pond fill physically predetermines future production.
ideas.instrument: Albemarle (ALB), SQM (SQM), Pilbara Minerals (PLS.AX), and the Global X Lithium ETF (LIT) - all deep-options large-caps.
ideas.mechanism: Producers report quarterly volumes and give annual production guidance; pond-stage inventory is a physical leading indicator the market cannot see, and front-runs price-reporting-agency lithium spot assessments. Guidance revisions are the catalyst.
ideas.lead: Because evaporation takes 12-18 months, production is visible 2-4 quarters ahead of the print.
ideas.exclusivity: The spectral-to-LCE calibration differs by basin (brine chemistry varies per salar) and the pond-stage registry take years plus ground-truth relationships to build. No vendor sells the finished per-salar output number.
ideas.why_clears_costs: ALB ~$95, 1-cent tick, ~3-8 cent spread; a production/guidance surprise moves it 6-12% ($6-11/share). LIT ~$45 moves 3-5% on a lithium-supply repricing. Capturing even $1.50-3/share pre-drift clears a sub-10-cent round trip many times over.
ideas.lens: Physical-world telemetry (grid, logistics, industrial) that leads a commodity or a liquid equity

ideas.name: Shop-Visit Clock
ideas.source: ADS-B flight tracking of the entire commercial fleet resolved to specific engine type. Aftermarket spare-parts and MRO revenue - the profit engine for GE Aerospace, RTX/Pratt, Honeywell, TransDigm - is driven by cumulative engine flight-hours and cycles that trigger scheduled shop visits and life-limited-part replacements.
ideas.collection: Ingest global ADS-B (multiple terrestrial plus satellite feeds), resolve each tail number to airframe and specific engine model via a maintained fleet registry, accumulate flight-hours/cycles per engine family, and apply published shop-visit interval and LLP curves to nowcast aftermarket demand and each OEM's spares/MRO revenue.
ideas.instrument: GE Aerospace (GE), RTX (RTX), Honeywell (HON), TransDigm (TDG), Safran (SAF.PA) - mega-caps with liquid options.
ideas.mechanism: Aftermarket revenue is the swing factor in these names' quarterly beats; flight-hours accumulate continuously and are complete before the print, while sell-side models off stale traffic data and airline commentary.
ideas.lead: Flight-hours are known in real time; the aftermarket revenue they imply prints 3-9 weeks later. Also leads recovery-narrative repricings after traffic disruptions.
ideas.exclusivity: Tail-to-engine resolution fused across feeds, plus a proprietary shop-visit interval library (which parts, which intervals, which margins per engine family), is a multi-year build. The raw ADS-B is public; the engine-economics layer is the moat.
ideas.why_clears_costs: GE ~$210, 1-cent tick, ~2-4 cent spread; an aftermarket-driven beat moves it 4-7% ($8-15/share). TDG ~$1,500 moves $50-100 on aftermarket surprises. Pre-positioning captures multiple dollars against a few-cent round trip; options add leverage.
ideas.lens: Physical-world telemetry (grid, logistics, industrial) that leads a commodity or a liquid equity

ideas.name: Pit Pulse
ideas.source: High-resolution satellite imagery and short-dwell video of the largest open-pit copper mines (Escondida, Collahuasi, Grasberg, Morenci, Cerro Verde). Ultra-class haul trucks cycling between the pit face and crusher are directly countable, and cycle count x payload = ore moved, the leading input to reported copper production.
ideas.collection: Task sub-meter imagery (Planet SkySat, Maxar, Umbra SAR for cloud/night) over each pit; run CV to detect and track individual 300-400t haul trucks, estimate cycle times and crusher-queue lengths, and convert to daily ore tonnage using per-mine payload and grade models, aggregated to each miner's attributable output.
ideas.instrument: Freeport-McMoRan (FCX), Southern Copper (SCCO), BHP (BHP); COMEX copper futures (HG) and CPER ETF.
ideas.mechanism: Miners report quarterly production; truck-cycle tonnage accumulates through the quarter and is finished before the print, while the market prices off prior guidance and lagged Chilean/Peruvian export stats. Also front-runs ICSG output and disruptions show up in truck idle-time within days.
ideas.lead: 4-8 weeks ahead of quarterly production reports; strikes/slope failures visible within days.
ideas.exclusivity: Capex of tasking imagery plus a CV pipeline tuned to pit geometry, truck classes, and grade-blending - years of work per mine - and SAR fusion to see through Andean cloud is a hard capex/engineering barrier a software-only rival cannot leap.

ideas.name: Fifty-Hertz Tap
ideas.source: Real-time electrical grid frequency (nominal 50Hz) from an independent distributed sensor network inside China (and other opaque manufacturers). Instantaneous frequency deviation is an un-fakeable sub-second readout of the whole synchronous grid's supply-demand balance - total system load minus generation.
ideas.collection: Deploy and operate low-cost mains-frequency data loggers on ordinary wall outlets across industrial provinces (the academic grid-frequency-monitoring technique), stream the frequency time series, and model the load-following signature to nowcast heavy-industrial electricity draw independent of the smoothed, lagged statistics-bureau numbers.
ideas.instrument: SGX iron-ore futures, LME/COMEX copper, and China-proxy equities (FXI, KWEB, or BHP/RIO/VALE which sell into China).
ideas.mechanism: China's official industrial-production and power-consumption data is distrusted, smoothed, and lagged; a real-time grid-load read is the only credible independent input, and heavy-industry electricity demand leads commodity demand. There is no consensus number for the edge to decay against.
ideas.lead: Days-to-weeks ahead of monthly NBS industrial output and utility data; captures holiday/curtailment shifts in real time.
ideas.exclusivity: A physical, in-country sensor network (Genscape-style hardware access moat) that a software-only rival cannot replicate, plus the load-disaggregation model - and it keeps working when the official channel is dark or manipulated.
ideas.why_clears_costs: SGX iron-ore ~$105/t, 100t contract (~$10,500 notional), moves $3-8/t (= $300-800/contract) on China-demand surprises versus a $0.05/t ($5) tick. Copper and FXI options offer similar multiples; the macro instruments are enormous and clear costs trivially.

ideas.name: Cavern Creep
ideas.source: Radar interferometry (InSAR) over salt-cavern natural-gas and NGL storage fields (Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, and European caverns). Injection/withdrawal changes cavern pressure, causing millimeter-scale surface heave/subsidence directly above each cavern - a physical proxy for stored inventory.
ideas.collection: Process Sentinel-1 (free, 6-12 day revisit) and commercial X-band SAR (ICEYE/Umbra, daily) interferograms over a registry of cavern wellheads; convert the surface-deformation time series into per-cavern volume change via a geomechanical model, and aggregate to regional storage change ahead of the official release.
ideas.instrument: Henry Hub natural-gas futures (NG) and UNG; Mont Belvieu NGL exposure via Enterprise (EPD), Targa (TRGP).
ideas.mechanism: The EIA weekly natural-gas storage report is a slow, scheduled, market-moving number; an independent cavern-deformation read estimates the same injection/withdrawal days ahead. Salt caverns are the swing/peaking storage, so they lead the balance most sharply.
ideas.lead: Days ahead of the Thursday EIA storage print; multi-day lead over regional NGL inventory data.
ideas.exclusivity: InSAR processing (atmospheric correction, phase unwrapping) plus a per-cavern geomechanical deformation-to-volume model is a deep-tech pipeline, not a licensable dataset; the cavern registry and calibration are the years-of-work barrier.
ideas.why_clears_costs: NG ~$3.50/MMBtu, 10,000 MMBtu contract (~$35,000 notional); a storage surprise routinely moves NG $0.10-0.30 (= $1,000-3,000/contract) versus a $0.001 ($10) tick. UNG options and the futures are highly liquid; even a modest storage-miss capture clears costs many-fold.

ideas.name: Meltshop Heat
ideas.source: Electric-arc-furnace mini-mills radiate an intense, intermittent thermal signature each tap cycle and draw huge, characteristic power spikes. Both are observable and both track molten-steel output ahead of quarterly shipment reports.
ideas.collection: Combine thermal-IR satellite passes (Landsat TIRS, ECOSTRESS, Sentinel-3) over a registry of EAF meltshops with substation load telemetry / power-market nodal draw near each mill; detect tap cycles, count heats per day, and convert to tons of liquid steel per mill using furnace-size models, aggregated to each producer.
ideas.instrument: Nucor (NUE), Steel Dynamics (STLD), Cleveland-Cliffs (CLF); CME hot-rolled-coil (HRC) steel futures.
ideas.mechanism: Steel shipments and ASPs are scheduled quarterly disclosures; heat-count tonnage accumulates continuously and is finished before the print, while consensus prices off lagged AISI capacity-utilization and stale scrap prices. The heat-count IS the shipment proxy.
ideas.lead: 4-8 weeks ahead of quarterly shipment reports; leads the weekly AISI raw-steel utilization series by days.
ideas.exclusivity: Fusing furnace-cycle thermal detection with nodal power draw and a heat-to-tonnage model per meltshop is a multi-year, multi-source build; neither raw feed alone yields the number, and the dual-source fusion is unreplicable by capital-plus-code alone.
ideas.why_clears_costs: NUE ~$140, 1-cent tick, ~2-4 cent spread; a shipment/ASP surprise moves it 4-8% ($5.60-11/share). HRC futures ~$800/ton, 20-ton contract (~$16,000), move $30-80/ton (= $600-1,600/contract) on output surprises versus a $1/ton ($20) tick. Comfortable clearance in both.

ideas.mechanism: Monthly sales/deliveries and export figures are scheduled disclosures; port-yard-plus-carrier throughput is a near-complete proxy accumulated before the print, while the market prices off prior-month sales and dealer surveys. Distinct from single-factory finished-inventory counts.
ideas.lead: 2-5 weeks ahead of monthly export/sales releases; captures chip shortages and port strikes in real time.
ideas.exclusivity: The vehicle-counting CV over marshalling yards, the RoRo draft-to-units model, and per-terminal automaker attribution are years of work - materially beyond generic AIS tracking and beyond one-factory lot monitoring.

ideas.name: Sportsbook Structural-Hold Nowcast
ideas.source: Full opening-to-closing odds boards across every US online sportsbook and state (spreads, totals, props, parlays), plus final game/prop results.
ideas.collection: Continuously ingest per-book, per-state lines via odds APIs and board captures; compute each event's theoretical hold from the posted vig; simulate each operator's realized P&L as results settle; weight by state-level handle share and free-bet/promo drag; model parlay outcome-correlation.
ideas.instrument: DKNG, FLUT (US ADR), PENN, CZR common + listed options; BETZ for sector expression.
ideas.mechanism: Online-gaming revenue = handle x win margin. Realized win margin is finished as games settle through the quarter and swings hard from expected hold when correlated outcomes (favorites/overs/popular parlays) all cash — a structurally bad or good stretch for the book — while sell-side models a static hold assumption.
ideas.lead: Accumulates continuously across the reporting quarter; the structural realized-hold read is essentially complete weeks before the revenue/earnings release.
ideas.exclusivity: Moat is the multi-book, multi-state odds-capture pipeline plus parlay-correlation modeling of realized hold and per-operator handle-share weighting, calibrated on years of line-and-result history.
