ideas.name: Earnings-Call Vocal-Stress Drift
ideas.source: The raw AUDIO of quarterly earnings calls and analyst-day webcasts (not the transcript everyone else reads).
ideas.collection: Acoustic feature extraction (pitch/f0 micro-tremor, jitter/shimmer, filled-pause and latency rates, articulation-rate variance) with speaker diarization to isolate the CEO and CFO, scored by a model trained on cognitive-load/affect features against subsequent 20-60 day abnormal returns and restatement/guidance-miss outcomes.
ideas.instrument: Single-name large-cap equities and their listed options (directional delta trade, since IV crushes post-print).
ideas.mechanism: Vocal cues of hesitation and cognitive load when executives discuss guidance/segments predict negative post-earnings drift and elevated restatement risk (consistent with Mayew & Venkatachalam's 'Power of Voice'). The marginal reader prices off the text and misses the paralinguistic channel entirely.
ideas.lead: The drift accrues over days-to-weeks AFTER the call while the transcript-reading crowd has already priced the words; the voice-derived score is complete the moment the call ends.
ideas.exclusivity: Requires a curated per-executive voiceprint/baseline library across years of calls plus a validated acoustic-to-return model. It is processing, not a purchasable dataset — nobody sells 'CFO vocal-stress score aligned to forward returns.'
ideas.why_clears_costs: Flagged names show 2-5% directional drift over the following weeks. On a $100 large-cap, a 3% move = $3.00/share against a 1-cent tick and typically 1-2 cent spread — ~150-300x friction; deep option chains make the delta trade scalable.
ideas.lens: Novel exclusive-processing plays on audio/video/text streams that lead a liquid instrument

ideas.name: Brand Ad-Flight ACR Census
ideas.source: Live linear-TV broadcast streams (hundreds of national/cable channels) plus connected-TV (CTV) ad inventory captured by instrumented playback.
ideas.collection: Automated content recognition fingerprints every ad creative in the broadcast/CTV stream, classifies it to advertiser/brand/product, and counts spot volume and estimated GRPs per brand per week across all monitored channels — an advertiser-side spend census built from raw video/audio.
ideas.instrument: Consumer/pharma/gaming large-caps: LLY & NVO (GLP-1 DTC flights), DKNG & FLUT (sportsbook flights), streaming/telco, auto insurers (PGR, ALL) — stock + options.
ideas.mechanism: Ad-flight ramps and cuts lead the customer-acquisition, new-patient-start, or betting-handle numbers those campaigns are designed to produce; a surprise surge/cut vs. consensus SG&A and net-adds moves the print.
ideas.lead: Weeks: campaign flights run ahead of the reporting-period sales they drive, so the spend census is essentially complete before the quarter closes and long before the CAC/net-add disclosure.
ideas.exclusivity: The ACR fingerprint library, brand classifier, and multi-hundred-channel + CTV capture rig is a heavy engineering/capex build. The finished 'brand spot count' is not licensable off the shelf tied to a ticker.
ideas.why_clears_costs: An ad-spend/CAC surprise moves a name like DKNG ~4-6% at the print. On DKNG near $40, 5% = $2.00/share vs a 1-cent tick and penny spread — ~200x friction; LLY at 3% is >$20/share. Weekly options carry the size.
ideas.lens: Novel exclusive-processing plays on audio/video/text streams that lead a liquid instrument

ideas.name: Ship-Channel VHF Voice Tripwire
ideas.source: Marine VHF voice traffic (harbor control, vessel-traffic-service, pilots, tugs) monitored via coastal SDR receivers at the Houston Ship Channel, Sabine-Neches, and LA/Long Beach.
ideas.collection: 24/7 ASR over marine-VHF voice with a maritime-phraseology lexicon ('channel closed', 'allision', 'aground', 'reduced visibility restrictions', 'one-way traffic', 'security zone'), geofenced by channel segment, extracting closure onset/duration and affected berths.
ideas.instrument: RBOB gasoline futures (RB) and crude spreads; refiner equities VLO, MPC, PSX (stock + options).
ideas.mechanism: A multi-hour-to-multi-day channel closure backs up crude receipts and refined-product loadings on the US Gulf, widening gasoline cracks and pressuring the affected refiners' throughput — the verbal closure call is a direct read on a supply disruption.
ideas.lead: VHF voice reports the grounding/fog closure/allision in real time, hours ahead of USCG marine-safety bulletins, shipping-agent circulars, and energy-newswire coverage.
ideas.exclusivity: Deployed coastal hardware plus robust ASR on noisy marine VHF with maritime domain lexicon is a capex + field-ops moat a software-only rival cannot leap; the raw radio is public but nobody else converts it into a clean closure-duration series.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A multi-day HSC/Sabine closure moves RB ~3-8 cents/gal. RB is 42,000 gal/contract, so 5 cents = $2,100/contract against a $0.0001 tick ($4.20) and ~1-3 tick spread — a 150x+ multiple. VLO at a 2% move is ~$3/share vs a penny.

ideas.name: Xinwen Lianbo Broadcast Decoder
ideas.source: China's 19:00 CST state-TV evening news (CCTV 'Xinwen Lianbo') and paired State Council/NDRC broadcast segments — the authoritative signal of top-level policy emphasis.
ideas.collection: Real-time Mandarin ASR of the live broadcast + a segment-structure model (order, on-screen duration, leadership-name placement) and a trained policy-emphasis lexicon (property easing, SOE directives, stimulus, price controls, 'security', supply guarantees) scored against subsequent policy actions and market moves.
ideas.instrument: SGX 62% Fe iron-ore futures, copper (LME/HG), and China equity ETFs FXI/KWEB plus liquid China ADRs; CNH.
ideas.mechanism: The broadcast's segment ordering, air-time, and phrasing telegraph policy direction (stimulus vs. tightening, property support, commodity-supply campaigns) before the formal document lands, moving the China-beta commodities and equities.
ideas.lead: Hours over English-language translation/analyst summaries the same evening, and days over the actual policy circular; the read is fully formed at 19:30 CST.
ideas.exclusivity: Requires real-time broadcast ASR in Mandarin, a years-deep archive to model segment structure, and a policy lexicon that maps political phrasing to market outcomes — an interpretive build, not a purchasable feed.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A clear stimulus/property-easing signal moves iron ore 2-5% and FXI 2-4%. SGX iron ore is 100 tonnes/lot, so $3/t = $300/contract vs a small tick; FXI near $30 at 3% = $0.90/share against a 1-cent tick and penny spread — ~90x friction.
ideas.lens: Novel exclusive-processing plays on audio/video/text streams that lead a liquid instrument

ideas.name: Foreign-Gazette Clearance Scanner
ideas.source: Foreign-language official regulatory notice streams — China SAMR merger-review postings (Chinese), the EU Official Journal, and comparable Korean/Brazilian/Japanese competition gazettes — that clear or block global M&A.
ideas.collection: Real-time scrape + machine-translation + entity-resolution pipeline that maps each freshly posted notice to the exact pending deal and its US/EU-listed target ticker, flagging conditional approvals, clearances, and remedy demands the instant they post.
ideas.instrument: Merger-arb spreads on liquid large-cap deal targets awaiting a foreign competition approval (stock long / spread trade + options).
ideas.mechanism: For a deal whose remaining gate is Chinese SAMR or an EU decision, the notice IS the binary catalyst; an unexpected clearance snaps the gross spread shut and re-rates the target.
ideas.lead: Hours over English-language newswires, which lag translation and formatting of the foreign posting; the notice appears in the source language first.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is multilingual, real-time scraping + translation + deal-to-ticker entity resolution across several regulators' idiosyncratic posting systems — a maintained build, not a licensed 'deal-approval' dataset.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A surprise clearance on a deal trading at a 3% gross spread compresses it to ~0.5%, an ~2.5% jump in the target. On an $80 target that is ~$2.00/share against a 1-cent tick and penny spread — ~200x friction; the target's options add convexity.
ideas.lens: Novel exclusive-processing plays on audio/video/text streams that lead a liquid instrument

ideas.name: AdCom Webcast Vote Predictor
ideas.source: The live FDA Advisory Committee (AdCom) webcast — panel discussion, sponsor Q&A, and the roll-call vote — streamed as audio/video, plus paired EMA/CHMP oral hearings.
ideas.collection: Real-time ASR with panelist diarization + an FDA-review lexicon (efficacy endpoints, safety signals, benefit-risk phrasing, 'I can't support', 'I would vote yes but') feeding a vote-prediction model trained on historical AdCom transcripts and their subsequent approval outcomes.
ideas.instrument: Large-cap pharma (LLY, PFE, MRK, ABBV, BMY, GILD, AMGN) and liquid biotech + XBI (stock + options straddles).
ideas.mechanism: Panelist tone during the multi-hour meeting is a tight leading proxy for the vote, and the committee recommendation itself leads the final FDA action; the name re-rates sharply on the read.
ideas.lead: The diarized sentiment score is complete during the webcast, minutes-to-hours ahead of the official vote-tally readout and clean newswire framing; the AdCom recommendation itself leads the FDA's final decision by weeks.
ideas.exclusivity: Medical-panel diarization, an FDA benefit-risk lexicon, and a vote model trained on years of historical AdComs is a specialized build; the webcast is public but the calibrated probability is not for sale.
ideas.why_clears_costs: AdCom outcomes move single-name biotech 10-40% and large-cap pharma on a key drug 3-8%. On a $150 pharma name a 5% move = $7.50/share against a 1-cent tick and penny spread — ~750x friction; straddles capture the binary.
ideas.lens: Novel exclusive-processing plays on audio/video/text streams that lead a liquid instrument

ideas.name: Hearing-Hostility Valence Index
ideas.source: Live-televised Congressional oversight, appropriations, and antitrust hearings (audio/video webcasts) where members question CEOs/regulators about a sector.
ideas.collection: Real-time diarized ASR mapping each utterance to the speaking member, scored by a member-specific hostility/valence lexicon and mapped to the companies/sector named — a Prattle-style instant, identical read of a multi-hour hearing.
ideas.instrument: Sector ETFs (XBI on drug-pricing, XLK on Big-Tech antitrust, XLF on bank oversight, ITA on defense) and the named large-cap's options.
ideas.mechanism: Aggregate questioning hostility predicts the regulatory/headline risk the market will price into the sector; the machine read beats slow, uneven human parsing of a 3-hour multi-member hearing.
ideas.lead: The valence score is instantaneous and consistent, firing before pundit summaries and before retail/algos react to a single cherry-picked soundbite — minutes-to-hours of lead over the formed human consensus.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is a member-specific trained lexicon plus real-time diarization and company mapping built over many hearing archives — the same 'years-built lexicon that can't be reconstructed overnight' pattern, applied to hearing audio.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A hostile drug-pricing/antitrust hearing moves the sector ETF 1-3% and the named large-cap more. On XBI near $90, 2% = $1.80/share against a 1-cent tick and penny spread — ~90-180x friction; large-cap options add leverage. The standing hearing calendar gives repeatability.
ideas.lens: Novel exclusive-processing plays on audio/video/text streams that lead a liquid instrument

ideas.name: Streaming Ad-Fill Instrumentation
ideas.source: The actual video ad breaks delivered inside streaming platforms' ad-supported tiers (Netflix, Disney+, Peacock, Max, Roku, Paramount+), captured by a fleet of instrumented playback clients.
ideas.collection: Geo-diverse instrumented streaming devices run sessions across each platform's ad tier; ACR fingerprints every delivered ad creative to measure fill-rate (filled vs. house/unfilled slots), ad-load (minutes/hour), and advertiser mix per platform over time.
ideas.instrument: NFLX, DIS, ROKU, WBD, PARA, CMCSA (stock + options).
ideas.mechanism: Fill-rate x ad-load x advertiser mix is a direct, continuously accumulating proxy for the platform's ad revenue and ad-ARM (ad revenue per member), the exact metric the platform will report; a surprise leads the print.
ideas.lead: A full quarter: fill-rate ramps continuously through the reporting window and is essentially complete before the ad-tier revenue disclosure, which the sell-side can only model loosely.
ideas.exclusivity: Requires a maintained fleet of geo-diverse instrumented streaming clients plus ACR on delivered creatives — publisher-side telemetry that physically cannot be scraped by outsiders and is not licensable, distinct from advertiser-side spot counts.
ideas.why_clears_costs: Streaming ad-revenue/ARM surprises move NFLX several percent. On NFLX near $700, a 2% move = $14/share against a 1-cent tick and typically sub-5-cent spread — >250x friction; ROKU at 4% is ~$3/share vs a penny. Options chains are deep.
ideas.lens: Novel exclusive-processing plays on audio/video/text streams that lead a liquid instrument

ideas.name: Foreign-Supplier Call Decoder
ideas.source: The AUDIO of overseas suppliers' earnings calls held in Mandarin, Japanese, Korean, and German BEFORE their US customer reports — qualitative order-volume, pricing, and demand commentary.
ideas.collection: ASR + diarization + machine-translation of foreign-language supplier calls, extracting demand/pricing/inventory commentary and routing it through a maintained bill-of-materials supply-chain graph to the US large-cap customer.
ideas.instrument: US large-cap customers whose Asian/European suppliers report first — AAPL, NVDA, AMD, AVGO, TSLA suppliers-of — traded via the US customer's stock + options.
ideas.mechanism: A supplier's qualitative demand tone (order pull-ins, ASP pressure, capacity notes) that contradicts consensus is a leading read on the US customer's quarter and re-rates the customer at its print.
ideas.lead: Days-to-weeks: foreign suppliers frequently report before the US customer, and the commentary is in a language the US crowd does not systematically monitor, so it stays un-priced.
ideas.exclusivity: The moat is multilingual real-time ASR/diarization/translation PLUS a maintained supplier->customer BoM graph — an interpretive processing build, wholly distinct from licensing a supplier's headline monthly-revenue number.
ideas.why_clears_costs: A supplier-derived demand surprise moves the US large-cap 3-8% at its print. On NVDA near $120, 4% = ~$4.80/share against a 1-cent tick and penny spread — ~480x friction; the deep US-large-cap option chains carry real size.
ideas.lens: Novel exclusive-processing plays on audio/video/text streams that lead a liquid instrument

triage.name: Data-Center Waste-Heat Thermal Census
triage.data_exists: Landsat-9 TIRS (100m, 16-day) and ECOSTRESS (70m, 1-5 day, irregular ISS orbit) are real and public but coarse and cloud-limited; commercial high-revisit thermal smallsats are nascent, coarse and expensive. No source resolves a campus into more than a handful of noisy pixels.
triage.lead: Not the binding issue, but weak: chip DEMAND is what NVDA trades on, not live campus heat, which is a coincident read on already-deployed capacity. EIA regional power data, utility interconnection queues and PPA/power channel checks cover the same ground.
triage.dollar_test: Passes on arithmetic and is NOT the binding constraint: NVDA weeklies are penny-wide, moves 6-10% (~$11-18) on data-center prints, so a 1.5% pre-print drift (~$2.70) dwarfs the ~$0.02 spread. The edge dies on data quality, not execution economics.
triage.reason: At 70-100m with 8-16 day cloud-limited revisit you get a few noisy pixels per site, and a large share of hyperscale reject heat is LATENT (evaporative/adiabatic cooling towers) leaving no sensible-heat signature, so the heat-to-megawatts inversion is not credible at the needed precision. Worse, thermal state reads already-deployed utilization, not NVDA's forward chip-order demand that the stock actually prices.

triage.name: Electric-Arc-Furnace Thermal Pulse Index
triage.data_exists: Thermal-IR satellites are real but revisit is 1-16 days, not sub-minute; no constellation re-images the same furnace during each ~40-60 minute tap-to-tap heat. The melt occurs inside an enclosed steel melt-shop, so the space-visible signal is muted roof/off-gas, not the arc.
triage.lead: AISI weekly raw-steel utilization publishes Monday for the prior week - a heavily-telegraphed 1-2 day lead at most, and steel equities trade more on HRC price and guidance than on the well-anticipated utilization line.
triage.dollar_test: Passes on arithmetic and is not binding: NUE moves 3-5% (~$4-7); a 2% drift (~$2.80) is ~56x a nickel spread. Execution is fine; the count itself is impossible.
triage.reason: The core claim - detecting and counting 'sub-minute melt transients' per furnace from orbit - does not exist: revisit is days, not minutes, and the furnace is enclosed so you'd capture a random snapshot, never a duty cycle. Cannot reconstruct heats-per-week, so there is no signal to trade.

triage.name: Refinery Process-Heater Thermal Run-Rate
triage.data_exists: VIIRS (daily hotspot/flare), Landsat TIRS (100m, 16-day) and commercial thermal are real, but unit-level segmentation (CDU charge heaters vs flares/coker/sulfur units) at 100m is hard and cloud-limited.
triage.lead: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report (Wednesday) is already intensively nowcast by multiple vendors, so the pre-print lead is largely arbitraged out.
triage.dollar_test: Passes on arithmetic, not binding: RBOB tick $4.20, a 2c/gal crack move ~$840/contract vs ~$4-8 round-trip; VLO 2% drift ~$2.80 vs ~3c spread. Economics fine; exclusivity is the problem.
triage.reason: Satellite refinery-throughput nowcasting is a mature, commoditized product category (Kpler, Vortexa, Wood Mackenzie/Genscape, IIR, Ursa) whose estimates already feed the EIA-anticipation trade in liquid VLO/MPC/RBOB. No moat, no incremental lead - a crowded, commoditized trade.

triage.name: Ammonia Synthesis-Loop Thermal Outage Detector
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (INFORMATIONAL LEAD); compounded by Filter 6/7 thin capacity
triage.data_exists: Strongest of the set: steam reformers are large, persistent, very-hot sources and an unplanned trip is a robust BINARY state change (not a fragile continuous inversion), catchable with VIIRS-class daily thermal plus Landsat. Physically the most sound idea here.
triage.lead: This is the fatal point. The nitrogen market is small and intensively covered by specialist trade press (Argus, ICIS, CRU, Profercy, Green Markets) that reports major trips within hours via human sources, and operators issue force-majeure notices that leak immediately. The events big enough to move CF are exactly the wire-covered ones.
triage.dollar_test: Passes clearly: CF near $90 moves 4-8% (~$3.60-7) on outage/nitrogen news; a 3% anticipatory move (~$2.70) is ~90x the ~$0.03 spread, options penny-to-nickel wide.
triage.reason: Closest to advancing - physics and dollar test both pass - but the harvestable lead is thin: material outages surface via force majeure and Argus/ICIS at roughly the same time, and CF's price is dominated by Henry Hub gas and Chinese urea-export policy, with single-trip direction/attribution ambiguous (own-plant volume loss vs competitor supply cut). Non-material trips that thermal might front-run do not move the stock. Very low event capacity and a thin de-overlapped sample compound the kill.

triage.name: Cement Kiln Active-Burn Thermal Census
triage.fails_which_filter: Mechanism / signal-to-instrument mismatch (fatal at the data-drives-instrument premise, akin to Filter 1)
triage.data_exists: The data is real and robust: rotary kilns are among the most unambiguous thermal sources and VIIRS Nightfire-class detection of burning/idle state is well established. The remote sensing is not the problem.
triage.lead: Irrelevant given the mismatch - USGS cement stats are lagged, but cement is not what these tickers trade on.
triage.dollar_test: Passes on arithmetic and is not binding: VMC ~$280 moves 3-5% (~$8-14) on VOLUME, a 2% drift (~$5.60) is ~70x a dime spread. Execution is fine; the measured variable is just the wrong one.
triage.reason: Verified: VMC and MLM are AGGREGATES companies - aggregates are ~70-76% of profit, quarried by crushing with no kiln and no thermal signature, and Vulcan carries no cement segment at all. Clinker/cement output (what the census measures) does not drive these instruments' earnings, which turn on aggregates volume and pricing. A clean thermal read of the wrong variable is still worthless for the named trade.

triage.name: AIS-Dark Tanker RF-Geolocation Flow Meter
triage.data_exists: Partly degraded: one named source, Kleos Space, is bankrupt/trading-suspended (verified). HawkEye 360, Unseenlabs and SAR (Sentinel-1, ICEYE, Capella) are real, but RF+SAR voyage reconstruction is expensive and incomplete.
triage.lead: None to speak of: dark-fleet and sanctioned-barrel flows are already tracked and sold by Kpler, Vortexa and TankerTrackers and are constantly in the general press.
triage.dollar_test: Passes on arithmetic and is not binding: WTI tick $10/lot, a $0.50-2.00 supply move is $500-2,000 vs ~$10-20 round-trip. Cheap to trade, but the signal doesn't predict the instrument.
triage.reason: A named data source is defunct, and more decisively front-month crude is a macro instrument (OPEC policy, demand, macro, inventories) on which a marginal grey-flow revision has negligible predictive power, while dark-fleet tracking is already a crowded, commoditized commercial product. No exclusive edge and no mechanistic pull on CL/BZ.

triage.name: SAR All-Weather Iron-Ore Port Stockpile Volumetrics
triage.data_exists: Sentinel-1 is free and ICEYE/Capella/Umbra are real, but SAR-to-pile-VOLUME on bulk stockpiles is noisy (backscatter/layover, not clean photogrammetric height); optical shadow photogrammetry remains the volumetric standard.
triage.lead: Thin: Mysteel and SteelHome publish weekly Chinese port ore inventories, and multiple satellite vendors already sell port-stockpile monitoring - the survey is widely anticipated.
triage.dollar_test: Passes on arithmetic, not binding: SGX 62% Fe 2-4% move ~$200-400/lot vs a few-dollar round-trip; VALE ADR (~$11) 2-3% (~$0.28) is ~28x a 1c spread.
triage.reason: Chinese port ore inventory is among the most-surveilled datasets in commodities - Mysteel/SteelHome plus numerous satellite vendors already cover it - so there is no exclusive lead, and iron-ore price is driven more by Chinese steel demand and policy than by port-stock wiggles. Crowded trade, and the SAR volumetric inversion is less reliable than the pitch claims.

triage.name: Sentinel-5P NO2 China Industrial-Activity Nowcast
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 7 (crowded/commoditized, zero-moat public data), secondarily Filter 2
triage.data_exists: TROPOMI NO2 is real, daily and FREE/public at ~3.5x5.5km; the de-weathering and industrial-masking methods are well published and openly available - which is precisely the problem, not an asset.
triage.lead: Weak: NBS output/PMIs are distrusted, but copper prices on LME/macro/USD/China-policy flow continuously, and NO2-based China activity nowcasts have been ubiquitous among academics, central banks and macro funds since the 2020 COVID episode.
triage.dollar_test: Passes on arithmetic, not binding: HG 2-4c/lb move is $500-1,000/contract vs ~$25 round-trip; FXI 1-2% (~$0.35-0.70) vs a penny spread. Cheap to trade, but no proprietary signal.
triage.reason: Built entirely on free public satellite data using a saturated, textbook technique - there is no exclusivity or moat, and de-weathered NO2 as a China-activity proxy is already standard practice. Front-month copper is a global macro instrument on which the weekly index adds little incremental predictive power. Commoditized, crowded, no edge.

triage.name: GNSS-Reflectometry Root-Zone Soil-Moisture Yield Model
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 7 (crowded/commoditized), secondarily Filter 1 (overstated physics) and Filter 6 (once-a-year, overlapped)
triage.data_exists: Overstated: SMAP and GNSS-R measure NEAR-SURFACE (0-5cm) moisture, not root-zone (which must be modeled/inferred), and CYGNSS is an OCEAN/hurricane mission whose land soil-moisture product is coarse (hundreds of m to km) and degraded over vegetated/arid cropland - verified. The 'root-zone reflectometry' premise is a stretch.
triage.lead: Grain markets reprice on Corn Belt weather and soil moisture continuously (daily GFS/ECMWF), and satellite yield nowcasting is saturated (Descartes Labs, Gro Intelligence, Pro Farmer, USDA-NASS), so the WASDE lead is largely competed away.
triage.dollar_test: Passes on arithmetic, not binding: ZC WASDE surprises move 10-25c/bu ($500-1,250) vs ~$25 round-trip; ZS larger. Deep, tight markets - execution is not the issue.
triage.reason: The physical claim (root-zone moisture from reflectometry) is overstated - the sensors see only the top few cm and CYGNSS is a degraded land product - and, decisively, weather/satellite-driven yield nowcasting is one of the most crowded alt-data arenas, with futures already pricing moisture continuously. Yield is also effectively a once-per-season signal with heavily overlapped daily reads (fake t-stats), so the WASDE edge is neither exclusive nor independent.

triage.name: Dark-Fiber DAS Rail-Traffic Census
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 7 (EXECUTABLE/CAPACITY - capex + partial coverage), secondarily Filter 2 (lead) and Filter 6
triage.data_exists: DAS train detection/classification is real, proven technology, but it requires dark-fiber IRUs physically paralleling specific rail corridors - a large capex/contract barrier that a small trader cannot leap, and it only ever covers a fraction of each railroad's network.
triage.lead: The AAR publishes comprehensive weekly rail traffic (carloads + intermodal) every Wednesday for the prior week; a partial-corridor DAS sample cannot reliably beat a complete national count with only days of lag.
triage.dollar_test: Passes on arithmetic and is not binding: UNP ~$230 moves 3-6% (~$7-14), a 2% drift (~$4.60) is ~150x a 3c spread. Execution economics are fine; the build and coverage are the problem.
triage.reason: Not executable at capacity for a small trader - securing DAS across enough corridors to be nationally representative is a heavy capex/contract undertaking that still leaves a partial sample, which cannot reliably front-run AAR's comprehensive weekly report; railroad equities also trade on pricing, operating ratio and guidance more than on already-public weekly volumes. Continuous same-corridor data is also highly autocorrelated, so pooled t-stats overstate significance.

triage.name: Reinsurer Live-Cat Loss Model
triage.data_exists: Yes for inputs: NHC advisories, HWRF/HMON windfields, FEMA/USGS parcel and building-stock data are public. But per-company net-of-reinsurance tower reconstruction from 10-K/Schedule P is coarse, and the RMS/Verisk-class vulnerability-times-exposure model the thesis admits takes 'years of actuarial engineering' is not buildable by a small trader — the exclusivity claim is also the reason YOU cannot build it.
triage.lead: Thin. Verified: KCC/RMS/CoreLogic publish flash industry insured-loss estimates within ~1-2 days of landfall (Idalia +2 days, Michael, Milton, Melissa), and they are broadcast to exactly the insurance/ILS trading community. The convergence you want to front-run happens in a day or two.
triage.dollar_test: PASSES in isolation. RNR ~$230-260; an above/below-threshold call drives roughly $12-38/share (5-15%) over 1-5 days against a ~$0.02-0.05 stock spread on penny ticks. The gross dollar move dwarfs frictions by ~2 orders of magnitude. The kill is not the dollar test.
triage.reason: Passes the dollar test but fails as a strategy. Filter 6/7: material US landfalls number a handful per year (some years zero); a 'book' of a few same-season, correlated events yields no de-overlapped t-stat and near-zero capacity — this is a lumpy rare-event bet, not a compounding portfolio. The counterparties are RMS/AIR-licensed reinsurance and ILS specialists with their own rapid loss models, not markable retail — a crowded specialist trade (filter 7) with a lead already competed away by third-party flash estimates (filter 2).

triage.name: Agency mREIT Book-Value Nowcast
triage.data_exists: Yes. TBA/agency-MBS and specified-pool runs, TRACE prints, on-the-run Treasury/swap curves, and the 10-Q portfolio disclosure are all obtainable; the daily convexity/prepay mark is real quant work but doable.
triage.lead: None. The rate and MBS moves that drive book value are public in real time, the mark is near-mechanical, multiple sell-side desks publish weekly BV estimates, and mREITs have historically disclosed estimated book value directly. Consensus already embeds the nowcast — the crowd does NOT only learn book value at the print.
triage.dollar_test: FAILS on the incremental move. NLY ~$20 moves 3-8% ($0.60-1.60) on a book-value SURPRISE — but the surprise is measured against a consensus that already contains the public rate-driven mark. Your incremental edge over that consensus is a few cents, i.e. inside the ~$0.01-0.02 spread. The headline 30-150x-spread math prices the whole move, not the sliver you actually add.
triage.reason: Filter 2 kills it: the driving inputs are public real-time and the BV nowcast is already published by the Street and the companies. Also filter 5 — the price-to-book discount/premium is a rational premium for convexity, prepayment and management risk, not free money — and filter 3 once you net out consensus.

triage.name: Constant-Quality Used-Vehicle Price Nowcast
triage.data_exists: Yes. Listings are scrapeable; Manheim is paywalled/lagged (verified: official reading on 5th business day, mid-month is a 'checkpoint' that Manheim explicitly says is NOT a directional flash). The hedonic mix-adjustment is buildable.
triage.lead: None that is exclusive. Verified: YipitData (and M Science) sell used-car/wholesale nowcasts explicitly covering CVNA and KMX to 150+ hedge funds, and sell-side models Manheim. The 'moat' is a commodity product sold to hundreds of funds.
triage.dollar_test: Nominally large but not harvestable as claimed. CVNA ~$300 moves $20-50 on used-car data — but that move is driven by GPU, credit/financing and volume, not just wholesale-price direction; the wholesale sliver you add is already in consensus, so incremental edge is small vs a name already saturated with alt data.
triage.reason: Filter 2/7: this is a commoditized alt-data trade (YipitData/M Science coverage of CVNA/KMX confirmed). CVNA is one of the most alt-data-saturated, crowded names on the tape; there is no informational lead and no exclusivity.

triage.name: Restaurant Comp Price/Mix Model
triage.data_exists: Yes. Item-level menu prices are scrapeable geo-panel; comp definitions are disclosed.
triage.lead: None. The thesis literally calls this a 'YipitData-class build' — YipitData sells menu-pricing and transaction panels on exactly these chains to 150+ funds. Commoditized; consensus already prices it.
triage.dollar_test: FAILS on signal completeness. CMG moves 5-12% on the comp print, but comps = traffic + price/mix and you only observe the price/mix half — the smaller, near-mechanical piece. Traffic (the swing that sets the sign of the surprise) is unobservable from menus, so your read does not predict the print's direction; the tradeable edge net of that is small versus tight spreads.
triage.reason: Filter 2/7: self-admittedly a commoditized YipitData-class product with no lead. Compounded by a partial-signal problem — modeling price/mix while traffic drives the surprise means the confident-sounding 50-200x-cost move is not one you can actually forecast.

triage.name: Airline Unit-Revenue Inversion Model
triage.data_exists: Partially. Published fares, fare-class buckets and seat maps are scrapeable and ASMs are scheduled — but actual booking VOLUMES and load factors are NOT public. Inverting posted fares plus availability into realized PRASM/TRASM without booked-volume data is heroic; the error bars swamp the guidance surprise.
triage.lead: None. Airlines issue frequent mid-quarter 8-K/investor-update guidance on unit revenue, and fare scraping is a long-standing, widely-run alt-data trade. The market learns RASM direction from the carrier itself, often before your inversion stabilizes.
triage.dollar_test: Nominally fine, effectively not. DAL ~$50 / UAL ~$90 move $3-12 on a RASM guidance surprise against cent-wide spreads — but the RASM estimate error from missing booking volumes is large relative to that surprise, so realized edge after model noise is thin.
triage.reason: Filter 1: the core quantity (realized yield) requires booking volumes that are not obtainable, so the 'reconstruction' is under-identified. Filter 2: carriers self-disclose unit-revenue guidance mid-quarter and fare-scraping is crowded — no durable lead.

triage.name: Earnings-Move Overpricing Model
triage.data_exists: Yes. Option chains, surprise history and seasonality are public.
triage.lead: N/A — this is not an information-lead trade; it is a volatility/event-risk-premium harvest.
triage.dollar_test: Deceptively fine per unit. A 1-2 vol-point mispricing is ~$0.30-1.00 of edge per straddle against a $0.05-0.15 option spread — several times the spread. But the payoff is short convexity: you collect small credits repeatedly and pay out large in the tail, so per-trade edge overstates the true expectation.
triage.reason: Filter 5: selling earnings straddles is the documented, heavily-harvested earnings/variance risk premium — the retail lottery buyer on the other side is paying for real gap/jump convexity, so it is a paid-for risk, not free money, and it is crowded. Filter 6: the payoff has a positive median but a fat left tail; the portfolio MEAN each season is dominated by the occasional large-move blowups, and pooled per-name t-stats across correlated season rows are fiction. A linear read of 'several times the spread' loses money when the tail arrives.

triage.name: Clinical Probability-of-Success Model
triage.data_exists: Yes. ClinicalTrials.gov design fields are public and a hand-labeled outcome DB is buildable (Intelligencia/BioAI-class, hard but real).
triage.lead: Weak. Design fields are public and event IV is already rich into readouts/PDUFA dates; the option-implied probability the thesis folds in is set by the same public design plus sponsor data.
triage.dollar_test: FAILS on the cost stack. Readouts move names 40-100% ($10-40 on a $30-50 stock) and straddles cost 15-40% of spot — but single-name biotech EVENT options carry very wide spreads and brutal post-event IV crush. A claimed 10-15pp PoS edge is within the calibration error of PoS models and is frequently smaller than spread + IV-crush cost, so gross edge does not clear frictions.
triage.reason: Filter 4: biotech binary-event option spreads plus IV crush eat a within-model-error 10-15pp edge — the cost stack is the whole game here and it wins. Filter 5: binary-readout options embed a documented jump/event-risk premium; the marginal seller is compensated for real gap risk. Diversification (the one genuinely good feature) controls variance but cannot manufacture edge when gross < cost stack.

triage.name: P&C Reserve-Adequacy Triangle Model
triage.data_exists: Yes but low-frequency. Verified: detailed Schedule P loss-development triangles appear in the ANNUAL statutory statement only (filed ~Feb-March for the prior year); quarterly statements lack the full triangle. So the signal updates once a year, lagged 2-3 months after year-end.
triage.lead: Weak. Sell-side actuarial analysts and dedicated insurance short-sellers already mine Schedule P; reserve development is slow and telegraphed. The GAAP charge/release is anticipated well before it books.
triage.dollar_test: Nominally fine, undermined by cadence. TRV ~$240 / CB ~$280 move $7-22 (3-8%) on a material charge or release against cent spreads — but you get roughly one fresh triangle observation per name per year.
triage.reason: Filter 1: annual cadence with multi-month latency makes this a once-a-year, stale signal, not a tradeable stream. Filter 6: one de-overlapped observation per name per year across a handful of names yields no honest t-stat — you cannot build a compounding book, and the slow, analyst-covered nature means the surprise is small by the print.

triage.name: Auto-Parts Comp Demand Model
triage.data_exists: Yes but lagged. Verified: FHWA Traffic Volume Trends (VMT) is released with a ~2-month lag; fleet-age/registration data (S&P Global Mobility) is annual. So the 'realized' inputs are stale and low-frequency, and the freshest in-quarter month is unavailable when you need it.
triage.lead: Weak. Miles-driven, fleet age and weather are public macro exhaust that sell-side already maps to auto-parts comps; and auto-parts same-store sales are structurally low-variance (steady mid-single-digit compounders).
triage.dollar_test: FAILS. AZO ~$3,300 nominally moves $130-300 (4-9%), but AZO/ORLY comp SURPRISES are typically only ±1-2pp (these names beat by tiny margins), and AZO options are thin with wide spreads (often $2-$20). The realized surprise-driven move is modest and option illiquidity eats much of it — the '40x the spread' claim assumes a large surprise and a tight spread, neither of which holds.
triage.reason: Filter 1: the driving inputs are lagged 2 months (VMT) and annual (fleet age), so the 'complete weeks before earnings' claim is false. Filter 7: AZO's ~$3,300 options are illiquid with wide spreads and limited capacity, and the low-variance comp series produces small surprises — an un-crowded but un-harvestable edge.

triage.name: Utility Realized-Weather Earnings Model
triage.data_exists: Yes. NOAA degree-days are public in real time; load shapes and the decoupling/weather-rider mechanism are disclosed in rate-case filings.
triage.lead: None. Degree-days are public real-time — the entire market sees the same weather as it happens — and sell-side routinely runs weather-adjusted utility EPS models. There is nothing the crowd learns only at the print.
triage.dollar_test: FAILS. NEE ~$70 / DUK ~$110 move only 2-4% ($1.50-4.50) on a weather-driven EPS surprise, AND the thesis's own key insight is that most large utilities are decoupled/weather-normalized, so the true EPS weather effect is near zero for exactly the names that matter. Utility options are thin with wider spreads. A thin move on a name where the effect is often ~0 after normalization does not clear costs.
triage.reason: Filter 2: weather is the most public real-time input imaginable and is already in sell-side models — no lead. Filter 3: the tradeable dollar move is small (2-4%) and shrinks toward zero once decoupling is applied to the very names named, while utility option spreads are wider — the edge does not beat tick+spread.

triage.name: BNPL Checkout-Offer Panel
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 1 (Data Reality / measurement validity); secondary Filter 2
triage.data_exists: Checkout offers are real and visible per cart, but the collection method breaks the measurement. Approval and APR depend on the applicant, so a panel of synthetic personas with fabricated BINs measures the approval rate of your invented identities, not Affirm's real applicant mix. There is no anchor to calibrate synthetic-persona approval to the reported population. Submitting fabricated identities into a lender's live underwriting engine at scale is also legally fraught (ToS/CFAA, potential application-fraud), and an active anti-bot arms race degrades coverage.
triage.lead: Even if calibrated, AFRM GMV is demand-driven (real consumer purchase volume). Offer terms are the supply-side knob, not the volume that sets GMV/RLTC. You would be reading the lever, not the throughput.
triage.dollar_test: AFRM ~$50-70 moves $8-15 on earnings vs ~1-2c spread and 1c tick — the raw dollar test passes by ~3 orders of magnitude. Friction is NOT the binding constraint; signal validity is.
triage.reason: A synthetic-identity panel cannot be calibrated to Affirm's real approval population and doesn't measure demand-driven GMV. Dies on data reality, not on cost.

triage.name: National Menu-Price Grid
triage.data_exists: Yes — menu prices are public and scrapable at full footprint, and this part is real. But it measures only the price/ticket component, which is the guided, telegraphed half of comps.
triage.lead: No lead on the surprise. Management explicitly guides pricing ('we took ~3% price'), and sell-side already backs menu price out of comps (a 6% SSS on 7% price is a 1% real decline — analysts adjust for exactly this). The variable that actually moves the stock is TRAFFIC/transactions, which menu prices do not observe. You would nowcast the known number and stay blind to the unknown one.
triage.dollar_test: MCD ~$300 x 3-5% = $9-15; CMG/SBUX $3-8 — all dwarf pennies of friction. Raw dollar test passes; it is not the binding constraint.
triage.reason: Measures the guided/announced price component and is blind to the traffic surprise that determines the beat/miss. No informational lead.

triage.name: Achievement-Unlock Install-Base Nowcast
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (Informational Lead); secondary Filter 1 (no absolute denominator)
triage.data_exists: Achievement/trophy percentages are public but are RELATIVE, not counts. After Valve's April-2018 privacy change, SteamSpy-style owner estimates collapsed into wide ranges; console rarity is also percentage-only. Back-solving absolute units from a percentage requires the denominator that is precisely what's unknown, so the rarity-to-owners regression is heroic and noisy.
triage.lead: Publishers issue day-one/week-one unit PR ('sold X million in Y days' — standard for GTA, CoD, Hogwarts Legacy), so the wire beats the panel on the units read. Worse, TTWO/EA bookings are dominated by recurrent/live-service spend (NBA 2K VC, EA FC Ultimate Team), which launch unit count does not capture.
triage.dollar_test: TTWO ~$200 x 8-15% = $16-30; EA $9-18 vs pennies — raw dollar test passes. Not the binding constraint.
triage.reason: No absolute denominator post-2018, publisher PR pre-empts the units read, and bookings are driven by in-game spend that unit-at-launch cannot see.

triage.name: Smart-TV ACR Viewing Panel
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 1 (Data Reality — not obtainable); plus disqualifying legal (App Annie)
triage.data_exists: No — not obtainable by a trader. The idea concedes it requires OWNING or exclusively licensing the OS/SDK telemetry; it 'physically cannot exist for a rival.' A small trader has no path to it. And the one party who does have it (the OS owner) using its customers' confidential device telemetry to trade Roku is exactly the fact pattern the SEC charged in the App Annie 10b-5 case ($10M penalty, founder barred).
triage.lead: Moot — the data cannot be acquired lawfully by anyone positioned to trade on it.
triage.dollar_test: ROKU ~$70-90 moves $12-20 — irrelevant; there is no obtainable instrument-feeding dataset, so friction never enters.
triage.reason: Ownership moat means the data is unobtainable by a trader, and the owner trading on it is the App Annie MNPI violation. Fails at acquisition.

triage.name: Quote-Engine Rate & Conversion Panel
triage.data_exists: Quotes are scrapable, but the two most valuable things are unavailable: rate changes are filed publicly (SERFF) and heavily telegraphed, and conversion/bind (the actual demand response) cannot be observed from synthetic quotes you never bind. You capture quoted price only.
triage.lead: Tiny-to-none. PGR discloses MONTHLY (e.g., June results on July 15; April on May 20) the actual net premiums written, PIF, and combined ratio — the real numbers, at ~20-day latency, from the company itself. Your panel proxies the price half that is already public via filings, and cannot see the conversion half that is the real unknown.
triage.dollar_test: PGR ~$240 x 5-8% = $12-18; ALL $8-14 vs ~1-2c spread — raw dollar test passes. Not the binding constraint.
triage.reason: Measures public, telegraphed price and is blind to conversion; PGR's own near-real-time monthly release removes any lead.

triage.name: Cruise Booking-Curve Nowcast
triage.data_exists: Per-sailing price/availability is scrapable, but this is an established, commoditized alt-data category with multiple vendors selling cruise-pricing panels. Displayed availability is revenue-managed (scarcity display, category throttling), not true remaining inventory, so occupancy reconstruction is invalid — and ships already run ~100%+ double occupancy, so occupancy is not where the surprise lives.
triage.lead: Thin. The yield surprise is price and onboard spend; onboard you cannot see (upsell package price is a weak proxy), and forward pricing strength is pre-announced qualitatively every quarter ('booked ahead of last year at record pricing').
triage.dollar_test: RCL ~$230 x 5-10% = $12-23; CCL $1.50-3 vs pennies — raw dollar test passes. Not the binding constraint.
triage.reason: Commoditized panel; true occupancy and onboard spend are unobservable, and forward pricing is telegraphed. Crowded with no residual edge.

triage.name: Resale-Premium & Sellout Velocity
triage.data_exists: Secondary prices and on-sale depletion are scrapable, but the signal doesn't map to LYV's P&L: resale premium accrues to StubHub/scalpers, not to Live Nation's recognized revenue, and concert-segment AOI margin is razor-thin so ticket volume barely flows to profit.
triage.lead: None worth harvesting. Sellouts and hot tours are reported in the press in real time (ordinary news beats the panel). Meanwhile the stock is currently dominated by the DOJ/Ticketmaster antitrust breakup overhang, which swamps any concert-demand nowcast — a correct demand read need not move the stock your way.
triage.dollar_test: LYV ~$140 x 5-10% = $7-14 vs ~1-3c spread — raw dollar test passes. Not the binding constraint.
triage.reason: Press reports sellouts instantly, resale premium doesn't accrue to LYV revenue, and the DOJ overhang dominates the tape.

triage.name: Used-Vehicle Listing-Velocity Panel
triage.data_exists: VIN inventory is scrapable, but Carvana inventory-velocity scraping is the canonical, most-crowded single-name alt-data trade — every fund and vendor already tracks days-to-sale, markdown cadence, and VIN counts. And it is structurally GPU-blind: ~$1,800/unit (roughly a third of total GPU, and the key swing factor) comes from gain-on-loan-sales/securitization, which is invisible to listings. A vanished VIN is also ambiguous (sale vs inter-hub transfer vs pull).
triage.lead: None over the crowd — the signal is fully arbitraged by the time you compute it.
triage.dollar_test: CVNA ~$250-350 x 20-30% = $50-100 vs pennies — raw dollar test passes enormously. Not the binding constraint.
triage.reason: The most-crowded scrape in the market, and finance GPU (the actual earnings swing factor) is not visible in inventory data.

triage.name: Theme-Park Wait-Time Panel
triage.data_exists: Wait times are already FREE and public — queue-times.com offers a free API with data back to 2014, and thrill-data/themeparks.wiki already publish crowd calendars. There is no data moat. The wait-to-attendance link is also broken: Disney actively manages posted waits via ride uptime, staffing, virtual queues, and Lightning Lane, so posted minutes are decoupled from crowd size.
triage.lead: None — the raw data is public and already converted into crowd calendars by free sites, and Parks is only one DIS segment (the stock is driven by DTC/streaming/linear, diluting attribution).
triage.dollar_test: DIS ~$110 x 5-9% = $6-10, but only a fraction attributable to a parks read vs pennies of friction. Raw dollar test passes; attribution and exclusivity do not.
triage.reason: Data is free and public, wait-to-attendance calibration is operator-manipulated, and parks is a minority driver of DIS. No edge.

triage.name: Carrier-Switch Net-Adds Nowcast
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 1 (Data Reality — not obtainable); plus disqualifying legal (App Annie)
triage.data_exists: No — not obtainable by a trader. On-device carrier-change telemetry exists only for whoever owns the SDK/device panel; the idea itself calls it an ownership moat that 'cannot be licensed by a rival.' The party that does hold it using that consented device telemetry to inform telco trades is precisely the App Annie 10b-5 fact pattern the SEC charged.
triage.lead: Moot — no acquirable dataset for a trader, and the owner trading on it crosses the App Annie line.
triage.dollar_test: TMUS ~$220 moves $7-13 — irrelevant; no obtainable feed, so friction never enters.
triage.reason: Ownership moat renders the data unobtainable by a trader, and the SDK owner trading on it is the App Annie MNPI violation. Fails at acquisition.

triage.name: Menu-Price Comp Decomposition
triage.data_exists: Yes. Menu prices are public on brand sites and delivery apps (DoorDash/UberEats), scrapeable daily. Already commercialized (Datassential and numerous delivery-platform price trackers), so not exclusive.
triage.lead: No usable lead. Menu pricing is the management-TELEGRAPHED, guided half of comps ('low-to-mid single-digit pricing' is literally issued as guidance). The comp SURPRISE is driven by TRAFFIC, which is absent from menu-price data. You would nowcast the part the market already knows and still need a separate traffic panel (the idea admits this) — and that credit-card/foot-traffic panel is the real, already-crowded product.
triage.dollar_test: CMG ~$55, a comps beat/miss moves 6-10% = $3.30-5.50/share; MCD ~$300 moves $9-15. Versus $0.01 tick + ~1-2c spread this passes the narrow dollar test by orders of magnitude. But the move is driven by the traffic component the scrape does not capture, so the large dollar move is not harvestable from this signal.
triage.reason: Passes the tick/spread dollar test easily but fails on lead: price is the guided, low-variance input; traffic is the surprise driver and is not in the data. Menu-price scraping is also a commoditized product.

triage.name: Auto-Insurance Quote-Engine Rating-Cell Scraper
triage.data_exists: Yes. Live quotes are scrapeable, though multi-step flows with captchas/session logic are hard. Filed rates are already public via SERFF.
triage.lead: No. Two independent kills: (a) Progressive REPORTS MONTHLY — net premiums written, combined ratio, and policies-in-force straight from the company (verified: e.g., 'Progressive Reports June 2026 Results,' reported ~July 15) — so a weekly quote scrape does not beat the issuer's own monthly print. (b) The combined-ratio SURPRISE is driven by LOSSES (accident frequency/severity, catastrophes, reserve development, social inflation), not by rate. Rate is slow, telegraphed, and public via SERFF; quote data measures the least-surprising input.
triage.dollar_test: PGR ~$240 moves 5-8% = $12-19/share on a combined-ratio surprise; TRV ~$260 similar. Versus $0.01 tick + ~2-4c spread this clears the narrow dollar test. But the surprise driver (losses) is not in quote data and PGR's own monthly disclosure front-runs the scrape.
triage.reason: Dollar move dwarfs frictions, but the informational lead collapses: the issuer publishes monthly, and the metric that moves the stock (loss trend) is not what quotes measure.

triage.name: Multifamily Asking-Rent & Concession Crawler
triage.data_exists: Yes, but a near-identical PUBLIC product already exists: Zillow's ZORI is a free, monthly, ZIP-level, dollar-denominated asking-rent index with a dedicated Multi-Family series (verified, updated ~16th monthly). Plus Apartment List, CoStar, RealPage, Yardi Matrix. Not exclusive.
triage.lead: Weak. The claimed 'asking-minus-concession' edge is exactly ZORI's domain, and like ZORI it is ASKING not executed rent — same limitation the idea tries to sell as a moat. REIT same-store revenue is slow and heavily guided on prior-quarter blended rates; the market already tracks public rent indices.
triage.dollar_test: AVB ~$200 moves 3-6% = $6-12/share; MAA ~$150 similar. Versus $0.01 tick + ~3-5c spread this passes the narrow dollar test. But there is no exclusive lead over free public indices, so the move is not attributable to this scrape.
triage.reason: Fails on crowding/commoditization — a free public asking-rent index (ZORI) plus several paid vendors already deliver the same signal — and provides no differentiated lead.

triage.name: Cruise Per-Diem Booking-Curve Scraper
triage.data_exists: Yes. The sailing x cabin x date price matrix is scrapeable, though multi-million-cell de-duping across OTAs is heavy.
triage.lead: There is a genuine STRUCTURAL lead (cruises book 6-12 months out), but sell-side cruise-pricing surveys are a long-standing weekly/monthly staple, so the market already tracks scraped cruise pricing — no exclusivity. Worse, scraped GROSS brochure fare is not NET per-diem (net of discounts, onboard credits, non-commissionable fares) and excludes onboard revenue and cost-per-ALBD; occupancy inferred from price velocity is noisy.
triage.dollar_test: RCL ~$230 moves 6-12% = $14-27/share on a yield surprise; CCL ~$25 moves $1.25-2.50. Versus $0.01 tick + ~5-10c spread this passes the narrow dollar test. But gross price != net yield and the pricing signal is already surveyed by the Street.
triage.reason: Best structural lead of the batch, but killed by crowding (established sell-side pricing surveys) and a loose gross-price-to-net-yield mapping that breaks the mechanism.

triage.name: Parcel Rate-Card & Surcharge Yield Model
triage.data_exists: Yes. Rate cards and surcharge tables are public PDFs.
triage.lead: None. GRIs are ANNOUNCED via newswire/press release months ahead — the 5.9% 2026 headline hit PRNewswire the day UPS/FedEx announced (verified) — so the market learns it instantly. And published rate != REALIZED yield: the majority of parcel volume rides customer-specific negotiated discounts, and mix plus discount escalators drive the yield management actually discusses. The rate card tells you almost nothing about the yield print.
triage.dollar_test: UPS ~$130 moves 5-9% = $6.50-12/share; FDX ~$270 moves $16-27. Versus $0.01 tick + ~2-3c spread this passes the narrow dollar test. But the input is a public wire number that does not map to realized yield, so there is no edge to monetize.
triage.reason: The signal is a press-release headline (no lead) and the published rate diverges structurally from realized yield (broken mechanism). Both kill it independently.

triage.name: Fiber Serviceability Footprint Crawler
triage.data_exists: Partly public. The FCC National Broadband Map / Broadband Data Collection publishes address-level serviceability from ISPs twice a year (verified); providers also issue explicit homes-passed guidance and multi-year build targets.
triage.lead: Weak. Homes-passed is a slow, GUIDED metric (AT&T and peers guide to fiber-locations-passed targets). The stock-moving SURPRISE is broadband NET ADDS, which turns on take rate, competition, and promo intensity — none captured by serviceability flips. National address-grid crawling to detect marginal weekly homes-passed is very noisy.
triage.dollar_test: CHTR ~$350 moves 6-12% = $21-42/share on a broadband-add surprise; T ~$27 moves $1-2. Versus $0.01 tick + ~5-10c spread this passes the narrow dollar test. But the surprise driver (net adds/take rate) is not measured and homes-passed is guided, so the move is not attributable to this signal.
triage.reason: Passes the dollar test but fails on lead: it measures a guided, partly-public input (homes passed) rather than the subscriber-add/take-rate variable that actually moves the stock.

triage.name: Markdown-Cadence Gross-Margin Nowcast
triage.data_exists: Yes, but retail price/promo tracking is one of the MOST commoditized alt-data categories — DataWeave, EDITED, and numerous retail-focused vendors sell SKU-level markdown depth/breadth. Not exclusive.
triage.lead: Weak to none. Promo tracking is ubiquitous across sell side and buy side. Gross margin also depends on far more than markdowns — product cost, freight, FX, channel mix, shrink — so markdown breadth/depth is only a noisy partial proxy for the GM print.
triage.dollar_test: LULU ~$300 moves 8-15% = $24-45/share on a GM/inventory surprise; TJX ~$120 moves $5-8. Versus $0.01 tick + ~5-10c spread this passes the narrow dollar test. But the signal is commoditized and mechanistically incomplete, so the move is not a proprietary edge.
triage.reason: Fails on crowding — markdown/promo scraping is a mature, widely-sold product — and the mechanism is only a partial driver of gross margin.

triage.name: Dealer New-Vehicle Inventory & Incentive Scraper
triage.data_exists: Yes, but the owner of the listing marketplaces publishes the answer for free: Cox Automotive (Autotrader/KBB/vAuto/Dealer.com) releases MONTHLY days-supply and inventory reports publicly (verified: e.g., 'Days' Supply Falls in March... June days' supply 80'), and KBB/Cox publish average transaction price and incentive data monthly; J.D. Power publishes incentive spend.
triage.lead: Weak. Days-supply and incentive intensity are public monthly from Cox; gross-per-unit is also management-discussed. The scrape offers only a marginal timing edge over free public monthly releases.
triage.dollar_test: LAD ~$300 moves 6-11% = $18-33/share; AN ~$180 moves $9-16; GM ~$50 moves $2-4. Versus $0.01 tick + ~3-8c spread this passes the narrow dollar test. But the underlying data is largely public monthly, so there is little exclusive information to trade.
triage.reason: Dollar move is fine, but the data is substantially public (Cox Automotive's own monthly reports), gutting the lead and exclusivity.

triage.name: Quota-Carrying Sales-Capacity Nowcast
triage.data_exists: Yes, but job-posting/headcount data is a commoditized alt-data category — Revelio Labs, LinkUp, Live Data Technologies, Thinknum, Coresignal all sell hiring/headcount signals with role classification. Not exclusive.
triage.lead: Weak and very noisy. AE headcount -> new-ARR with a claimed 2-4 quarter ramp is a long-and-variable-lag, heavily confounded signal: postings != filled seats; attrition, rep productivity, pricing, and macro all intervene. Low signal-to-noise, and the crowd already buys headcount data.
triage.dollar_test: CRM ~$250 moves 6-12% = $15-30/share on a bookings/guide surprise; NOW ~$900 moves $45-90. Versus $0.01 tick + ~5-15c spread this passes the narrow dollar test. But the predictive link from postings to the bookings print is weak and lagged, so the large move is not reliably capturable.
triage.reason: Fails on commoditization (headcount data is widely sold) and on a weak, noisy, long-lag mechanism; the dollar move is real but not tied tightly enough to this signal.

triage.name: Colo Availability & Power-Sold-Out Crawler
triage.data_exists: Yes, but datacenterHawk publishes quarterly metro vacancy/absorption/pricing (verified: 'U.S. colocation vacancy... 1.2% in Q1 2026, most new supply already pre-leased, landlord pricing power'), and CBRE/JLL/Avison Young publish the same. The scarcity story is mainstream consensus.
triage.lead: None differentiated. The AI-datacenter-shortage / pricing-power thesis for EQIX/DLR is the single most crowded market theme of 2025-26 and is fully priced. Availability pages do not cleanly map to bookings, and reported utilization is guided.
triage.dollar_test: EQIX ~$850 moves 5-9% = $42-76/share on a bookings/utilization surprise; DLR ~$170 moves $7-14. Versus $0.01 tick + ~10-20c spread this passes the narrow dollar test. But the theme is consensus and the signal is public/quarterly, so there is no under-priced information to harvest.
triage.reason: Passes the dollar test but fails on crowding: the 'power sold out' narrative is a fully-priced consensus trade with public quarterly availability data (datacenterHawk/CBRE/JLL). No proprietary lead.

triage.name: Vol-Control De-Risk Cascade
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (informational lead); also Filter 5 and Filter 7
triage.data_exists: YES — realized vol from index prints, target-vol bands from prospectuses, AUM from N-PORT/NAIC. But the reconstruction is not private: Nomura QIS (McElligott), Deutsche Bank and Goldman publish the aggregate vol-control + CTA de-allocation notional to their entire client base daily.
triage.lead: NONE. Verified: McElligott broadcasts explicit figures (e.g. a -3.0% close implies ~ -$62.9bn US-equity de-allocation) to thousands of clients the same evening. The 'moat reconstruction' IS the widely-distributed sell-side product; the whole desk sees the identical forced-flow estimate at the same time.
triage.dollar_test: PASSES in isolation but irrelevant: ES 0.5-1.5% = 27-82 pts = $1,350-$4,100/contract vs ~$16 round-trip. Dollars are real; the problem is everyone holds the identical signal simultaneously so the move is priced before you can act.
triage.reason: The consensus systematic-flow narrative — maximally crowded. You are also providing liquidity into a price-insensitive stress selloff (catching a falling knife); the 'symmetric re-leverage' is compensation for real gap/path risk (Filter 5), not free money. No lead over the broadcast, no uncrowded entry.

triage.name: Buffer-ETF FLEX Roll Front-Run
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 3 (dollar test) and Filter 4 (cost stack); also Filter 7
triage.data_exists: YES — daily holdings and outcome-period calendars are published by Innovator/First Trust/Allianz/Calamos. But FLEX options are OTC, negotiated bilaterally with a single dealer, so the reset leaves no lit SPX-book footprint to front-run at those strikes.
triage.lead: Weak/none in tradeable form. Reset dates are public weeks ahead, but the roll is transacted off-exchange dealer-to-fund, so the 'strike-level demand curve' never hits the screen you would trade against.
triage.dollar_test: FAILS on the real instrument. Claimed edge is vega on ~1-year SPX options: $4-22/contract for a 0.5-1.5 vol-pt shift — but 1-year SPX option bid-ask is routinely $1.00-$5.00+ wide (not the $0.10-0.50 asserted), so the spread eats the entire edge. The SPY analog ($0.30-0.80 vs $0.02) requires isolating a sub-vol-point skew wiggle from one fund inside massive SPY option flow — undetectable.
triage.reason: The purported vol/skew dislocation is smaller than the realistic bid-ask on the long-dated SPX contracts you must trade, and the actual roll is OTC with no lit footprint. Sub-spread edge = arithmetic, not economics.

triage.name: Income-ETF Call-Write Roll Pin
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 1 (data reality) and Filter 7 (crowded); also Filter 2
triage.data_exists: PARTIAL/NO for the dominant AUM. Verified: the two largest funds (JEPI + JEPQ, ~two-thirds of the ~$90B) do NOT write listed index options — they buy OTC equity-linked notes (unsecured bank debt from JPM/GS/Citi/RBC) with undisclosed strikes/terms. The dealer's hedge is internal and cannot be reconstructed from public holdings. Only QYLD/XYLD/RYLD write listed index calls, and their schedule/moneyness is fully public.
triage.lead: NONE. For QYLD/XYLD the write rule is a documented third-Friday ATM roll everyone knows; for JEPI/JEPQ the strikes are unobservable, so there is nothing precise to front-run.
triage.dollar_test: Moot. NQ 0.3-0.8% = 60-160 pts = $1,200-$3,200 would clear the $12 cost IF the pin existed and were mappable — but the net-gamma-by-strike surface cannot be built when the majority of the notional is OTC ELNs. Cannot size the edge.
triage.reason: The 'net dealer gamma surface' rests on strikes that are not disclosed for the bulk of the complex, and the reconstructable part (QYLD/XYLD) is a relabeled, broadcast GEX/short-vol trade. Data reality fails.

triage.name: Treasury Futures Roll Congestion
triage.data_exists: YES — OI migration and CFTC TFF positioning are public and timely.
triage.lead: NONE that is exploitable. OI migration and the long/short cohort imbalance are visible to every rates desk; the roll direction is common knowledge.
triage.dollar_test: PASSES arithmetically but the 'dislocation' is fair value. 1-3/32 = $31-94/contract vs $16-31 cost, but the calendar spread trades AT its implied-repo/carry fair value — the level is the financing rate, not a mispricing that reverts. The whoever takes the other side is paid balance-sheet/repo funding (rational, compensated).
triage.reason: The TY/US calendar roll is arbitraged continuously to implied-repo fair by every relative-value desk in the deepest market on earth, with CTD/delivery optionality priced in. There is no reversion to a 'true' level because the spread already is the true level. A documented financing premium, not free money.

triage.name: Auction Concession Cycle
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 5 (documented risk premium) and Filter 7 (commoditized); also Filter 2
triage.data_exists: YES — auction calendar/sizes and FR 2004 dealer positions are public (FR 2004 at multi-day latency).
triage.lead: NONE. The calendar is known to all; the concession is the market's compensation to dealers for absorbing supply — competed into fair by every primary dealer and RV fund.
triage.dollar_test: PASSES only in cherry-picked cases. TY DV01 ~ $65-70/bp, so a clean 1.5-3bp cheapen-then-richen path = $100-210 vs ~$16-31 cost — but empirically the concession is ~1-2bp, noisy, and absent in many auctions, so the cross-sectional MEAN net of the frequent no-path auctions and the competed-away premium is ~zero (Filter 6).
triage.reason: Auction concession is a decades-documented, textbook risk premium paid for underwriting supply — it is the compensation, not an anomaly. Fully anticipated, small, inconsistent, and competed to fair.

triage.name: Month-End Agg Duration Extension
triage.data_exists: YES, but as a PUBLISHED number, not a private computation. Verified: Bloomberg publishes a daily forward-looking Projected Universe for the Agg (and applies a T-2 month-end lockout), and index/rates desks broadcast the projected month-end extension to all clients well ahead of the last business day.
triage.lead: NONE. The 'moat is computing this month's extension' is false — the extension is a distributed, published figure. The month-end duration bid is the single most anticipated rates flow of the month, run by everyone.
triage.dollar_test: PASSES on dollars but the flow is pre-priced. TY DV01 ~ $70/bp, a 1-3bp richening into the close = $70-210/contract vs ~$16-31 cost — real dollars, but the pre-close richening is already front-run because the size/direction is public a week-plus out.
triage.reason: No informational lead over Bloomberg's Projected Universe and the desks that publish the extension; a maximally crowded month-end trade with the flow anticipated into the price.

triage.name: MSCI Inclusion-Factor Ladder
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 7 (crowded/commoditized) and Filter 6 (mean vs median / reversal); borderline
triage.data_exists: YES — float, ADV, foreign-room and size-segment data are obtainable; MSCI GIMI methodology is replicable and announcements land ~2 weeks before effective date.
triage.lead: Real but heavily competed. Methodology replication does give a lead over MSCI's ~2-week announcement, but dedicated index-arb desks run the identical GIMI prediction, so the lead is shared with the most sophisticated players.
triage.dollar_test: PASSES clearly — the ONE idea that unambiguously clears tick+spread: a predicted large add can move a $180 ADR 1-4% = $1.80-$7.20/share vs a $0.01 spread; even EEM/VWO clear a penny spread on a 0.3%+ move. Dollars are not the problem here.
triage.reason: Killed on crowding, not economics. Verified: index-change prediction is an explicitly competitive/crowded trade whose 'index effect' has decayed, and adds show post-inclusion REVERSAL (~2% pre-inclusion outperformance largely given back after), so a hold-into/through-the-effective-date book bleeds. You are competing head-to-head with specialist index-arb desks running the same replication. Fails Filter 7 despite passing the dollar test.

triage.name: Commodity Index January Reweight
triage.data_exists: YES, but the target weights are PUBLISHED, not something you must reverse-engineer. Verified: S&P Dow Jones released the full 2026 S&P GSCI Reference Percentage Dollar Weights on 6 Nov 2025 — the exact new weights are public ~2 months before the January reweight (BCOM likewise announced Nov 2025).
triage.lead: NONE. The 'moat is replicating the formula before the funds trade' collapses — S&P hands the market the final weights in November; no production-data archaeology is needed and everyone's screen shows the same target.
triage.dollar_test: PASSES on dollars but irrelevant: front WTI 0.5-1.5% = $0.35-1.05 on $70 oil = $350-1,050/contract vs ~$15 cost. Real dollars, zero informational edge — the reweight/roll flow is the most-studied commodity-index flow and is front-run by the entire complex.
triage.reason: The published November weights eliminate any reconstruction moat, and the January reweight flow is a textbook, commoditized trade anticipated for two months.

triage.name: Vanna-Charm OPEX Drift
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 1 (data reality) and Filter 2 (lead); also Filter 7
triage.data_exists: NO for the critical input. The listed OI surface exists, but the dealer book's SIGN — who is long vs short each strike — is an unobservable assumption, not data. The entire vanna/charm sign flips on a guessed dealer-vs-customer ownership split that is never disclosed.
triage.lead: NONE. The output is broadcast daily by multiple vendors (SpotGamma, Menthor Q) and sell-side (McElligott's vanna/charm notes). Maximally commoditized retail/prosumer narrative.
triage.dollar_test: PASSES only if the drift materializes: ES 0.5-1.5% = 27-82 pts = $1,350-$4,100/contract vs ~$16 cost — but this is a low-signal, regime-conditional estimate built on guessed positioning, so the realized mean is unreliable and often wrong-signed.
triage.reason: The reconstruction rests on unknowable dealer sign assumptions (data reality fails), the drift is weak and regime-dependent, and every vol vendor broadcasts the same estimate — no lead, deeply crowded.

triage.name: Month-End FX Hedge-Rebalance Fix
triage.data_exists: YES — hedged-ETF AUM, disclosed hedge ratios, and the month's cross-market return gap are all obtainable. But the flow model is already a broadcast product.
triage.lead: NONE. Verified: Barclays and Citi publish month-end fixing-model signals — explicit direction and strength by currency (e.g. 'USD buying, moderate vs EUR/AUD') — to clients ahead of the fix. The 'flow model is the work' is false; the street receives the same signal days early.
triage.dollar_test: PASSES on dollars but pre-priced: EUR/USD 10-40 pips = $125-500/contract vs ~$12 cost; 6J similar. Real dollars, but the post-2013-scandal fix window was widened to ~5 minutes (diffusing impact) and the whole street leans the same way from the same published signals, so it is front-run into the penultimate session.
triage.reason: No informational lead over Barclays/Citi month-end fix models, a famously crowded flow, and a deliberately widened fix window that dilutes the mechanical impact.

triage.name: AdCom Briefing-Book Reader
triage.data_exists: YES — FDA posts 100-300pp briefing packages to the meeting page ~2 U.S. business days before the panel, publicly and free.
triage.lead: None for a small trader. The PDF is public to EVERYONE at the ~2pm drop, not to you alone. Verified: stocks move ~15% within MINUTES of the drop; the claim that 'sell-side and retail take a day-plus' is false. Specialist biotech event funds refresh the same page with better NLP and co-located parsing.
triage.dollar_test: PASSES in isolation: a $40 AdCom name moving 10-40% on the doc is $4-16/share vs a 1-2c spread. The move is real and large — so filter 3 is NOT the killer here. The kill is that everyone captures the same move simultaneously.
triage.reason: This is one of the most crowded, most-watched event trades in all of biotech. The catalyst document is public to the entire market at a single instant and the price adjusts within minutes. There is no exclusive access and no reliable machine-vs-human latency edge; the marginal counterparty is a well-capitalized specialist desk. The 'subtle division-specific tone' alpha beyond the obvious summary/safety sections is marginal and arbitraged.

triage.name: FAERS Signal Front-Run
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (informational lead / no datable catalyst); mechanism failure
triage.data_exists: YES but degraded — FAERS quarterly files are public, lagged ~1 quarter, and notoriously dirty (duplicate patient/physician/manufacturer reports, free-text drug names).
triage.lead: Illusory. Verified: disproportionality (PRR/ROR) is prone to false positives at low counts; 'not every major postmarket drug safety action traces back to a FAERS statistical signal'; the FDA acts on an unpredictable timeline (1-4+ quarters, frequently never). You cannot date the catalyst, and when action lands it hits FDA safety communications/wires simultaneously.
triage.dollar_test: A black-box warning or withdrawal is $10-30/share on a $100 name — passes IF and WHEN it fires. But with no datable trigger, an options position bleeds theta for quarters against a low-base-rate event, and equity exposure has no defined horizon.
triage.reason: The signal-to-action link is weak, noisy, and slow. Most disproportionality flags never become regulatory actions, timing is unmodelable, and the effect is diffuse — so there is no clean binary to position around. When a real action occurs it is public via FDA safety communication and newswire at once. The 'moat' pharmacovigilance pipeline produces hypotheses, not a tradeable calendar.

triage.name: Star-Ratings Reconstructor
triage.data_exists: NO for the required inputs. Verified: CMS releases the measure-level data tables WITH the star ratings in early October, not before. Current-cycle per-contract measure data is not publicly obtainable ahead of the release, and the Tukey outlier-deletion cut-points depend on the full national distribution that no outsider can compute until CMS does. Plans see their own ratings only in a non-public preview window (MNPI).
triage.lead: The premise ('component measures knowable weeks-to-months before the composite') fails: the public component files drop simultaneously with the composite, and the cut-points/guardrails are unknowable ex ante. There is no public reconstruction path that beats the October print.
triage.dollar_test: The catalyst itself is real — Humana's Oct-2023 slip below 4 stars was ~19% / ~$50 on a ~$260 share vs a 1-2c spread — so filter 3 passes. But you cannot reach the trade because the inputs are not public before the release.
triage.reason: The idea dies at the data source, not the payoff. Faithfully replicating CMS methodology is worthless without the current-year measure inputs and the nationally-derived cut-points, none of which are public ahead of the October release. Any party that DID have them (the insurer, via preview) would be trading on material non-public information.

triage.name: NCD Coverage Clock
triage.data_exists: YES — the NCD tracking sheet, proposed decision memo, comment window, and final decision are all public on cms.gov on a statutory clock.
triage.lead: None on direction. The idea is backwards: the PROPOSED decision memo is itself the public, wire-covered catalyst (e.g., the April-2022 proposed Aduhelm CED-restriction NCD moved BIIB the same day). The final decision ~90 days later almost always matches the proposal and is largely a non-event. The statutory clock tells you WHEN a proposed memo may drop, but not its DIRECTION — and direction is what moves the stock, revealed to all at once.
triage.dollar_test: $6-15/share on a $60 diagnostic on a coverage grant/denial — real, so filter 3 is fine. But the move happens at the proposed-memo instant, public to the whole market; there is no residual edge to harvest at the final.
triage.reason: The market does not 'trade the final headline' — it trades the proposed memo, which is exactly as public and just as instantly disseminated. Front-running the final off the proposed is not an edge because the proposal already priced it. Parsing CED nuance seconds faster is a marginal, crowded claim.

triage.name: Embargo-Lift Abstract Scanner
triage.data_exists: YES — ASCO/ESMO/ASH/AHA/ACC titles ~1 week ahead; full abstracts at a precise, access-gated embargo-lift time.
triage.lead: None that is exclusive. The embargo-lift IS the catalyst and it is one of the most-watched moments in biotech; every specialist hits the same endpoint at the same instant, and sponsors routinely issue press releases AT the embargo lift. The 'humans take a day to skim' premise is false — the move is instantaneous. Access is also gated by an embargo agreement, creating legal friction on trading it.
triage.dollar_test: $6-18/share on a $30 name moving 20-60% — real, filter 3 passes. But the direction is disseminated to the entire credentialed crowd plus the company wire at the identical lift instant.
triage.reason: Maximally crowded and commoditized. The abstract release is the single most anticipated data moment of each congress; specialist funds and sell-side all parse it at the lift. No latency or access edge survives, and the sponsor's own PR removes any bulletin-vs-wire lead.

triage.name: CHMP Agenda Decoder
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (no lead over company wire); Filter 7/3 support
triage.data_exists: YES — the CHMP agenda posts days before the monthly meeting and the opinion lands in the EMA 'highlights' bulletin on the Friday of the meeting week.
triage.lead: None reliable. Verified: sponsors (Regeneron, BMS, Gilead, Valneva, Pfizer) issue their OWN press releases the same day as — frequently coincident with or ahead of — the EMA highlights, because the sponsor is notified of the opinion. The company wire, not the EMA bulletin, is the market's source, so there is no dependable minutes-to-hours edge. Which assets are up for opinion is also already largely public (MAA acceptance is announced).
triage.dollar_test: Squeezed on both ends. Liquid large-cap ADRs (NVS/AZN/GSK/SNY): one product opinion is a small fraction of a diversified name — often sub-$1/share and usually already expected (filter 3 weak). Mid-cap single-asset names that move 20-40% are largely foreign-listed/thin (filter 7).
triage.reason: The information reaches the market via the sponsor's own simultaneous press release, eliminating the claimed bulletin lead. Where the move is big enough to matter the instrument is foreign/illiquid; where the instrument is liquid the move is too small and pre-priced.

triage.name: FERC eLibrary Certificate Clock
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (covered specialist area; orders public); mechanism weakness; Filter 3 for large caps
triage.data_exists: YES — eLibrary carries filings, EIS documents, comment-close notices, and orders (clunky and poorly indexed, but public).
triage.lead: Weak.
