FERC certificate timing is NOT cleanly modelable: the flagship Mountain Valley/Equitrans saga was dominated by 4th Circuit vacaturs and ultimately resolved by CONGRESS (the 2023 debt-ceiling bill), not FERC's own clock — the real catalysts were courts and legislation, public to all. Energy event desks and dedicated FERC-watcher services already cover these dockets intensely.
triage.dollar_test: $1-12/share on a $10-40 project pure-play IF one exists — but pure-plays are largely gone (Equitrans was acquired by EQT in 2024). For diversified WMB/KMI/ET a single certificate is a small fraction of the name (filter 3 fails). So the big-dollar case has no vehicle and the liquid vehicle has no big-dollar case.
triage.reason: The order is public and the space is already worked by specialists; the statutory 'clock' has low predictive power because real outcomes turn on court and congressional action, not modelable NEPA milestones. The instruments that would move meaningfully are scarce or acquired.

triage.name: H.2 Bank-Merger Handicapper
triage.data_exists: YES — the Fed H.2 weekly, FDIC/OCC pipelines, and CRA-protest/comment filings are all public.
triage.lead: None against the marginal holder, who is a dedicated merger-arb desk staffed with ex-regulator counsel modeling the exact same Fed/FDIC/OCC/DOJ pipeline. The application cadence is public and already priced into the spread.
triage.dollar_test: The 3-8% spread on a $30 target is $0.90-2.40/share of gross — but a deal break costs 20-30% ($6-9). The spread is the risk premium: expected value after break probability is thin, and that thin residual IS the compensation, not free money.
triage.reason: Textbook merger arb — a well-documented, heavily-harvested risk premium. The other side is rational and is paid for genuine regulatory-break risk. A small trader has no informational or modeling edge over specialist arbs, and cannot diversify across enough simultaneous deals to earn the cross-sectional mean while surviving single breaks.

triage.name: Pesticide Docket Kill-Switch
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (wire coverage / no lead); materiality + datability failure
triage.data_exists: YES — registration-review dockets, PIDs, and risk assessments are public on regulations.gov.
triage.lead: Illusory. When an EPA action is material (chlorpyrifos and similar), the PID/risk assessment is wire-covered by Reuters and the ag press immediately — no lead. Timing is glacial and litigation/court-dominated (chlorpyrifos spanned decades and multiple court remands), not a clean datable binary.
triage.dollar_test: 3-8% on CTVA ($60) is $1.80-4.80/share IF a single active ingredient is material — but it rarely is: diversified majors (Corteva, Bayer, FMC) carry hundreds of products. The one franchise-level ag-chem catalyst of the era (glyphosate) came through LITIGATION (Roundup jury verdicts), not an EPA docket.
triage.reason: A single active-ingredient decision is seldom material to a diversified registrant; when it is material it is wire-covered instantly with no lead; and the timeline is dominated by courts and multi-year comment/reregistration processes, so there is no clean, datable, high-probability catalyst to front-run.

triage.name: PMTA Order Docket Tracker
triage.data_exists: Partial — federal court dockets/argument calendars are public (PACER); FDA does NOT publish granular per-application TPL/deficiency review status, so the claimed 'telegraphs by weeks' input is largely not obtainable.
triage.lead: None on direction. MDOs/MGOs and court rulings are public and wire-covered instantly (the 2022 Juul MDO was immediate news). A public docket calendar tells you a ruling DATE, not its DIRECTION, and it is equally visible to every event fund on PACER; when the order/ruling fires it is simultaneous to all.
triage.dollar_test: 3-10% on MO/BTI ($50) is $1.50-6/share vs a 1-2c spread — real, so filter 3 is fine. The kill is the absent lead: you learn the outcome at the same instant as the wire and the rest of the docket-watching crowd.
triage.reason: The submission-number-to-product mapping is a mild data-plumbing moat but confers no informational edge on the catalyst itself. Direction is revealed only when the FDA order or court ruling publishes, simultaneously to the whole market, and the granular pre-order status that might telegraph it is not publicly available.

triage.name: Catalog-Multiple Ticker
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (Informational Lead); also weak on 1 (cadence) and 6 (thin/heterogeneous data)
triage.data_exists: Partly. Royalty Exchange/SongVest/ANote closed auctions are public but clear tiny catalogs (~$5k-$500k) at sporadic, low cadence (dozens/yr), with heterogeneous royalty accounting. This is a noisy scatter, not a continuous 'multiple index.'
triage.lead: No usable lead. WMG/UMG equity is priced on streaming subs/ARPU growth and the majors' own large-catalog M&A, not on micro-cap auction clears. Headline catalog deals (Dylan, Springsteen, Queen) are reported by Billboard/press at announcement, so any large-multiple signal is public. Small-auction multiples do not foretell major-label re-rates.
triage.dollar_test: Claimed $3-6 SOTP shift on ~$35 WMG (1c tick, 2-4c spread) would nominally clear the stack, but the input->output causal chain is unproven, so the dollar move is not actually harvestable.
triage.reason: A different asset class (small private catalogs) mapped onto major-label equity through a broken causal chain, with no informational lead over public catalog-M&A comps. Thin, heterogeneous, sporadic data compounds the problem.

triage.name: Wholesale Lane Nowcast
triage.data_exists: Core feed is not publicly obtainable. Manheim/ADESA per-lot hammer prices sit behind dealer credentials; ACV/OPENLANE give only partial views, not the clean cross-platform lane universe the pitch needs. The public artifact is the Manheim MUVVI (5th business day + an explicit mid-month checkpoint that is NOT a directional flash estimate).
triage.lead: MUVVI is a trusted, closely-watched benchmark; sell-side tracks wholesale used prices obsessively and watches it ahead of used-car CPI. A private daily index buys at most a days-ahead read that the mid-month checkpoint largely closes, and CVNA GPU depends on retail spread/inventory/finance, not wholesale cost alone.
triage.dollar_test: $500/unit wholesale swing -> ~$300-400 GPU delta; CVNA can move several dollars on a ~$200+ stock (1c tick, 5-10c spread) — magnitude passes, but the price feed required to generate the signal is credential-gated and not public.
triage.reason: The lane-level price feed that would create the edge is behind dealer paywalls (not publicly obtainable), and the public MUVVI is already the market's watched benchmark, so there is no clean, obtainable lead.

triage.name: NdPr Shadow Price
triage.data_exists: Yes. Asian Metal / SMM / Baotou publish daily NdPr oxide and metal quotes (subscription), and the same prices are relayed same-day by Fastmarkets, Argus and Reuters.
triage.lead: None. NdPr is THE headline rare-earth price and MP/Lynas are the direct equity proxies analysts explicitly model off it; the Chinese prints hit Western terminals same-day. MP's larger moves come from DoD offtake/price-floor and tariff/policy news, not from an 'underweighted' NdPr fixing.
triage.dollar_test: 10% NdPr move (~$6-7/kg) -> MP $1-3 on a ~$15-30 stock (1c tick, 2-3c spread). Magnitude is fine, but the price is public and already embedded, so the dollar move is not front-runnable.
triage.reason: Widely-published, obsessively-tracked benchmark; the 'US investors underweight the Chinese print' premise is false. No informational lead.

triage.name: Guangzhou Night Tape
triage.data_exists: Premise is fabricated. GFEX runs NO night session for lithium carbonate — night trading is only under study and only for platinum/palladium. The '~21:00-23:00 CST night tape that closes before the US open' does not exist. GFEX day-session LC futures and SMM spot are real and, since July 2026, open to overseas traders and widely tracked (Fastmarkets, Bloomberg).
triage.lead: There is no overnight lithium lead because there is no overnight lithium session. The day-session tape is on every commodity terminal, and ALB/SQM realized prices are contract/index-based, decoupled from daily spot.
triage.dollar_test: Even granting 5% -> ~$1-3 ALB gap on a ~$70-90 stock (1c tick, 3-5c spread), the settled 'night tape' you would trade the US open against does not exist as a trigger.
triage.reason: The named data source (a GFEX lithium night session) does not exist; day-session prices are public and widely tracked. Fails data reality outright.

triage.name: Get-In Premium Panel
triage.data_exists: Yes. StubHub/SeatGeek/Vivid/Viagogo get-in prices and listing depth are scrapeable, though noisy, bot-laden, and hard to back-fill face price on.
triage.lead: Weak. LYV concert/ticketing AOI is driven by show count, primary Ticketmaster volume, sponsorship and on-site spend; resale premium is a minor, noisy slice. Tour grosses and on-sale results are reported by Pollstar/Billboard, and sell-side already runs tour-tracker / 'brand heat' notes, so no exclusive lead to a specific print.
triage.dollar_test: Claimed $3-8 on a ~$90-150 LYV (1c tick, 3-6c spread) is large, but attributing a print to a resale-premium index is unproven — the harvestable, attributable dollar move is speculative.
triage.reason: Resale premium is a weak, noisy proxy for LYV's actual revenue drivers, with no clean lead to a specific print; near-daily scraping of the same tours also produces heavily overlapping, non-independent observations.

triage.name: Barge-and-Tampa Netback
triage.data_exists: Yes but subscription-gated. Green Markets / Profercy / Argus report NOLA urea/UAN barge clears and the Tampa ammonia monthly settlement; these are among the most-cited fertilizer benchmarks.
triage.lead: None. CF/NTR/MOS analysts track NOLA barge weekly and treat the Tampa settlement as a headline event; Bloomberg/trade press disseminate both immediately. The 'US holders underweight barge microstructure' claim is false for these single-commodity price-times-volume names.
triage.dollar_test: $50/ton nitrogen move -> CF $3-6 on a ~$80-100 stock (1c tick, 3-5c spread). Magnitude passes, but the benchmark is public and already the consensus modeling input, so no front-runnable edge.
triage.reason: NOLA barge and Tampa ammonia are the closely-watched public benchmarks for exactly these stocks; no informational lead over the wire.

triage.name: Pre-IPO Mark Arbitrage
triage.data_exists: Secondary marks (Caplight/Forge/NPM/EquityZen/Hiive) exist but are thin, access-gated and conflicting; the biggest rounds (SpaceX, Stripe, OpenAI) are reported near-immediately by The Information/Bloomberg.
triage.lead: The premise that DXYZ re-rates toward NAV is broken. Verified: DXYZ trades as a sentiment-driven CEF unmoored from NAV — roughly 2,000% premium at launch, later swinging to steep discounts — driven by retail lottery demand, ATM-offering overhang and short positioning, not by NAV marks.
triage.dollar_test: Even a multi-dollar NAV shift on a ~$25-50 DXYZ (1c tick, but 10-20c+ spread, thin) is swamped by premium/discount swings that dwarf NAV moves; the 'gap to NAV' does not mean-revert, so there is nothing to harvest.
triage.reason: Documented lottery-demand / sentiment premium: DXYZ price is decoupled from NAV, so the secondary-mark -> NAV -> price arbitrage does not hold. Compounded by a thin, wide-spread instrument.

triage.name: Resale Heat Index
triage.data_exists: Yes. StockX/GOAT/eBay SKU last-sale, bid/ask and volume are scrapeable — and StockX-based demand signals are already sold by multiple alt-data vendors.
triage.lead: Weak and commoditized. NKE/DECK revenue is dominated by wholesale/DTC volume, inventory and China, not by hype-SKU resale premium. Resale-based 'brand heat' is a well-known, widely-sold read with no exclusive lead.
triage.dollar_test: Claimed NKE $2-5 on a ~$70-100 stock (1c tick, 2-4c spread) is only nominal; the resale-premium -> reported-revenue link is loose, so the attributable, harvestable move is small and uncertain.
triage.reason: Resale premium is a weak proxy for the actual print, and the signal is already commoditized across alt-data vendors — no exclusive informational lead.

triage.name: Lease-Rate-Factor Mark
triage.data_exists: No high-cadence public feed. Lease-rate factors and current-market-value appraisals (Ishka / Cirium-Ascend / IBA) are subscription-gated AND sticky — appraised values update quarterly/annually, not continuously. The 'continuous repricing' premise is false.
triage.lead: Lessor book marks lagging the transaction market is a known, priced feature; AER trades largely on capital returns/buybacks, and the market already discounts book-mark lag. There is no fast, obtainable signal to front-run.
triage.dollar_test: A 5% CMV shift could move AER NAV several dollars on a ~$90-110 stock (1c tick, 4-8c spread), but the underlying appraisals do not move fast enough or publicly enough to trade ahead of the print.
triage.reason: Data is gated and low-cadence (aircraft appraisals are not continuous), and the book-mark lag is a widely-understood, already-priced feature. Fails data reality.

triage.name: Rate-on-Line Precursor
triage.data_exists: Cat-bond primary spreads, weekly dealer secondary runs, and UCITS ILS-fund NAVs exist, but dealer runs are gated and weekly. Meanwhile industry cat-loss estimates (Verisk, Moody's RMS, Karen Clark) are published fast and publicly.
triage.lead: Backwards. After a catastrophe, RNR/EG/ACGL move same-day on the event and public cat-loss estimates; weekly cat-bond secondary marks LAG the equity rather than lead it. Renewal rate-on-line trajectory is heavily covered by sell-side into Jan-1/mid-year.
triage.dollar_test: An RoL inflection could move RNR $5-12 on a ~$200-260 stock (1c tick, 5-15c spread) — magnitude passes, but the equity has already moved on the wire before the ILS marks print.
triage.reason: Event and cat-loss information hits the wire and repriced reinsurer equity same-day; ILS secondary marks lag it. Also a documented catastrophe risk premium, not free money. No lead.

triage.name: Kiln Glow Index
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (informational lead / mechanism mismatch); also Filter 1 (cadence)
triage.data_exists: Partly. Landsat-8/9 TIRS is 100m thermal on an 8-16 day combined revisit that cloud degrades further; Sentinel-3 SLSTR is daily but 1km resolution (too coarse to isolate a single kiln); ASTER is on-demand. Imagery is public but too sparse and cloud-broken to reconstruct continuous kiln burn-hours.
triage.lead: Claimed 3-8 weeks ahead of quarterly volume, but the lead is to the wrong variable.
triage.dollar_test: VMC ~$270, 1-cent tick, 2-5 cent spread; claim is to capture $2-4/share pre-drift on an $11-22 print move. Verified: VMC/MLM are ~70% aggregates companies whose earnings surprise is driven by aggregate PRICING (compounding 6-8%/yr) and mix, not cement clinker tonnage; cement is a small downstream segment. For pure-cement names (EXP, CX) the print is dominated by price and energy cost. So a clinker-tonnage nowcast targets a line item that is not the swing factor — the predictable dollar move is near zero, not $2-4.
triage.reason: Instrument/mechanism mismatch: the signal measures cement clinker, but VMC/MLM print on aggregates volume and pricing, and pure-cement names print on price/energy spread. No clean lead to the actual return driver, and thermal cadence cannot produce continuous burn-hours anyway.

triage.name: Brine Bloom
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 5 (already a lithium-price macro premium) + Filter 2 (no lead to the price driver)
triage.data_exists: Yes. Sentinel-2 (10m, 5-day) and PlanetScope cover the ponds; pond-stage monitoring is real and already commercialized as a satellite alt-data product.
triage.lead: Claimed 2-4 quarters ahead of production, but production is guided and stable — not the variable that moves the stock.
triage.dollar_test: ALB ~$95, 1-cent tick, 3-8 cent spread; claim is $1.50-3/share capture. Verified: ALB and SQM move on lithium SPOT PRICE — the 2022-2025 price collapse drove ALB into outright losses despite stable volumes. Company production is guided and low-variance; a pond-derived volume nowcast is orthogonal to (and if anything, via added supply, negatively correlated with) the lithium price that drives the equity. The harvestable pre-print dollar edge from the company's own marginal volume is small; the real variance is macro lithium spot.
triage.reason: The instruments are lithium-price bets (a known, already-harvested commodity/distress premium). A production-volume lead does not front-run the price driver and can be perversely bearish (more visible supply = lower price).

triage.name: Shop-Visit Clock
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (no lead — air traffic is the most-watched real-time series) + Filter 7 (crowded)
triage.data_exists: Yes, genuinely. ADS-B is public and real-time via FlightRadar24, ADS-B Exchange, OAG, Cirium; tail-to-engine registries exist. This is the most defensible data layer of the ten.
triage.lead: Effectively none. Global flight-hours by engine type are tracked in real time by every sell-side aero desk (Cirium/OAG/IATA); airlines report monthly traffic.
triage.dollar_test: GE ~$210, 1-cent tick, 2-4 cent spread; claim is 'multiple dollars' capture. Verified: 40%+ of GE services revenue is under LTSAs recognized over time on a cost-incurred basis with flight-hour billing — an annuity-like, smoothed stream, so flight-hours do NOT translate into a sharp same-quarter aftermarket surprise. Combined with zero informational lead on traffic, the predictable pre-print dollar edge is near zero despite a real $8-15 print move.
triage.reason: Air traffic / flight-hours are among the most-watched real-time datasets, so there is no informational lead; LTSA accounting smooths aftermarket revenue so hours do not map to a quarter's surprise; and the trade is crowded.

triage.name: Pit Pulse
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 7 (crowded/commercialized) + Filter 2 (grade invisible; stocks print on copper price)
triage.data_exists: Partly. Sub-meter tasking (SkySat/Maxar) plus Umbra/ICEYE SAR is expensive but obtainable. Critically, ORE tonnage is visible but GRADE and recovery — which dominate contained-copper output — are invisible from space, so tons-moved does not convert to metal produced.
triage.lead: Claimed 4-8 weeks, but to a variable (tonnage) that is neither the metal-output driver nor the stock driver.
triage.dollar_test: FCX ~$45, 1-cent tick, 2-3 cent spread; claim $2.25-4/share. Verified: FCX Q2'26 copper sales volume fell ~30% yet earnings rose ~37% because copper PRICE dominates; the equity is a macro copper-price bet. Copper futures moves cited ($1,250-3,750/contract) are price-driven macro events, not something a mine-tonnage nowcast reliably front-runs. And the signal is already sold commercially (RS Metrics markets a 3-month-ahead CME copper predictive product; Orbital Insight/Ursa serve commodity funds).
triage.reason: Commercialized/crowded satellite mine-monitoring; grade invisibility breaks the tons-to-metal conversion; and FCX/SCCO/HG are driven by the copper price (macro), not the miner's marginal quarterly tonnage.

triage.name: Fifty-Hertz Tap
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 1 (the signal does not physically contain the claimed information; plus infeasible in-country deployment)
triage.data_exists: The mains-frequency monitoring technique (FNET/GridEye) is real academically, but the derived quantity the thesis needs does not exist in it. A synchronous grid is held to 50Hz by automatic generation control; frequency is stationary around nominal regardless of the LEVEL of load. Frequency deviation encodes instantaneous imbalance / ramp events, not provincial industrial-output level. Operating a physical logger fleet across Chinese industrial provinces also carries serious legal/operational risk.
triage.lead: Irrelevant — there is no reliable industrial-output level signal to lead with.
triage.dollar_test: SGX iron ore ~$105/t, 100t contract, $5 tick; claimed $300-800/contract moves are real market events but not predictable from this input. Because grid frequency does not measure load level, the expected harvestable directional move net of noise is approximately zero — you cannot size a dollar edge on a signal that does not carry the target variable.
triage.reason: Physics error: grid frequency, actively regulated to 50Hz, does not encode the level of industrial load — so the nowcast the thesis requires cannot be derived from it. The in-country hardware network is also legally/operationally infeasible.

triage.name: Cavern Creep
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 1 (coverage + cadence) + Filter 2 (pipeline-flow storage nowcasts already lead)
triage.data_exists: Partly. Sentinel-1 is free but 6-12 day revisit (degraded after S1B's 2021 failure until S1C in late 2024); mm-scale InSAR heave inversion to volume is very noisy. Verified: salt caverns are only ~7% of US working-gas capacity per EIA.
triage.lead: None that matters. The EIA weekly report is TOTAL working gas (mostly depleted reservoirs/aquifers); a 7% cavern slice cannot nowcast the market-moving total.
triage.dollar_test: NG ~$3.50, 10,000 MMBtu contract, $10 tick; claimed $1,000-3,000/contract surprise moves are real. But the harvestable edge is near zero: caverns are 7% of storage so you can't estimate the total EIA number, Genscape/Wood Mac/Criterion already nowcast EIA via pipeline-flow telemetry, and Reuters/Bloomberg analyst surveys are tight — the surprise you could predict is already largely priced. A 6-12 day InSAR cadence also cannot beat a weekly Thursday print.
triage.reason: Salt caverns are only ~7% of US storage capacity (cannot nowcast the total EIA number that moves NG); established pipeline-flow storage nowcasts plus tight consensus surveys already lead; InSAR revisit is too slow for a weekly print.

triage.name: Meltshop Heat
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (AISI weekly utilization is public; stocks print on steel price) + Filter 1 (plant-level power draw not obtainable)
triage.data_exists: Partly and asymmetrically. Thermal (Landsat TIRS/ECOSTRESS/Sentinel-3) is sparse and cloud-limited. The 'power draw' half is not publicly obtainable at plant level — US ISOs (MISO/PJM/ERCOT) publish nodal LMP PRICES, not a specific mill's physical MW load. The dual-source fusion the moat depends on cannot be assembled from public data.
triage.lead: None. AISI publishes weekly raw-steel capacity utilization by district every Monday — the market already has the near-real-time output proxy.
triage.dollar_test: NUE ~$140, 1-cent tick, 2-4 cent spread; claim $5.60-11/share. Verified: AISI weekly utilization is public, and Nucor issues mid-quarter EPS guidance, so the volume proxy is already in the market. The earnings/stock swing factor is HRC price and the metal spread, not NUE's volume (stable at high utilization). The predictable pre-print dollar edge from a volume nowcast is small and already competed away.
triage.reason: AISI releases weekly capacity utilization publicly (no lead), plant-level power telemetry is not public (only nodal prices), and NUE/STLD/CLF print on HRC price and spreads rather than their stable volumes.

triage.name: Yard-to-Deck
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (automakers self-report monthly volumes; thin lead) + Filter 7 (crowded; FX/mix drive the ADRs)
triage.data_exists: Yes. Sub-meter optical (Planet/Maxar) plus AIS berth/draft; port and vehicle counting is already a commercialized alt-data product. RoRo draft-to-units inversion is noisy, and one export port is a slice of a global automaker's volume.
triage.lead: Thin. Toyota/Honda/Hyundai report monthly production and sales themselves; JAMA/KAMA/Wards publish monthly industry data. A 2-5 week lead over self-reported data on a partial-coverage signal is weak.
triage.dollar_test: TM ADR ~$185, few-cent spread, claim $5.50-11; STLA ~$13, claim $0.50-1. But TM's quarterly print and its ADR are dominated by JPY/USD and mix/pricing, not marginal export unit counts — so a units-loaded nowcast does not map to the return driver. HYMTF is an illiquid pink sheet. The predictable dollar edge tied to the counted units is small relative to the FX/mix noise that actually moves the stock.
triage.reason: Automakers self-report monthly volumes (thin lead over a partial-coverage, already-commercialized port count), and the ADRs are driven by FX, mix, and pricing rather than the marginal export units the signal measures.

triage.name: Axle Ledger
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 1 (real-time WIM not obtainable; self-deploy infeasible) + Filter 2 (carriers self-report monthly; no carrier attribution)
triage.data_exists: No, not in the form required. State DOT WIM/continuous-count data exists but is typically published with a monthly-to-annual lag, not as a real-time national stream. Embedding one's own axle sensors in interstate pavement is not legally/operationally feasible for a trader. Crucially, a WIM sensor cannot tell an ODFL trailer from an Amazon or private carrier's — there is no carrier attribution.
triage.lead: Claimed 3-6 weeks, but there is no carrier-specific signal to lead with, and macro tonnage lags behind the carriers' own disclosures.
triage.dollar_test: ODFL ~$180, KNX ~$50, 1-cent ticks; claim $2-14/share. Verified: ODFL self-reports monthly LTL operating metrics (tons/day, revenue/cwt) plus mid-quarter updates — carrier-specific data straight from the source. National WIM tonnage cannot be attributed to a specific carrier, and LTL earnings are driven by yield/revenue-per-cwt (pricing), which axle weight does not see. The predictable carrier-specific pre-print dollar edge is effectively zero.
triage.reason: Real-time WIM feeds are not publicly obtainable and self-deploying interstate sensors is infeasible; a WIM axle count cannot be attributed to a named carrier; and carriers already self-report monthly metrics, with results driven by pricing/yield rather than raw tonnage.

triage.name: Reformer Runrate
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (stock is a nitrogen-price bet; outages disclosed fast) + Filter 5 (known commodity premium)
triage.data_exists: Partly. Thermal passes are sparse/cloud-limited and tank-car counts at plant yards are noisy; feasible in principle but not continuous.
triage.lead: Thin to nil. The thesis itself concedes only 'days ahead of price-agency confirmation,' but major unplanned outages are disclosed within days via company press releases and covered by Green Markets/ICIS/Profercy.
triage.dollar_test: CF ~$85, 1-cent tick, 2-4 cent spread; claim $4.25-8.50/share. CF runs near full utilization, so volume is low-variance; the earnings and stock swing factor is nitrogen/urea PRICE and the gas-price spread (Tampa ammonia, NOLA urea, Henry Hub), all macro. A production-run-rate nowcast is orthogonal to the price that drives the equity, and outages that do matter (because they tighten price) are announced quickly. The predictable pre-print dollar edge from the volume signal is small.
triage.reason: CF/NTR/MOS are nitrogen-price and gas-spread bets (a known, already-harvested commodity premium); volume is stable and material outages are disclosed rapidly by companies and price agencies, so there is no durable lead to the price driver.

triage.name: Sportsbook Structural-Hold Nowcast
triage.data_exists: Yes. Odds boards are publicly capturable, game/prop results are public, and state gaming commissions publish operator-level GGR/hold monthly (MA, NJ, CO, etc.); vendors like RG.org already reconcile per-operator handle/GGR. Verified.
triage.lead: Real but narrow. Realized in-quarter hold is finished as games settle, weeks before earnings; state reports lag ~2-3 weeks and don't give a finished quarterly margin-vs-consensus number. DKNG Q2'26 confirmed the market was genuinely surprised (~$80M outcome headwind from Knicks title + World Cup; ~18% EPS miss; stock gapped to $21.40) despite the inputs being public. Sell-side models static hold.
triage.dollar_test: DKNG actually ~$21-22 (idea overstated $40), moves 10-20% = ~$2-4/share on hold/revenue surprise; FLUT ~5-10% = $12-25; deep liquid options on both. Against $0.01 tick + ~1-2c spread the gross move clears costs by ~2 orders of magnitude. Passes decisively.
triage.reason: The one genuine fundamental nowcast in the batch, structurally like credit-card-panel retail alt-data. Mechanism is empirically confirmed (Q2'26 hold-driven miss moved the stock). The real hazard is estimation, not economics: handle distribution per operator is the operator's private data, so realized hold must be MODELED from public lines/results with meaningful error, and monthly state GGR reports partly pre-reveal it (mild Filter-7 crowding — RG.org already sells the raw inputs). But a finished handle-weighted, promo-adjusted realized-hold-vs-consensus simulation is not a sold product, and the dollar move is large with liquid options. Advance to deeper diligence on nowcast accuracy vs the monthly-report baseline and vs how much is already in the price.

triage.name: Prediction-Market Macro-Print Density
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (informational lead) + Filter 5 (price discovery is in the deep venue)
triage.data_exists: Yes. Kalshi CPI/NFP/UR/GDP/claims bracket ladders and order book are public; at-the-money spreads ~1c. But existence is not the problem.
triage.lead: None. SOFR/2y-Treasury/EURUSD are the deepest markets on earth and are where informed macro price discovery occurs first; price-discovery research (and the Fed's 'Kalshi and the Rise of Macro Markets') shows the liquid, high-informed-flow venue leads the thin one. The same nowcast inputs (ADP, card panels, inflation nowcasts) are used by rates desks with far more capital and speed. The tradeable rate already embeds real-time nowcasts, not a 'frozen' survey median (a strawman).
triage.dollar_test: Move size is fine (CPI/NFP surprise moves ZT ~$185-555/contract vs a $3.90 half-tick; EURUSD 30-80 pips). Irrelevant: that is precisely the move the deep market already prices as well or better. A large move you cannot forecast better than the incumbent is not an edge.
triage.reason: Thin, position-capped, retail-heavy Kalshi contracts do not lead the world's deepest rates/FX markets on the same public inputs. No lead means no harvestable edge regardless of the (real) move size.

triage.name: On-Chain Crypto-Catalyst Odds Engine
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (newswire/dockets move the equity simultaneously) + Filter 7 (on-chain/quasi-foreign venue)
triage.data_exists: Yes. Polygon is indexable and Polymarket CLOB fills are public. Wallet-clustering 'accuracy weighting' is unverifiable secret sauce, but data exists.
triage.lead: None. COIN/MSTR are among the fastest news-reactive liquid equities; spot-ETF-approval odds were a PUBLIC narrative set by Bloomberg ETF analysts and by SEC/court dockets, not a private on-chain read. The equity and the on-chain contract react to the same public feed at the same time; the 'equity underreaction' claim is unsupported for a stock this news-sensitive.
triage.dollar_test: COIN moves $10-45/share and miners $1-4 on crypto-reg catalysts — but simultaneously with the docket/wire, not lagging the odds. Move size clears ticks; timing edge does not exist.
triage.reason: Public regulatory catalysts hit COIN via wire/docket at least as fast as they hit the on-chain odds; no lead to trade. Polymarket's on-chain/quasi-offshore status is a secondary strike.

triage.name: Kalshi Weather-Catastrophe Odds Map
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (weather models are public, upstream, and read directly) + Filter 5 (crowded weather-driven NatGas trade)
triage.data_exists: Yes. Kalshi weather ladders exist but are thin; statutory insurer-exposure filings are public.
triage.lead: None, and inverted. GFS/ECMWF model runs and NHC advisories are free, public, 6-hourly, and read DIRECTLY by every energy, insurance, and weather desk (and countless meteorologists on X). Kalshi weather odds are downstream of the same models — they cannot lead the models the whole market already watches.
triage.dollar_test: NG moves $0.10-0.30/MMBtu = $1,000-3,000/contract on a landfall repricing (tick $10), and clears costs — but the move is driven by the public model run, not by a thin Kalshi contract that trails it. No timing edge.
triage.reason: The signal source (public weather models) is upstream of both Kalshi and the commodity desks, and the desks read it directly. Weather-driven NatGas is a crowded specialist arena. No lead.

triage.name: Legislative-Passage Odds Policy Beta
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (policy catalysts are public DC news that moves the ETF on the headline)
triage.data_exists: Yes, odds are public; the 'sharp DC flow filter' and hand-built outcome->ticker map are unverifiable but constructible.
triage.lead: None reliably. Rescheduling/agency/committee actions (DEA/HHS, ITC) hit Politico/wires and move MSOS/TAN instantly; both the thin prediction market and the ETF react to the same public DC news. Any occasional aggregation edge on niche bills is swamped by the fact that the big moves are headline-driven and simultaneous.
triage.dollar_test: TAN ~$35 moves $2-4/share on ITC news; MSOS 20%+ on rescheduling — but on the public headline. Non-headline odds drift is a few cents on a wider-spread thin ETF and does not clear.
triage.reason: Public legislative/regulatory news drives the policy-beta ETFs at least as fast as the odds; no dependable lead, and the large clearing moves are exactly the ones the wire delivers to everyone at once.

triage.name: Shutdown and Debt-Ceiling Odds Kink
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (X-date is public arithmetic; shutdown news is wall-to-wall public)
triage.data_exists: Yes; odds and contractor federal-revenue exposure are obtainable.
triage.lead: None. The bill-curve X-date kink is driven by public Treasury-cash arithmetic (Daily Treasury Statement, CBO/BPC X-date estimates) and traded by the deepest money-market desks; VIX and contractors move on the same saturated public shutdown/default headlines. The idea concedes the real driver is X-date arithmetic — which is public.
triage.dollar_test: VIX futures move 2-5 pts = $2,000-5,000/contract; LDOS $3-8/share — sizes clear ticks, but off public news and public cash arithmetic, not a leading odds read.
triage.reason: Every input is public and the bill kink is priced by deeper desks off Treasury-cash data; the prediction market does not lead. No edge.

triage.name: Betfair Political-Exchange FX Lead
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (political shocks are public wire news) + Filter 7 (foreign-only equities; crowded macro FX)
triage.data_exists: Yes. Betfair Exchange L2 is genuinely the deepest political book and is ingestible.
triage.lead: None consistently. No-confidence votes, leadership resignations, and referendum polls are public wire events; GBP/USD prices them at least as fast (Brexit night: FX desks with constituency-level models LED, the betting market lagged/was wrong). No robust Betfair-leads-cable evidence.
triage.dollar_test: GBP/USD moves 100-300 pips ($1,000-3,000/lot) on a UK political shock — but simultaneously with the wire, not after Betfair. FTSE/LLOY are LSE-listed (foreign-only for a US small trader).
triage.reason: Public political shocks move the deepest FX market at least as fast as the exchange; the deliverable equities are foreign-only and the FX macro trade is crowded. No harvestable lead.

triage.name: Central-Bank Leadership Odds Reaction Function
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (nominee news is high-profile public wire, traded instantly in deep rates)
triage.data_exists: Yes, odds exist; reaction-function scoring is subjective/unverifiable.
triage.lead: None. Fed-chair leaks, shortlist reports (WSJ/Bloomberg), and interviews are marquee public news traded instantly in ZQ/SR3/ZT/DXY — the deepest venues. Kalshi/Polymarket 'next Fed Chair' odds are a downstream mirror of that same wire, not a lead.
triage.dollar_test: A reaction-function repricing moves ZT $370-1,100/contract, DXY 50-150 pips — sizes are fine, but the deep market prices the leak first; the odds trail it.
triage.reason: High-profile nominee news reaches the deepest rates/FX markets at least as fast as the thin odds; subjective scoring adds no timing edge. No lead.

triage.name: Conflict-Odds Commodity Lead
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (oil/gold front-run headlines faster than a thin contract) + Filter 5 (geopolitical risk premium is a paid, crowded trade)
triage.data_exists: Yes; Polymarket conflict contracts and on-chain flow exist, though many are episodic/illiquid.
triage.lead: None, and inverted. Crude and gold are the fastest-reacting geopolitical-risk assets on earth, trading 24h and front-running the first flash headline; a thin Polymarket conflict contract cannot lead CL/GC on OSINT — the commodity gaps before the contract's fills settle.
triage.dollar_test: Escalation moves crude $1-5/bbl = $1,000-5,000/contract, gold $2,000-8,000 — large, but captured by the commodity on the headline, ahead of the odds, not after them.
triage.reason: The commodity complex is the leading indicator here, not the follower; geopolitical risk is exactly what oil/gold desks are paid to price (crowded, documented premium). No lead to trade.

triage.name: Tariff-Action Odds China-ADR Lead
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (tariff posts are the most violent instant-repricing public events)
triage.data_exists: Yes; odds and the tariff->equity/FX map are obtainable. Idea itself concedes 'raw odds alone are already arbitraged.'
triage.lead: None. Tariff impositions/exemptions arrive via Truth Social/USTR and are among the most violent instant repricings in markets; KWEB and USD/CNH gap on the post as fast as or faster than any thin contract. Negotiation-calendar leaks are also public news.
triage.dollar_test: KWEB ~$35 moves $1-3/share and CNH 200-500 pips on tariff news — but simultaneously with the announcement, not lagging the odds. Timing edge absent.
triage.reason: The catalyst is a public headline that moves the deep ADR/FX market at least as fast as the odds; the proposal admits the raw signal is already arbitraged. No lead.

triage.name: Ground-Stop Audio Decoder (LiveATC ASR)
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (Informational Lead); also fails Filter 3 (Dollar Test)
triage.data_exists: YES but degraded: LiveATC.net is real, free, volunteer-run, with 30s+ buffering, dropouts, and coverage gaps. Crucially, the SAME event is on an authoritative real-time public feed.
triage.lead: NONE — in fact negative. The FAA NAS Status API + SWIM feed publish active ground stops, EDCTs and ground-delay programs to the public in real time (nasstatus.faa.gov), and NAS Watch / FlightAware redistribute them instantly. A buffered ASR pipeline over garbled VHF LAGS the FAA's own structured feed rather than leading it.
triage.dollar_test: Claimed DAL 1.5-3% ($0.75/sh) on a hub ground stop is fabricated. Weather ground stops are routine daily noise; DAL does not re-rate intraday on a single-hub GS. Realistic expected move on a detected GS is ~$0.00-0.05, at or below the round-trip spread. The completion-factor cost is disclosed in monthly operational metrics, not repriced off an ATC tally.
triage.reason: The market reads the identical ground-stop/EDCT data from the FAA's real-time public API before the delayed audio decode completes, and single-hub ground stops are routine and do not move the stocks the claimed 1.5-3%. No lead, fabricated move.

triage.name: Earnings-Call Vocal-Stress Drift
triage.data_exists: YES — call audio is public.
triage.lead: The signal is a PUBLISHED academic result (Mayew & Venkatachalam, 'The Power of Voice,' Journal of Finance 2012) and vocal-stress / paralinguistic analytics on earnings calls have been commercialized by multiple vendors for 10+ years. There is no exclusive processing moat and no informational lead.
triage.dollar_test: Nominal magnitude is fine ($3/sh on a $100 name at 3%), but the dollar figure is attached to a 2-5% 'drift' the signal cannot reliably predict: the acoustic-to-return effect is small, disputed, and fragile out of sample. Net of noise and directional/IV risk, realized edge is a fraction of the quoted gross.
triage.reason: This is a documented, published, already-commercialized premium — not exclusive processing — and the underlying acoustic-alpha effect is weak and out-of-sample-fragile, so the harvestable edge does not survive.

triage.name: Brand Ad-Flight ACR Census
triage.data_exists: YES and it is SOLD: iSpot.tv, Nielsen Ad Intel and Vivvix all license national TV + CTV ad-occurrence/spend by advertiser/brand/product (Nielsen added CTV ad-spend in 2025). The idea's own claim that the finished spot-count 'is not licensable off the shelf tied to a ticker' is false.
triage.lead: No exclusive lead — the brand ad-spend census is a mature commercial product any well-resourced fund can buy and map to tickers itself.
triage.dollar_test: DKNG 5% = $2.00/sh would clear a penny spread IF the signal predicted the print, but ad-flight -> quarterly CAC/net-adds is heavily confounded (seasonality, creative efficiency, competitive response, pricing). The move is real; the attribution of a print surprise to spot counts is small and noisy. LLY '3% = $20/sh' likewise assumes a linkage the data doesn't cleanly deliver.
triage.reason: The 'engineering moat' is fiction — the ad-occurrence census is a commoditized, licensable product (iSpot/Nielsen/Vivvix) — and the spend-to-earnings-surprise linkage is too confounded to reliably beat the cost stack.

triage.name: Ship-Channel VHF Voice Tripwire
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 3 (Dollar Test) / Filter 6 (rare-tail, not mean); also Filter 2
triage.data_exists: YES — marine VHF is receivable; closures also appear on USCG MSIBs, VTS traffic, and pilot/agent circulars.
triage.lead: Modest at best. USCG bulletins, pilot associations, shipping-agent circulars and energy wires (Reuters/Platts/Argus) report Gulf channel closures quickly; the exclusive window is thin.
triage.dollar_test: The claimed 3-8 c/gal ($2,100/contract) is a rare Harvey-scale outcome (PADD3 throughput -34%, RB ~$1.67->$2.14), NOT the typical case. Brief fog/allision closures move RB ~0: Exxon and MPC kept producing through multi-day HSC closures on storage. Expected RB move on a randomly-detected closure is near zero, inside a 1-3 tick spread most of the time; the positive tail is dominated by hurricanes the whole market tracks days ahead on public forecasts.
triage.reason: Cross-sectional MEAN move per detected closure is ~zero because refineries run on storage during short closures; the fat right tail is hurricane-scale events that are widely telegraphed in advance, so there is no harvestable, leading dollar edge.

triage.name: Xinwen Lianbo Broadcast Decoder
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (Informational Lead); also Filter 7 (foreign-only legs / vague signal)
triage.data_exists: YES — the 19:00 broadcast is public.
triage.lead: NONE exclusive. Every China macro desk watches Xinwen Lianbo live, and Bloomberg/Reuters wire any genuine policy signal within minutes. 'Segment ordering / air-time' telegraphing is vague and low-information; actual market-moving policy lands in State Council documents and NDRC pressers, not the anchor's reading.
triage.dollar_test: FXI 3% = $0.90/sh would clear a penny spread in isolation, but a clean stimulus/property-easing signal is rare and, when it occurs, is disseminated globally within minutes; the iron-ore (SGX) and copper (LME) legs are foreign venues. Expected edge after 'everyone watches the same broadcast live' is ~0.
triage.reason: A universally-monitored state broadcast wired to English within minutes offers no durable lead, the segment-structure signal is vague, and two of the three instruments are foreign-only.

triage.name: Foreign-Gazette Clearance Scanner
triage.data_exists: YES — SAMR postings, EU Official Journal, and peer gazettes are public.
triage.lead: Minimal and non-durable. Merger-arb is a professionalized, crowded strategy; desks run automated regulatory-page monitors (Visualping, InsideArbitrage, bespoke scrapers) that fire alerts the instant a page changes, staffed by native-language analysts. A small trader will not beat dedicated arb pods to a SAMR/EU posting, and the gross spread already encodes the market's clearance probability.
triage.dollar_test: A 2.5% spread-snap on an $80 target = $2.00/sh clears a penny spread on the deals that DO clear, but you're racing to be first-by-seconds against desks already there, and adverse selection dominates: you get filled on the surprises that break AGAINST you. Net of that selection the edge is not $2.00.
triage.reason: The multilingual-scraping 'moat' is exactly the commoditized, tooled-up capability crowded merger-arb desks already run; there is no durable speed edge for a small trader and the spread already prices the probability.

triage.name: AdCom Webcast Vote Predictor
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 2 (Informational Lead); also Filter 4 (IV cost stack)
triage.data_exists: YES — the AdCom webcast is public.
triage.lead: NONE. The entire biotech trading community watches AdComs live; panel tone is heard by everyone simultaneously and the roll-call vote hits the wire within seconds. A 'diarized sentiment score complete during the webcast' gives no lead over the thousands listening to the same webcast in real time.
triage.dollar_test: Move magnitude is large (10-40% single-name) but that is precisely why front-week straddles imply ~40%+ moves: the binary IV + IV-crush means the gross move must beat an enormous premium, the stock is frequently halted around the event, and directional entries gap through your intended fill. The realized edge net of the option premium is not the quoted 10-40%.
triage.reason: No informational lead (all participants watch the same live webcast and the vote wires in seconds), and the binary-event IV/halt cost stack swallows the large gross move.

triage.name: Hearing-Hostility Valence Index
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 3 (Dollar Test) / Filter 6 (theater, no reliable move); also Filter 2
triage.data_exists: YES — hearings are televised. Note the cited comp, Prattle, was acquired by Liquidnet in 2019 and effectively wound down; congressional/Fed-sentiment-to-alpha did not sustain as a product.
triage.lead: None exclusive — hearings are watched live by everyone; the machine read hears the same words at the same time.
triage.dollar_test: Claimed XBI 2% ($1.80/sh) on a hostile hearing is fabricated. CEO grillings are political theater; sector ETFs rarely move materially on questioning tone and mean-revert intraday. Expected move attributable to a hostility score is ~noise, typically inside the day's normal range, so realized dollars per share are near zero against the spread.
triage.reason: The move is fabricated/unreliable — congressional hostility is theater that rarely produces durable sector re-rating or near-term regulatory action — and the televised hearing offers no lead.

triage.name: Streaming Ad-Fill Instrumentation
triage.fails_which_filter: Filter 1 (Data Reality — unrepresentative sample); also Filter 6
triage.data_exists: PARTIAL/INVALID at scale: you can only observe ads served to YOUR instrumented devices. Ad delivery is personalized and auction-driven, so a small device fleet's fill-rate/ad-load/advertiser-mix is a biased, non-representative sample of platform-wide delivery; you cannot recover platform ad-ARM from it. The 'publisher-side telemetry outsiders can't scrape' framing is backwards — outsiders can't measure it representatively either.
triage.lead: N/A — the measurement itself is statistically invalid at the panel scale a small operator can field.
triage.dollar_test: NFLX 2% = $14/sh clears any spread IF you had the metric, but ad revenue is a small (~single-digit %) and not-separately-disclosed slice of NFLX; the print moves on subs / total revenue / guidance. Even a correct fill-rate read maps weakly to the reported number, and the read isn't correct because the sample is unrepresentative.
triage.reason: A retail-scale instrumented fleet cannot represent personalized, auction-driven platform-wide ad delivery, and streaming ad-ARM is a small, un-cleanly-disclosed line that doesn't drive the print.

triage.name: Foreign-Supplier Call Decoder
triage.data_exists: YES — supplier calls (TSMC, Samsung, SK Hynix, Foxconn, ASML, German/Japanese suppliers) are public; many are held in or simultaneously interpreted into English.
triage.lead: NONE durable. Major Asian/European supplier calls are covered by English newswires within minutes, and read-throughs to AAPL/NVDA/AMD are published same-day by sell-side Asia desks. Supply-chain read-through (Bloomberg SPLC bill-of-materials graphs) is one of the most crowded analyses in semis; the claim that 'the US crowd does not monitor foreign-language supplier calls' is false.
triage.dollar_test: NVDA 4% = $4.80/sh clears a penny spread on a clean read, but a supplier serves many customers, so demand-tone attribution to one US name is confounded and noisy; and the clean reads are already wired same-day and priced into the customer's print. The dollar move exists but the exclusive, correctly-attributed signal does not.
triage.reason: Major foreign supplier calls are wired to English within minutes with published customer read-throughs, the supply-chain trade is crowded and well-staffed, and shared-supplier attribution to a single US customer is too noisy to be a clean lead.

referee.name: Sportsbook Structural-Hold Nowcast
referee.edge_case: The mechanism is real and empirically confirmed, not a statistical artifact: online-gaming revenue = handle x realized win margin, and realized margin swings hard from expected hold when correlated outcomes cash. DraftKings' Q2'26 miss (reported Aug 6-7, 2026) was explicitly hold-driven — management cited ~$80M of favorable-for-customer sports outcomes (Knicks championship in DKNG's largest state, World Cup group-stage results) and sportsbook net-revenue margin compressed to 6.8% from 8.7%. So the underlying fundamental is genuine, the names (DKNG, FLUT, PENN, CZR, BETZ) are liquid with deep listed options, and the per-share dollar moves on earnings are large ($2-4 on a ~$25 DKNG, $5-10 on a ~$96 FLUT) — orders of magnitude above the $0.01 tick and 1-2c spread. If a private, timely, accurate realized-hold read existed, the payoff channel would be clean.
referee.against_case: Four disqualifiers, verified: (1) NO INFORMATIONAL LEAD — realized hold is a PUBLISHED public number, not something you must model. New York posts weekly per-operator handle, GGR AND hold within days (e.g. week ending Aug 2, 2026: DKNG $130.2M handle / 12.4% hold, FDL $136.9M / 13.3%); IL, PA, MI, NJ and most regulated states post monthly per-operator hold ~10-20 days after month-end; free aggregators (RG.org operator stats, LegalSportsReport, SportsHandle, Covers, casinoreports.com's brand/GGR/parlay-handle/hold database) republish and analyze it. By earnings the realized-hold read is fully public for the bulk of national handle. (2) THE MOAT IS REDUNDANT AND INFERIOR — modeling hold from captured lines requires the unobservable per-operator handle distribution (how the money was split), so it carries large error; the state reports give you actual revenue/handle, which is more accurate than any line-based simulation. You'd be rebuilding a noisier version of a free product. (3) THE 'STATIC HOLD ASSUMPTION' PREMISE IS FALSE — the sell-side already models quarterly hold off these monthly/weekly state reports; it is standard industry practice. (4) THE PRICE REACTION IS DOMINATED BY ORTHOGONAL FACTORS — Q2'26 is the killer counterexample: a correctly-forecast hold miss coincided with the stock RISING ~5-8% because prediction-market growth (annualized volume $2.3B->$11B), guidance, promo trends and the Kalshi/CFTC competitive narrative drove the tape. FLUT is down from a $309 52-week high to ~$96 largely on the prediction-market threat, not hold. A right hold nowcast would have put you short into an up move.
referee.who_is_on_other_side: Event-driven and gaming-sector funds, sell-side gaming desks, and options market-makers — all of whom read the same free NY-weekly and state-monthly per-operator GGR-and-hold reports and price the earnings straddle accordingly. They are rational and at least as well informed; there is no informational asymmetry to harvest. Sports-outcome variance is a widely-discussed, well-understood risk factor narrated in real time by financial and industry media as games settle. You are not being paid an un-harvested risk premium; you are competing to quantify a publicly-tracked number with a method that has MORE estimation error than the public source.
referee.dollar_move_vs_costs: Dollar magnitude is NOT the binding constraint — it is a red herring in the pitch. DKNG (~$25.51, not the pitched ~$40) implies ~8-15% earnings moves = ~$2-4/share; FLUT (~$96, not ~$250) ~5-10% = ~$5-10/share. Spread ~1-2c, retail commission ~$0/share, no borrow needed (express short via puts). Gross move dwarfs frictions by 2-3 orders of magnitude. But that is irrelevant because there is no validated directional edge: the hold read is already public and, per Q2'26, the correct hold call mapped to the WRONG price direction. Options are the natural vehicle, but earnings IV already embeds the event (DKNG implied move ~10-14%); a directional straddle/put loses to IV crush unless you are right on the NET surprise including prediction markets, guidance, promo and tax/regulatory — none of which the hold nowcast tells you.
referee.event_frequency: Very low and highly correlated. Material hold swings concentrate in ~1-3 quarters/year (NFL-heavy Q4/Q1, with occasional off-season shocks like Q2'26's NBA/World Cup). Across DKNG/FLUT/PENN/CZR the swings share ONE underlying sports-outcome factor, so operator-quarters are not independent — effectively ~1-2 independent signals/year. Far too few de-overlapped observations to build statistical confidence; any live book would be a couple of concentrated directional bets per year, and Filter-6 (portfolio mean, de-overlap) cannot rescue a t-stat from pooled, correlated rows.
referee.capacity: High in principle and NOT the binding constraint — DKNG (~$25) and FLUT (~$96) are large/mega-cap with deep, liquid listed options; PENN and CZR tradeable; BETZ for sector expression. A small-to-mid trader could size freely. Capacity is ample precisely because the trade is commoditized: the input data set is free and crowded, so there is no scarce edge to be capacity-constrained around.
referee.net_edge_estimate: Negligible to negative after honest adjustment. The realized-hold signal is pre-revealed by free weekly (NY) and monthly (IL/PA/MI/NJ/+) per-operator state reports that the whole sell-side already tracks, so the informational lead is ~zero; the line-capture model is a noisier proxy for data you can read directly; and the actual earnings price reaction is dominated by orthogonal narratives (prediction markets, guidance, promo, tax/regulatory), empirically demonstrated by Q2'26 where a correct hold-miss call coincided with a ~5-8% rally. Expected net-of-cost, net-of-IV expectancy on a directional hold-based options bet is not distinguishable from zero and plausibly negative once IV crush and wrong-direction risk are included. The residual 'handle-weighted, promo-adjusted realized-hold-vs-consensus' aggregation is real work but is public-data aggregation any gaming analyst performs, not a proprietary lead.
referee.confidence: High on the core disqualifiers. Directly verified (Aug 2026): NY publishes weekly per-operator handle/GGR/hold; IL/PA/MI/NJ + most states publish monthly per-operator hold; multiple free aggregators republish it; the sell-side models quarterly hold off these reports; and DKNG's Q2'26 hold-driven miss coincided with a stock RISE on prediction-market growth (the decisive counterexample to the mechanism->price thesis). Prices in the pitch ($40 DKNG, $250 FLUT) are stale versus verified ~$25.51 and ~$96, further undermining the cost argument's framing. Lower-confidence only on the precise net expectancy magnitude, which cannot be pinned without a backtest — but the direction of the conclusion (no exploitable lead) is well supported.
referee.data_pipeline: Odds/line APIs (e.g. The Odds API) and board captures exist and are obtainable, but they are the wrong/redundant pipeline for this thesis: they let you estimate THEORETICAL hold from posted vig and, with heavy modeling and unobservable per-operator handle distribution, a noisy REALIZED-hold proxy. The superior data — actual per-operator realized hold — is published by state regulators: NY weekly (near real-time, within days of week-end), and IL, PA, MI, NJ and most regulated states monthly (~10-20 days after month-end), covering the large majority of national online handle before the quarterly earnings release. Aggregators (RG.org /statistics/operators, LegalSportsReport, SportsHandle, Covers, GamingToday, casinoreports.com with parlay-handle and hold breakdowns) collect and reconcile it for free. Net latency vs the wire: the market and sell-side receive the realized-hold read on the same public cadence you would, so the capture-and-simulate engine confers no timing or accuracy advantage.

survivors.name: Ammonia Synthesis-Loop Thermal Outage Detector
survivors.verdict: NOT CAPITAL. Deserves exactly one cheap, one-afternoon disconfirming probe before final burial — and most likely dies at it. It was killed at triage (Filter 2, informational lead), not resurrected here.
survivors.why: It is the only candidate in the batch where the two expensive-to-fake tests both passed: the physics is real (a synthesis loop tripping is a genuine, orbit-visible thermal event) and the dollar magnitude is material to a concentrated-exposure equity (CF, NTR/UAN nitrogen names). Every other survivor-shaped idea failed on data-that-doesn't-exist or commoditization. Ammonia failed on a single, narrow, cheaply-testable question — does a disclosure lead actually exist — which is the definition of something worth a free probe rather than a guess.
survivors.first_test: Cheapest first, $0, one afternoon, paper only: pull the last ~10-15 unplanned major nitrogen-plant outages (e.g. CF Donaldsonville/Yazoo City, Nutrien Trinidad, Koch, OCI) from ICIS/press/8-Ks. For each, timestamp (a) the first public disclosure vs (b) the first move in CF/NTR/UAN vs (c) when a satellite thermal signal would realistically have been available given revisit/cloud. If the equity has already moved before any public channel carries the outage — as the triage referee expects — the lead does not exist and you close the file. Only if a clean, repeatable multi-hour lead survives on a MAJORITY of events does it graduate to a paper-traded forward test, and only after that to the smallest possible capital.
survivors.expression: tradeable IFF ( thermal_signal_time < first_public_disclosure_time ) AND ( |implied_earnings/guidance_move| > round_trip_cost ) AND single_asset_concentration_high — the middle term already passes; the whole trade lives or dies on the left term, which is the thing to measure.

final.killed_summary: Of 100 candidates bred from documented-winner DNA, roughly 99 died at triage and the ~1 that reached the referee (Sportsbook Structural-Hold Nowcast) was then killed LIKELY-ILLUSORY; the red team had nothing left to attack, and no playbook was produced. Net survivors deserving capital: 0. Working from the visible triage sample, the two dominant killers are Filter 7 (crowded/commoditized, zero-moat public data) and Filter 1 (data reality — the signal physically can't be gotten at the needed cadence/resolution/latency), with Filter 2 (no informational lead) a close third and Filters 4/5/6 (instrument cost stack, already-harvested risk premium, once-a-year/handful-of-events cadence) recurring. Representative Filter-7 deaths: refinery throughput, AIS-dark tanker flow, SAR iron-ore port stockpiles, China NO2 activity, GNSS soil-moisture, DAS rail census, used-vehicle and restaurant-comp nowcasts — all already sold as products by Kpler/Vortexa/Mysteel/YipitData/M Science. Representative Filter-1 deaths: data-center waste-heat and electric-arc-furnace thermal counting (the sub-scene/sub-minute signal simply does not exist from orbit), airline realized yield, P&C reserve triangles, auto-parts demand. The referee kill on Sportsbook is the whole batch in miniature: the realized-hold signal is pre-revealed for free by weekly (NY) and monthly (IL/PA/MI/NJ+) per-operator state reports the entire sell-side already tracks, the dollar magnitude was a red-herring in the pitch, and the pitch even mis-stated the underlying (DKNG ~$25.51, not ~$40). This exactly mirrors the companion 40-candidate swarm in this repo: 38/40 killed at triage, both advancers failed the referee, 0 survivors.
patterns_that_survive: PARKING-LOTS DNA — physical observation of a fundamental driver with a real disclosure LEAD — still the strongest archetype, but ONLY on a thinly-covered small/mid-cap whose value concentrates in a single dominant asset AND where no live public dashboard or alt-data vendor already covers it. Ammonia was the closest instance. The mega-cap versions (refineries, iron-ore ports, China industrial NO2, tanker flows) are all dead on arrival because the data is commoditized (Filter 7). The pattern's binding constraint is always Filter 2 (lead), so future work should PRE-SCREEN for lead first — is the reference number published for free? — before spending a minute on physics or dollars.

BENTER DNA — structural mispricing against a documented recreational/uninformed counterparty — is a sound archetype whose failure mode is now specific and knowable: it dies wherever the outcome variable is disseminated for free (US regulated sportsbooks publish per-operator hold; Reg SHO publishes the threshold list). It is worth hunting only in venues where the structural edge exists AND the answer is NOT published — a narrow and shrinking space, but a real one.

THE NEGATIVE-SCREEN / DO-NOT-OWN PATTERN — the single genuinely validated surviving use across the entire program (from the FTD work, not this batch): a real, persistent, reproducible statistical pattern whose edge lives inside the tick/cost is worthless as a trade but valuable as a FREE risk control, because declining to own something costs no borrow, no spread, no squeeze tail. Any 'edge' this batch might have surfaced should be pressure-tested against this reframe before being called alpha.

THE DISCIPLINE ITSELF — measuring the edge in DOLLARS against the minimum tick and full round-trip cost BEFORE believing any percentage, and de-overlapping windows before believing any t-stat — is the meta-pattern that keeps surviving. It is what turned two celebrated 'monotone economic gradients' into arithmetic. It is cheaper than every other test and should run first, always.
final.verdict: Deploy zero capital on this batch. No candidate earned it. One candidate (Ammonia) earned a single free, one-afternoon disconfirming probe and nothing more — and it will most likely die at that probe. Everything else is dead. This is the honest answer and it is the SAME answer the companion 40-candidate swarm reached: two independent batches, each explicitly bred to imitate documented winners (Benter, parking lots), each terminating at ~0 validated edges. That is not a framework failure — it is the framework doing exactly its job, and the near-zero survival rate is itself the finding. What it means: imitating winners' DNA does not transfer their edge, because their edge WAS being early to exclusive, not-yet-commoditized data and processing. By 2026 the satellite / thermal / nowcast / alt-data frontier is saturated with vendors (Kpler, Vortexa, Orbital Insight, Mysteel, YipitData, M Science, Genscape), so the very informational LEAD that made those winners has been arbitraged away and repackaged as a subscription. That is precisely why the filters that kill hardest are F7 (you are late to a commoditized market), F1 (the data you need cannot physically be gotten), and F2 (the answer is already published for free) — they are detectors for 'this frontier is picked over,' and they are firing on nearly every idea. The value delivered here is negative knowledge, and it is real value: it saves capital and it redraws the map. The productive frontier is not another satellite nowcast. It is (1) genuinely proprietary or early data where you are not competing with a vendor, (2) structural inefficiencies against recreational flow where the outcome is NOT published, and (3) treating small-but-real patterns as free risk controls rather than trades. Fund none of these 100. Keep the framework — it is earning its keep by killing darlings before they cost money.
